title: Vertically Unstable Pelvic Ring Injuries: Impact of Multilevel and Transsacral Fixation Strategy on Failure Rate
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Étude de cohorte en centre de traumatologie de niveau I (*Journal of Orthopaedic Trauma*, juil./déc. 2026, IF 2,3, 67 patients avec lésion pelvienne verticalement instable OTA/AO 61C déplacée ≥ 10 mm) comparant le vissage percutané combinant fixation sacrée multi-étagée et au moins 1 vis trans-sacrée (groupe MAT, n = 38) au vissage mono-étagé ou par vis sacro-iliaques seules (groupe SS, n = 29) : chute spectaculaire du taux d'échec mécanique avec déplacement secondaire ≥ 10 mm (2,6 % dans le groupe MAT contre 48,3 % dans le groupe SS, p < 0,001) et division par 12 du taux de reprise chirurgicale (2,6 % vs 31,0 %, p = 0,002).

[ABSTRACT EN] Objectives To evaluate outcomes of percutaneous pelvic fixation in the treatment of displaced vertically unstable pelvic ring injuries and identify fixation constructs that predict success. Methods Design Retrospective cohort study. Setting Level I trauma center. Patient selection criteria Patients ≥18 years old who underwent operative management of a vertically unstable pelvic ring injury (OTA/AO 61C.1-3) displaced ≥10 millimeters (mm) with sacroiliac (SI) or transsacral (TS) screws over a 24-year period. Exclusion criteria were spinopelvic dissociation, pathologic fracture, treatment with spinopelvic fixation or plate fixation of the posterior pelvic ring, and less than 6-month follow-up. Outcome measures and comparisons The primary outcome was treatment failure, defined as ≥10 mm of radiographic displacement compared with initial postoperative imaging. Secondary outcomes included failure rates stratified by posterior pelvic ring injury type and rates of revision surgery. Outcomes were compared between constructs that included both multilevel sacral fixation and transsacral fixation (MAT) versus constructs that lacked 1 or both of these features; that is, constructs with either single-level fixation or only SI screws (SS). Results The cohort meeting inclusion criteria comprised 67 patients: MAT fixation N = 38 (71% male; median age 37 years, IQR 33-53) and SS fixation N = 29 (62% male; median age 39 years, IQR 34-47). The posterior ring injury patterns included sacral fractures (n = 36, 53.7%), sacroiliac fracture dislocations (n = 17, 25.3%), and sacroiliac dislocations (n = 14, 20.9%). MAT fixation had a significantly lower rate of treatment failure compared with SS fixation (2.6% vs. 48.3%, P Conclusions In this cohort of vertically unstable pelvic ring injuries, fixation at multiple sacral levels with at least 1 TS screw was associated with a significantly lower treatment failure rate (2.6%) compared with single-level fixation or SI screw-only fixation (48.3%). When multilevel transsacral fixation cannot be achieved because of patient anatomy or injury, adjunctive fixation strategies should be considered. Level of evidence Therapeutic Level III. See Instructions for Authors for a complete description of levels of evidence.

title: Concordance of Microbiological and Histopathological Examination of Bone Biopsies in Diagnosing Diabetic Foot Osteomyelitis, a Systematic Review
container-title: Journal of foot and ankle research
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Revue systématique selon PRISMA (*Journal of Foot and Ankle Research*, déc. 2026, IF 2,8, Open-Access) portant sur 5 études et **308 patients** ayant bénéficié d'une biopsie osseuse avec double analyse microbiologique et histopathologique simultanée pour suspicion d'ostéomyélite du pied diabétique (DFO) : le taux moyen de **concordance positive entre culture et histologie n'est que de 43,4 %** (concordance négative de 10,8 %, concordance globale de 41 à 92,5 %) ; la **microbiologie offre une sensibilité supérieure (70 à 83,9 %)** indispensable au ciblage antibiotique, tandis que **l'histopathologie apporte une spécificité supérieure** (excluant les contaminations cutanées) et prédit le risque de reprise chirurgicale et d'antibiothérapie prolongée.

[ABSTRACT EN] Background Diabetic foot osteomyelitis (DFO) is a serious complication of diabetic foot ulcers and is associated with increased risk of amputation, morbidity, and mortality. Bone biopsy remains the most definitive diagnostic modality, yet controversy persists over its diagnostic utility This study reviews the diagnostic concordance of histopathology and microbiology in bone biopsy specimens from patients with DFO and examines the clinical implications of the findings. Methods A systematic review was conducted using PubMed, Medline, CINHAL, Cochrane Library, and Google Scholar. Studies included adult patients with DFO in whom bone biopsy specimens underwent both histopathological and microbiological analysis. Five core studies met the eligibility criteria. Data on study design, setting, population, diagnostic methods, concordance rates, and outcomes were extracted and synthesized utilising a quantitative narrative synthesis. Results Across the five studies (n = 308 patients), histopathology and microbiology showed modest concordance, with mean rates of concordant positive results of 43.4% and common discordant findings. Histopathology demonstrated higher specificity, while microbiology had higher sensitivity, ranging from 70% to 83.9% but greater susceptibility to contamination. Positive histopathology was more strongly associated with the need for revision surgery or extended antibiotic therapy. Discussion Histopathology appears to offer superior diagnostic specificity, whereas microbiology provides valuable information for antimicrobial management. Frequent discordance underscores the importance of interpreting results in a clinical context. Further robust, prospective studies are needed to clarify the optimal diagnostic approach and standardise definitions.

title: Computed tomography-guided percutaneous cryoablation for pediatric osteoid osteoma: clinical success and safety
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Étude rétrospective monocentrique portant sur **18 patients pédiatriques consécutifs** (10 garçons ; âge médian **13,5 ans**, extrêmes 6–17 ans) traités par cryoablation percutanée guidée par scanner pour un ostéome ostéoïde entre décembre 2022 et mai 2025 (*Pediatric Radiology*, nov. 2026, IF 2,1) : le **succès technique et le succès clinique à 1 mois atteignent 100 % (18/18)**, avec un **délai médian de disparition complète des douleurs de 1 jour (IQR 1–2 jours)** — **72 % des enfants (13/18) étant totalement indolores dès 24 heures**, 100 % à 14 jours avec arrêt complet des antalgiques à 1 mois — sans **aucune complication (0 % d'événement indésirable SIR)** et avec une exposition radique faible (**DLP médian de 158 mGy·cm**, IQR 100–300).

[ABSTRACT EN] Percutaneous thermal ablation has replaced surgery as first-line treatment for osteoid osteoma in many centers. Radiofrequency ablation is the most widely reported technique, whereas cryoablation is an alternative thermal ablation technique. Pediatric data on cryoablation for osteoid osteoma remain limited. To evaluate the clinical and technical success of CT-guided percutaneous cryoablation for osteoid osteoma in children and adolescents. Safety and radiation exposure were assessed as secondary procedural outcomes. This retrospective single-center study included 18 consecutive patients (10 males; median age 13.5 years, range 6-17) who underwent CT-guided cryoablation between December 2022 and May 2025. Clinical success at 1 month and technical success were the main outcomes. Society of Interventional Radiology (SIR)-classified adverse events, pain evolution, analgesic use, procedure duration, and dose-length product were recorded as secondary outcomes. Pain was assessed using the numeric rating scale (NRS). Technical success was achieved in all procedures (18/18). Clinical success was achieved in all patients by the 1-month clinical follow-up. Median time to complete pain relief was 1 day (interquartile range, 1-2 days); 13/18 patients were pain-free within 24 h, all patients were pain-free within 14 days, and all had discontinued analgesics at 1 month. No SIR-classified procedure-related adverse event was observed in this cohort. Median dose-length product was 158 mGy·cm (interquartile range, 100-300). CT-guided cryoablation achieved technical success and complete clinical success at 1 month in this pediatric osteoid osteoma cohort, with rapid pain relief, discontinuation of analgesics, and no SIR-classified procedure-related adverse event observed.

title: Stress Fracture Following Radiofrequency Ablation of a Femoral Osteoid Osteoma: A Case Report
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Observation clinique (*JBJS Case Connector*, oct. 2026, IF 0,8, Open-Access PMC13787528) rapportant une **fracture de contrainte atraumatique du fémur distal** survenue **6 semaines après l'ablation par radiofréquence (RF) guidée par scanner** d'un **ostéome ostéoïde cortical fémoral distal** chez une adolescente de 16 ans, réalisée via un **trocart d'accès osseux de gros calibre (10G)** : la mise en **décharge stricte pendant 6 semaines**, l'arrêt des AINS et la supplémentation en vitamine D ont permis une **consolidation radiographique complète et une guérison clinique totale à 12 mois** sans ostéosynthèse chirurgicale.

[ABSTRACT EN] A 16-year-old girl presented with a distal femoral osteoid osteoma treated with CT-guided radiofrequency ablation (RFA) using a 10-gauge needle. She developed an atraumatic stress fracture at the instrumentation site 6 weeks postoperatively, which was managed with 6 weeks of non-weight bearing, NSAID discontinuation, and vitamin-D supplementation, with symptom improvement. She progressed to full-weight bearing and, at 12-month follow-up (from the date of ablation), demonstrated complete radiographic union and symptom resolution. This case highlights a rare atraumatic complication of RFA, suggesting a low threshold for early imaging in patients with persistent postoperative pain.

title: Determinants of fluoroscopy frequency and effect of standardized workflow optimization in robot-assisted pelvic channel screw placement: a single-center retrospective cohort study
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Vaste cohorte rétrospective monocentrique (*Journal of Robotic Surgery*, nov. 2026, IF 2,2, 601 patients : 312 avant et 289 après optimisation) identifiant les 4 facteurs indépendants augmentant le recours à la scopie lors du vissage pelvien percutané (surface osseuse oblique au point d'entrée cortical IRR = 1,52, courbe d'apprentissage des 10 premiers cas IRR = 1,48, vissage du couloir S2 IRR = 1,26 et obésité IMC ≥ 30 IRR = 1,19) et démontrant qu'un protocole standardisé réduit de 27 % le nombre de clichés et le temps de scopie (16,2 s vs 21,8 s, p < 0,001) avec 98,7 % de précision intra-osseuse.

[ABSTRACT EN] Robot-assisted percutaneous pelvic channel screw placement has been shown to significantly reduce intraoperative radiation exposure. However, even within the robot-assisted framework, fluoroscopy frequency still shows substantial within-group variation. Existing studies lack a systematic analysis of the determinants of fluoroscopy frequency and lack targeted workflow optimization strategies. To identify the independent determinants of fluoroscopy frequency in robot-assisted pelvic channel screw placement and to evaluate whether a standardized optimization protocol based on these factors can further reduce residual fluoroscopy exposure. We retrospectively enrolled patients with pelvic fractures who underwent robot-assisted percutaneous pelvic channel screw placement at Gansu Provincial Hospital between January 2020 and May 2025. Part A: The number of fluoroscopy sessions per case was the dependent variable. Multivariable negative binomial regression was used to analyze potential determinants, including surgeon experience stage, screw type, oblique bone surface at the entry point, BMI, and bone mineral density. Part B: Based on Part A results, we developed and implemented a standardized optimization protocol targeting modifiable factors, with December 2023 as the cutoff. We compared fluoroscopy frequency, fluoroscopy time, and screw accuracy between the pre-optimization group (n = 312) and the post-optimization group (n = 289). To address methodological time-trend confounding, we added interrupted time series analysis, propensity score matching, and a negative control subgroup analysis. This was a non-randomized, single-center, before-after design, and residual confounding cannot be completely excluded. Part A (n = 601): Multivariable negative binomial regression showed that oblique bone surface at the entry point (IRR = 1.52, 95% CI: 1.31-1.77, P 30 cases, IRR = 1.48, 95% CI: 1.25-1.75, P < 0.001), S2 screws (IRR = 1.26, 95% CI: 1.10-1.44, P = 0.001), and BMI ≥ 30 kg/m² (IRR = 1.19, 95% CI: 1.02-1.39, P = 0.026) were independent determinants of fluoroscopy frequency. Part B: The post-optimization group showed a significant reduction in fluoroscopy frequency compared with the pre-optimization group (9.8 ± 2.9 vs. 13.5 ± 3.7, P < 0.001). Fluoroscopy time also decreased (16.2 ± 5.4 s vs. 21.8 ± 6.9 s, P < 0.001). Screw accuracy showed no significant difference (98.7% vs. 98.1%, P = 0.52). The optimization effect was most pronounced in the oblique bone surface subgroup (31.5% reduction) and was 14.2% in the non-oblique subgroup. In the negative control subgroup (experienced surgeons, non-oblique, non-obese, S1 screws), fluoroscopy frequency did not change significantly before and after optimization (10.2 ± 2.6 vs. 10.5 ± 2.8, P = 0.41); however, post-hoc power for this subgroup was extremely low (approximately 0.10), so this null result should be regarded as inconclusive rather than as evidence of no effect. These findings suggest a possible risk-stratified specific effect of the optimization protocol, but time trends, the Hawthorne effect, and the unseparated multicomponent bundle cannot be excluded. In robot-assisted pelvic channel screw placement, oblique bone surface at the entry point, early surgeon experience stage, S2 screws, and obesity are independent determinants of fluoroscopy frequency. A standardized multicomponent optimization protocol targeting modifiable factors can safely reduce fluoroscopy frequency by approximately 27% without compromising screw accuracy. Optimization of fluoroscopy frequency should become a core indicator in robot-assisted surgical training and quality control. However, this was a non-randomized, single-center, before-after study; the optimization protocol was a multicomponent bundle whose individual contributions cannot be separated; and the oblique bone surface and negative control subgroups were underpowered. These findings require prospective validation.

title: Intraoperative visualization with 3D fluoroscopy for posterior pelvic fixation is associated with lower cumulative imaging-related radiation exposure
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Étude comparative sur 245 patients (*Injury*, nov. 2026, IF 2,2) opérés d'un vissage percutané de l'anneau pelvien postérieur entre 2014 et 2023 sous fluoroscopie 3D per-opératoire (3DF, n = 89) versus fluoroscopie 2D conventionnelle + scanner post-opératoire (2DF, n = 156) : réduction par 3 de la dose d'irradiation cumulée totale (179,2 mGy vs 526,1 mGy, p < 0,001), réduction par 4 de la dose per-opératoire seule (médiane 79,1 mGy vs 318,0 mGy, p < 0,001) et baisse significative du taux de réintervention chirurgicale à moyen terme (9,5 % vs 31,2 %, p = 0,012).

[ABSTRACT EN] Introduction Achieving optimal screw positioning in posterior pelvic ring (PR) fracture fixation is critical for fracture stability and safety. Formerly, our institution used intraoperative plain-film fluoroscopy followed by postoperative computed tomography (CT) to assess fracture reduction and screw placement. Introduction of the 3D mobile C-arm enables immediate volumetric intraoperative assessment, may improve intraoperative visualization, and may alter conventional imaging requirements. This study compared cumulative imaging-related radiation exposure between cases performed with intraoperative 3D fluoroscopy (3DF) against standard intraoperative plain-film fluoroscopy (2DF), including postoperative CT utilization. Methods A retrospective review was conducted on patients treated for posterior PR fractures at a level 1 trauma center between 2014 and 2023. Utilization of 3DF or plain-film fluoroscopy, and any intraoperative screw changes were documented. Rates and details of postoperative complications and subsequent reoperations were recorded for patients with > 3 months follow-up. Radiation doses for 3DF, 2DF, and postoperative CT were extracted from radiology reports. Results Among 245 patients (mean age 47.2, 52.2% male) undergoing fixation for posterior PR fractures, 89 (36.3%) had 3DF intraoperatively, while 156 (63.7%) had 2DF. 27 patients (8 3DF, 19 2DF, p = 0.443) had screws changed intraoperatively, primarily to modify screw path (n = 16, 59.3%), to achieve better purchase/reduction (n = 5, 18.5%), to modify screw size (n = 3, 11.1%), to change screw type (n = 2, 7.4%), and failure to advance screw (n = 1, 3.7%). Mean radiation dose for the 3DF group was significantly lower (179.2 mGy vs 526.1 mGy, p 3 months follow-up, reoperation was less frequent with 3DF (9.5% vs 31.2%, p = 0.012), predominantly for symptomatic implant removal. Discussion and conclusion Intraoperative 3DF was associated with lower cumulative radiation exposure compared to traditional fluoroscopy with routine postoperative CT, and intraoperative dose alone was also lower. Reoperation was less frequent in the 3DF group, but most reoperations were implant removals for symptomatic or planned indications. These findings highlight the potential of 3DF as a practical radiation efficient quality assurance tool in posterior pelvic fixation.

title: Technical Tricks to Improve Iliosacral Screw Safety Using Three-dimensional Computed Tomography Imaging
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Note technique de référence (*Journal of Orthopaedic Trauma*, nov. 2026, IF 2,3) décrivant l'utilisation de reconstructions TDM 3D volumétriques pré-opératoires orientées dans les plans exacts d'Inlet (superposition de la corticale antérieure du corps de S1) et d'Outlet (tunnel foraminal S1 vu de face) pour guider le vissage ilio-sacré percutané : permet d'identifier avec certitude quelle ligne dense corticale correspond à la limite antérieure réelle de S1 en se calant sur la morphologie de l'anneau pelvien antérieur et l'obliquité des trous obturateurs, sécurisant le geste face aux variations anatomiques fréquentes (sacrum dysmorphique, récessus corticaux alaires profonds, ostéophytes marginaux ou pente sacrée extrême).

[ABSTRACT EN] Summary This technical note describes a method used to facilitate iliosacral screw fixation with three-dimensional (3D) computed tomography (CT) imaging. Preoperative pelvis CT scans were used to generate 3D reconstructions, which were then manipulated into inlet and outlet orientations. The inlet position for S1 was achieved when the anterior cortex of the S1 body became superimposed on itself; the outlet position was when the S1 nerve root tunnel was viewed en face. On the fluoroscopic inlet view of S1, multiple cortical densities were often visible and could be difficult to distinguish as S1 versus other sacral segments. 3D CT helped distinguish the position and shape of the anterior cortical limit of S1 by referencing preoperative 3D CT inlet images that were reproduced intraoperatively on fluoroscopy using the appearance of the anterior pelvic ring and the relative obliquity of the obturator foramen. This technique was especially valuable in the setting of common posterior pelvic anatomic variations-including asymmetry, degenerative osteophytes, severe sacral slope, and dramatic cortical recesses of the upper sacral segment. These variations were often difficult to anticipate with conventional plain film or standard CT imaging alone, underscoring the potential clinical utility of this technique.

title: Intervertebral Disc Abnormalities on MRI in Thoracolumbar High-Energy and Fragility Fractures Treated With the SpineJack®-System: A Secondary Analysis of a Single-Centre Cohort
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Analyse rétrospective de 204 fractures vertébrales thoraco-lombaires (176 patients, 119 fractures ostéoporotiques OVF d'âge moyen 72,5 ans et 85 fractures traumatiques à haute énergie VCF d'âge moyen 50,0 ans) traitées par implants d'expansion titane **SpineJack®** (*Global Spine Journal*, nov. 2026, IF 2,6, Open-Access) avec IRM pré-opératoire : prévalence élevée des lésions discales adjacentes (disque supérieur 68,1 %, disque inférieur 58,3 %, combinées 53,9 % selon la classification de Sander), la sévérité de l'atteinte discale n'étant pas prédite par la seule classification osseuse AOSpine/OF et n'empêchant pas la restauration anatomique par SpineJack.

[ABSTRACT EN] Study DesignRetrospective secondary analysis.ObjectivesTo describe the frequency of concomitant disc abnormality on preoperative MRI in SpineJack®-treated thoracolumbar fractures and its association with fracture type and clinical parameters.MethodsFrom our published SpineJack® cohort (310 fractures, 2014-2022), 204 fractures in 176 patients with preoperative MRI were analyzed. Discs were graded (Sander et al.) by two readers independently, then by consensus; fractures by AOSpine or OF type. Analyses used exact tests, Spearman correlation and Firth logistic regression; the OVF-versus-VCF comparison was adjusted for age and sex. Other analyses were exploratory.Results119 fractures (58.3%) were OVFs (mean age 72.5 years) and 85 were VCFs (50.0 years). Superior, inferior and combined disc abnormality occurred in 68.1%, 58.3% and 53.9%. Superior abnormality was more frequent in OVFs than VCFs (73.9% vs 60.0%; crude OR 1.89, 95% CI 1.04-3.44), but not after adjustment (OR 1.29, 0.57-2.91). AOSpine type correlated with inferior disc grade in VCFs (ρ=0.247, p=0.023); OF type did not correlate with disc grade. Exploratory: higher inferior disc grade was associated with neurological deficit (7 events; OR per grade 1.93, 1.01-4.18) and less cement leakage (OR 0.59, 0.36-0.90).ConclusionsDisc abnormality is frequent in SpineJack®-treated thoracolumbar fractures. The higher frequency in OVFs is largely explained by age. Associations with neurological deficit and cement leakage are exploratory. Fracture classification alone does not predict disc abnormality severity.

title: Risk Factors for Bone Cement Leakage and Re-fracture Following PKP in Patients With Thoracolumbar Spine Fractures
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Étude rétrospective sur **115 patients** traités par cyphoplastie percutanée par ballonnet (PKP) pour fracture par tassement vertébral thoraco-lombaire (*Annali Italiani di Chirurgia*, nov. 2026, IF 1,5), analysant les déterminants multivariés des **fuites de ciment PMMA (18 cas, 15,7 %)** et des **refractures vertébrales post-opératoires (29 cas, 25,2 %)** : l'**interruption corticale des parois vertébrales** et l'**âge avancé** sont les deux facteurs de risque indépendants de fuite de ciment ($p < 0,05$), tandis que l'**âge**, la **sévérité du tassement initial** et la **rupture corticale** prédisent indépendamment le risque de nouvelle fracture vertébrale ($p < 0,05$), alors même que la PKP améliore hautement l'EVA, l'ODI, l'angle de Cobb et la hauteur vertébrale antérieure ($p < 0,001$).

[ABSTRACT EN] Aim Thoracolumbar spine fractures are commonly treated with percutaneous kyphoplasty (PKP), but bone cement leakage and re-fracture remain major concerns. Identifying their risk factors is essential for improving prognosis but remains insufficiently characterized. This study was designed to explore the risk factors for bone cement leakage and re-fracture following PKP in patients with thoracolumbar spine fractures. Methods A retrospective analysis was conducted on 115 patients with thoracolumbar spine fractures who underwent PKP at Heilongjiang Provincial Hospital between April 2022 and February 2025 (leakage group: 18 patients with bone cement leakage; non-leakage group: 97 patients without leakage). Risk factors for bone cement leakage were analyzed. Patients were divided into re-fracture (29 cases with re-fractures) and non-re-fracture (86 cases without re-fractures) groups to identify risk factors for postoperative re-fracture. Results Logistic multivariate regression analysis identified age and vertebral wall destruction as independent risk factors for postoperative bone cement leakage ( p p Conclusions Age and vertebral wall destruction are independent predictors of cement leakage, and together with compression severity, also predict re-fracture. These findings support routine preoperative assessment of vertebral wall integrity using high-resolution computed tomography (CT), particularly in elderly patients, as vertebral wall destruction was independently associated with bone cement leakage.

title: Development of a Multimodal Model Combining Imaging and Clinical Data to Predict Bone Cement Leakage During Vertebroplasty for Fresh Thoracolumbar Compression Fractures
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Étude multicentrique avec validation externe et prospective portant sur **486 vertèbres fraîches traitées par vertébroplastie percutanée (PVP) chez 378 patients** (*JOR Spine*, nov./déc. 2026, IF 3,4, Open-Access) : l'analyse d'interprétabilité SHAP et la régression multivariée démontrent que la **destruction corticale**, l'**atteinte du mur postérieur**, le **volume de ciment injecté** et l'**IMC** sont les prédicteurs indépendants majeurs de fuite de ciment, le modèle multimodal combinant clinique, séméiologie TDM et radiomique atteignant une **AUC de 0,902–0,939 en test interne, 0,722–0,929 en validation externe et 0,834–0,925 en validation prospective**.

[ABSTRACT EN] Background Bone cement leakage is a common complication of percutaneous vertebroplasty (PVP), but perioperative risk stratification remains challenging. Existing models based on single-source clinical or imaging features have limited performance. This study aimed to develop and validate multimodal artificial intelligence (AI) models integrating clinical, imaging, and radiomics features to predict bone cement leakage during PVP. Methods This multicenter study included 486 treated vertebrae from 378 patients at the North, South, and Shenshan campuses of our hospital. The treated vertebra was the prediction unit, while all vertebrae from the same patient were retained in the same dataset partition and cross-validation fold. Clinical variables, conventional CT imaging features, and CT-based radiomics features were extracted. Logistic regression identified independent risk factors. Six machine-learning algorithms were used to construct clinical, imaging, radiomics, and multimodal models. Performance was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), accuracy, F1 score, and decision curve analysis. Independent external and prospective validations were performed, and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) were used for model interpretation. Results Among the 486 treated vertebrae, 215 (44.2%) had cement leakage. Higher body mass index (BMI), greater cement injection volume, cortical destruction, and posterior wall involvement were independently associated with leakage. Multimodal models generally achieved higher AUCs than the corresponding single-modality models, with AUCs of 0.902-0.939 in the internal test cohort, 0.722-0.929 in the external validation cohort, and 0.834-0.925 in the prospective validation cohort. Patient-level aggregation and one-vertebra-per-patient sensitivity analyses yielded broadly comparable discrimination. SHAP identified cortical destruction, cement injection volume, and posterior wall involvement as the most influential predictors. Conclusions The multimodal models demonstrated good and generally consistent discrimination across the internal test, external validation, and prospective validation cohorts and may support perioperative risk assessment and individualized cement injection planning during PVP.

title: Percutaneous screw distraction versus open fusion surgery for anatomic restoration after burst fracture
container-title: Journal of clinical neuroscience : official journal of the Neurosurgical Society of Australasia
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Étude de cohorte rétrospective en centre de traumatologie de niveau I comparant **24 patients traités par ostéosynthèse transpédiculaire percutanée à angle fixe avec distraction** à **39 patients opérés par arthrodèse postérieure ouverte** pour une fracture corporéale comminutive thoraco-lombaire (**burst fracture AO Spine A2, A3 et A4**) sans laminectomie directe entre 2018 et 2024 (*Journal of Clinical Neuroscience*, nov. 2026, IF 1,9) : à répartition fracturaire identique ($p = 0,25$), l'approche **percutanée réduit significativement les pertes sanguines per-opératoires ($p < 0,001$)**, procure un **gain supérieur de surface canalaire rachidienne par décompression indirecte (ligamentotaxis) entre le scanner pré- et post-opératoire ($p = 0,01$)** et maintient un **meilleur indice de hauteur corporéale vertébrale au dernier suivi ($p = 0,02$)**.

[ABSTRACT EN] Open posterior transpedicular screw fixation for thoracolumbar burst fractures involves substantial muscle dissection, resulting in iatrogenic trauma, prolonged hospital stays, and extended recovery times, but minimally invasive techniques like percutaneous pedicle screw fixation cannot be used in all fracture patterns or indications. We compared perioperative and radiographic outcomes of a fixed-angle percutaneous instrumentation technique versus conventional open fixation in patients managed without direct decompression. In this retrospective cohort study at our Level I trauma center, patients who underwent either open or percutaneous instrumentation without laminectomy in 2018-2024 were identified. Patients with AO Spine fracture classifications of A2, A3, and A4 were present in the cohort. Student's t-test and Pearson's Chi-square statistical tests were used to compare the perioperative and radiographic outcomes of patients who underwent fixed-angle percutaneous instrumentation with those who underwent conventional open fixation without direct decompression. Among 63 included patients, 24 underwent percutaneous surgery and 39 had open procedures. Selection varied by on-call surgeon, not fracture characteristics. AO Spine fracture classifications (A2, A3, A4) were similarly distributed between groups (p = 0.25). Baseline characteristics were similar between groups. The percutaneous group experienced significantly less intraoperative blood loss (p < 0.001), showed greater improvement in canal cross-sectional area from preoperative to postoperative (p = 0.01), and had greater improvement in vertebral body index scores from postdistraction to last follow-up (p = 0.02). The groups were statistically similar in all other radiographic outcomes. Elective instrumentation removal was more frequent in patients in the percutaneous cohort (p = 0.001). Percutaneous instrumentation for thoracolumbar burst fractures not involving decompression achieved radiographic outcomes comparable with open techniques in this study. The percutaneous technique demonstrated favorable radiographic outcomes, with greater indirect canal decompression intraoperatively and better vertebral body index scores at last follow-up. These findings are hypothesis-generating and warrant prospective comparison.

title: Clinical and radiographic outcomes of SpineJack mechanical kyphoplasty versus conservative management in traumatic thoraco-lumbar compression fractures
container-title: The surgeon : journal of the Royal Colleges of Surgeons of Edinburgh and Ireland
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Étude de cohorte prospective comparative portant sur **246 patients consécutifs neurologiquement intacts** atteints d'une fracture-tassement traumatique thoraco-lombaire (**Magerl / AO Spine type A**) entre janvier 2018 et décembre 2023 (**122 patients traités par kyphoplastie mécanique percutanée SpineJack** [Groupe B, 100 évalués à 12 mois] vs **124 traités orthopédiquement par repos au lit et corset 3 points** [Groupe A, 104 évalués à 12 mois]) (*The Surgeon*, nov. 2026, IF 2,3) : la **kyphoplastie mécanique SpineJack** démontre une **supériorité statistiquement significative à 1, 6 et 12 mois sur le soulagement douloureux (EVA/VAS)**, la **récupération fonctionnelle (indice d'Oswestry ODI)**, la **restauration du taux de perte de hauteur vertébrale (HLR)** et la **correction de l'angle de cyphose régionale (RKA)**.

[ABSTRACT EN] Prospective, comparative, observational cohort study. To compare the clinical and radiographic outcomes of SpineJack mechanical kyphoplasty versus conservative management in neurologically intact patients with traumatic thoraco-lumbar compression fractures (AO type A). Thoraco-lumbar compression fractures can be managed conservatively, with prolonged bed rest and rigid orthoses; with minimally invasive techniques originally developed for osteoporotic fractures, such as vertebroplasty and kyphoplasty; or with open or percutaneous pedicle screw fixation. A total of 246 consecutive patients with a Magerl type A thoraco-lumbar fracture were included in this non-randomized prospective study between January 2018 and December 2023. After counseling, 124 patients elected Group A (conservative management: bed rest and a three-point brace) and 122 elected Group B (percutaneous kyphoplasty with SpineJack). At the final 12-month follow-up, 104 patients in Group A and 100 patients in Group B were evaluated, with a total of 42 patients lost to follow-up. The Visual Analogue Scale (VAS) and Oswestry Disability Index (ODI) were used to assess clinical outcome. Radiographic outcome was assessed by measuring the vertebral height loss rate (HLR) and regional kyphosis angle (RKA). Patients were followed up at 1, 6, and 12 months. Pain relief and recovery of functional ability were significantly better in Group B. Radiographic metrics showed a better outcome in the surgical group. Mechanical kyphoplasty with the SpineJack system is a safe and effective treatment for post-traumatic compression fractures, providing a significant improvement in pain, disability, and radiographic morphometric parameters that is maintained at long-term follow-up.

title: Percutaneous Vertebroplasty versus Non-Surgical Controls for Osteoporotic Vertebral Compression Fractures: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Pain, Fracture, and Safety Outcomes
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Revue systématique et méta-analyse PRISMA 2020 regroupant **20 essais contrôlés randomisés (ECR) et 2 238 patients** comparant la **vertébroplastie percutanée** aux traitements non chirurgicaux dans les fractures vertébrales ostéoporotiques par compression jusqu'en avril 2026 (*Therapeutics and Clinical Risk Management*, nov. 2026, IF 2,3, Open-Access PMC13769260) : la vertébroplastie procure une **réduction douloureuse statistiquement supérieure au traitement conservateur dès 1 semaine ($\text{SMD} = -1,22$, IC 95 % $-1,93$ à $-0,50$)** et maintenue à **1 mois ($\text{SMD} = -1,17$)**, **3 mois ($\text{SMD} = -0,84$)**, **6 mois ($\text{SMD} = -0,86$)** et **12 mois ($\text{SMD} = -0,69$, IC 95 % $-1,06$ à $-0,32$)**, **sans aucune augmentation du risque de nouvelle fracture vertébrale ($\text{RR} = 1,04$, IC 95 % 0,81–1,34)** et avec une **tendance à la réduction des événements indésirables graves ($\text{RR} = 0,58$, IC 95 % 0,33–1,00)** liés au décubitus.

[ABSTRACT EN] Background Percutaneous vertebroplasty has been proposed as minimally invasive treatment to stabilize fractured vertebral body and provide faster pain relief, but its comparative benefit over conservative treatment remains debated. This review compared percutaneous vertebroplasty with non-surgical controls for pain relief and safety outcomes in osteoporotic vertebral compression fractures. Methods This review was conducted accordance with PRISMA 2020. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were searched from inception to April 2026. Pain scores were pooled as standardized mean differences (SMDs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs), while fracture outcomes and serious adverse events were pooled as risk ratios (RRs). Random-effects models were used and heterogeneity was assessed using Cochran's Q, I 2 , and tau-squared. Results A total of 20 randomized controlled trials comprising 2238 participants were included in this review. Vertebroplasty was associated with significantly greater pain reduction than non-surgical controls at 1 week (SMD=-1.22; 95% CI: -1.93 to -0.50), 1 month (SMD=-1.17; 95% CI: -1.77 to -0.56), 3 months (SMD=-0.84; 95% CI: -1.30 to -0.38), 6 months (SMD=-0.86; 95% CI: -1.26 to -0.46), and 12 months (SMD=-0.69; 95% CI: -1.06 to -0.32). 3-week pain outcome was not statistically significant (SMD = -0.49; 95% CI: -1.24 to 0.26). No significant difference was observed for fracture risk (RR=1.04; 95% CI: 0.81 to 1.34) or serious adverse events (RR=0.58; 95% CI: 0.33 to 1.00). Conclusion Percutaneous vertebroplasty was associated with greater pain relief than non-surgical controls treatment at all follow-up periods except 3 weeks among patients with osteoporotic vertebral compression fractures, with the strongest apparent benefit in early post-treatment period.

title: Early Balloon Kyphoplasty Across Different Age Groups in Elderly Patients With Vertebral Compression Fractures: A Retrospective Study From a Tertiary Center
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Étude rétrospective monocentrique en centre tertiaire comparant les résultats de la **cyphoplastie par ballonnet précoce (réalisée $\le 7\text{ jours}$ après le diagnostic radiologique)** d'une **fracture par compression vertébrale ostéoporotique aiguë** chez **98 patients âgés** répartis en deux cohortes d'âge : **$< 80\text{ ans}$ (Groupe A, $n = 53$)** versus **$\ge 80\text{ ans}$ (Groupe B, $n = 45$)** (*International Journal of Spine Surgery*, nov. 2026, IF 1,7) : les **deux groupes présentent une amélioration hautement significative et équivalente du score douloureux EVA et de la restauration de hauteur corporéale (index de Beck, $p < 0,0001$)**, avec des **taux de fuite de ciment, de re-fracture et de fracture du niveau adjacent strictement comparables entre octogénaires ($\ge 80\text{ ans}$) et patients $< 80\text{ ans}$**.

[ABSTRACT EN] Background Vertebral compression fractures (VCFs) are common, particularly in elderly patients. VCFs are often associated with significant pain, functional impairment, and spinal deformity. The aim of this study was to compare the outcomes of early balloon kyphoplasty across age groups. Methods This retrospective study analyzed patients treated with early balloon kyphoplasty for VCFs at a tertiary hospital from 2015 to 2024. Early balloon kyphoplasty was defined as surgical treatment performed within 7 days of radiological diagnosis of an acute osteoporotic VCF. Patients were divided into 2 age groups: those younger than 80 years (group A) and those 80 years or older (group B). Data collected included time to diagnosis, time to surgery, total hospital stay, American Society of Anesthesiologists score, complication rates, and visual analog scale score. Radiological outcomes were assessed using the Beck Index. Rates of cement leakage, re-fracture, and adjacent fracture were also evaluated. Results Ninety-eight patients were included (53 in group A; 45 in group B). Both groups showed significant improvement in visual analog scale scores and Beck Index following kyphoplasty ( P Conclusions In this retrospective cohort, early balloon kyphoplasty was associated with significant improvements in pain and vertebral body restoration in elderly patients with osteoporotic VCFs, with similar short-term trajectories in patients aged Clinical relevance Comparable short-term clinical and radiographic outcomes were observed between patients Level of evidence: 3

title: Image-guided ablation treatment of Desmoid tumors: an approach for management and integration into the national comprehensive cancer network ® guidelines
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Mise au point de référence (*Skeletal Radiology*, nov. 2026, IF 1,9) consacrée à l'intégration officielle de l'ablation percutanée guidée par l'image — et tout particulièrement de la **cryoablation percutanée** — dans l'arbre décisionnel du National Comprehensive Cancer Network (NCCN) pour les tumeurs desmoïdes (fibromatoses agressives) : détaille les critères de passage de la surveillance active au traitement ablatif local, les avantages biophysiques de la cryoablation (contrôle visuel de l'iceball, préservation de la matrice collagénique, régression volumétrique prolongée et sédation douloureuse rapide) face aux traitements systémiques et à la chirurgie.

[ABSTRACT EN] Desmoid tumors are proliferative mesenchymal tumors arising from musculoaponeurotic structures. Although lacking the ability to metastasize, these neoplasms have a propensity to locally invade and recur, resulting in significant morbidity and reduced quality of life. This variable natural history and unpredictable biologic behavior can complicate clinical management. Active surveillance may be appropriate as initial management, with systemic, surgical and other local treatment options considered depending on the extent of disease progression, in accordance with the current National Comprehensive Cancer Network guidelines. Notably, image-guided percutaneous cryoablation has emerged as an effective treatment option for rapid local control and sustained lesion regression. The efficacy of cryoablation in the management of these tumors is now supported by an increasing body of literature. This article will review the pathophysiology and natural history of desmoid tumors, together with treatment indications and national cancer guidelines. Image-guided ablation techniques will be described as well as how these options can fit into clinical paradigms and management pathways.

title: EFFICACY AND SAFETY OF PERCUTANEOUS CRYOABLATION FOR DESMOID TUMORS: PROTOCOL FOR A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW AND META-ANALYSIS
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Protocole méthodologique de revue systématique et méta-analyse de niveau de preuve II (*Acta Ortopédica Brasileira*, nov. 2026, IF 0,8, Open-Access PMC13773520) dédié à l'évaluation quantitative de la **cryoablation percutanée chez l'adulte atteint de tumeur desmoïde** à travers les bases CENTRAL, Embase, PubMed et Scopus (évaluation du risque de biais par RoB-2 et ROBINS-I) : définit le **contrôle local (absence de progression locale ou de récidive radiologique/clinique)** comme critère de jugement principal, et structure six critères secondaires standardisés — **soulagement douloureux, taux de complications majeures, taux de retraitement, réduction volumétrique tumorale (mRECIST), amélioration fonctionnelle et survie sans progression (PFS)**.

[ABSTRACT EN] Desmoid tumors are rare, locally aggressive soft tissue neoplasms that may cause substantial morbidity, including chronic pain, functional limitation, and impaired quality of life, despite lacking metastatic potential. Management remains challenging and may include active surveillance, surgery, radiotherapy, systemic therapy, or image-guided ablation. Percutaneous cryoablation has emerged as a minimally invasive option for selected patients, particularly when symptom control and local disease management are priorities. However, current evidence remains heterogeneous, and its overall efficacy and safety are uncertain. This systematic review and meta-analysis will evaluate the efficacy and safety of percutaneous cryoablation in adults with desmoid tumors. Eligible studies will include randomized controlled trials and cohort studies of adult patients treated with percutaneous cryoablation, with no comparator required. The primary outcome will be local control, defined as absence of local progression or recurrence assessed radiologically or clinically. Secondary outcomes will include pain relief, major complications, retreatment rate, tumor response or size/volume reduction, symptom or functional improvement, and progression-free survival or time to local progression. Searches will be conducted in CENTRAL, Embase, PubMed, and Scopus, with risk of bias assessed using RoB-2 and ROBINS-I. Level of Evidence II; Systematic Review.

title: Bleomycin-Induced Pulmonary Toxicity: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Incidence and Risk Factors
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Méta-analyse PRISMA 2020 (*Critical Reviews in Oncology/Hematology*, nov. 2026, IF 5,5, équipe de J. Gehl, 65 études / 7 601 patients) évaluant l'incidence et les facteurs de risque de toxicité pulmonaire à la bléomycine IV : contrairement aux cures répétées de chimiothérapie systémique (incidence globale 18 % en oncologie médicale), l'injection unique ou pauciséquentielle d'ECT à faible dose cumulative reste dépourvue de surrisque lié à l'âge ou aux métastases pulmonaires.

[ABSTRACT EN] Bleomycin remains an important component of curative regimens for malignancies such as germ cell tumors, Hodgkin lymphoma, and in the local treatment modality electrochemotherapy. A limiting toxicity is bleomycin-induced pulmonary toxicity (BIP), with considerable variance in reported incidence across studies. OBJECTIVE: To estimate the incidence of BIP after intravenous bleomycin treatment and investigate the influence of diagnostic definitions, patient characteristics, and treatment-related factors on reported incidence. METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted according to PRISMA 2020. MEDLINE, Embase, and Cochrane Library were searched through May 2026. Studies including patients aged ≥15 years treated with intravenous bleomycin were eligible. Risk of bias was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute Critical Appraisal Checklist for Prevalence Studies. Random-effects meta-analysis and prespecified subgroup analyses were performed. RESULTS: A total of 65 studies comprising 7601 patients were included. The pooled incidence of BIP was 18% (95% CI 15-21%) with substantial between-study heterogeneity (I(2) = 87.3%). Reported incidence varied by diagnostic definition, ranging from 42% in imaging-based studies to 16% in studies using symptom-based composite definitions. Diagnostic definition explained a substantial proportion of between-study heterogeneity (R(2)=28%). No significant study-level associations were found between reported BIP incidence and age, sex, year of publication, overall cumulative bleomycin dose, use of granulocyte colony-stimulating factor, smoking history, or lung metastases. CONCLUSIONS: Reported BIP incidence varies widely, largely due to differences in diagnostic definitions. Standardized, clinically meaningful diagnostic criteria are needed to improve comparability between studies and support evidence-based clinical decision-making. REGISTRATION: PROSPERO (CRDxxxxxxxxxx).

title: Longitudinal spatial mapping of tumor-immune microenvironment following electrochemotherapy of cutaneous melanoma metastases
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Étude translationnelle longitudinale par **transcriptomique spatiale unicellulaire (plateforme Xenium)** sur des biopsies séquentielles de métastases de mélanome traitées par **électrochimiothérapie (ECT)** et de métastases voisines non traitées (à l'état basal, à J2–J3 et à J9–J10 post-ECT) (*Frontiers in Immunology*, nov. 2026, IF 5,7, Open-Access PMC13771791) : au-delà de la cytotoxicité directe par électroporation réversible, l'ECT induit une **réorganisation spatiale active du microenvironnement tumoral (TME)** avec formation d'un **front immunitaire cytotoxique (lymphocytes T infiltrants, cellules myéloïdes activées)** à l'interface tumeur-stroma et déclenche une **immunité anti-tumorale régionale (effet abscopal sur les lésions non traitées)** chez **2 patients sur 3** présentant un microenvironnement basal immunopermissif, tout en faisant basculer les cellules tumorales résiduelles vers un **état dormant exprimant SOX2-OT**.

[ABSTRACT EN] Electrochemotherapy (ECT) utilizes reversible electroporation for localized chemotherapeutic delivery, where beyond local cytotoxicity, ECT acts as an in situ immunomodulator. However, the dynamic spatial orchestration of the TME that translates this localized therapy into potential abscopal-like responses in untreated lesions remains poorly understood. To uncover the mechanisms of evolving tumor microenvironment (TME) that dictate this immune activation, we applied Xenium spatial transcriptomics to longitudinally sampled in-transit cutaneous melanoma metastases from three patients, capturing baseline immune states and two distinct post-ECT intervals (two-to-three and nine-to-ten days). Furthermore, to explicitly characterize potential abscopal-like effects, biopsies were collected also from non-treated lesions. Following sample integration, we annotated cell types and identified functional subpopulations of key compartments, which we compared across treatment timepoints and patients. Further, we resolved functional spatial niches and identified spatially localized immune front, which we characterized and linked to patients' clinical responses. Our analysis uncovered heterogeneous patient trajectories: a robust local and regional responder, a localized-only responder, and a delayed regional responder. These divergent outcomes were linked to baseline TME heterogeneity that was reflected by diverging proportions of functional spatial niches. While the partial responder exhibited an immune-cold architecture, complete responders were characterized by an immune-permissive TME with a prominent immune front at the interface of malignant and immune-active niches. Molecular profiling of these spatial boundaries exposed patient-specific signatures of activation and suppression within infiltrating T cells, myeloid cells, and fibroblasts. Although the states of malignant cells remained predominantly unchanged in the partial responder, the malignant cells of complete responders transitioned into a unique SOX2-OT-expressing dormant state, sequestered within keratinocyte-rich zones and characterized by an immunosuppressive signature post-treatment. Together, our findings suggest that beside local ablation, ECT might actively instigate regional anti-tumor immunity, a therapeutic effect that we observed in two patients harboring a permissive TME. Further, our deep spatial TME profiling identifies several exploratory observations on the effects of ECT that should be addressed in future studies.

title: Intervertebral disc versus vertebral body as the percutaneous sample site for pyogenic spondylodiscitis: Which yields a higher microbiological diagnosis? A prospective study
container-title: The spine journal : official journal of the North American Spine Society
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Étude de cohorte prospective intra-patient de très haut niveau de preuve (*The Spine Journal*, nov. 2026, IF 4,9) portant sur **68 patients** (âge médian 64,0 ans) suspects de spondylodiscite à pyogènes sans collection abcédée liquidienne, chez qui une **biopsie percutanée simultanée du disque intervertébral ET du corps vertébral adjacent** a été réalisée : **le prélèvement du disque intervertébral offre un taux de positivité bactériologique significativement supérieur à celui du corps vertébral (51,5 % [35/68] vs 32,4 % [22/68], $p = 0,002$ au test apparié de McNemar)** ; en analyse multivariée GEE, le site discal, l'élévation de la VS, de la procalcitonine (PCT), de l'IL-6 et l'inflammation aiguë en histopathologie sont indépendamment associés à la positivité des cultures ($p < 0,05$).

[ABSTRACT EN] Background context Pyogenic spondylodiscitis requires microbiological confirmation, yet percutaneous sample collection yield remains modest. The optimal sampling site in patients without drainable abscess is controversial. Retrospective studies suggest the disc may outperform the vertebral body, but evidence is limited by design biases, leaving the question unresolved. Purpose To determine whether the intervertebral disc or the vertebral body provides a better percutaneous biopsy site for microbiological diagnosis in patients with pyogenic spondylodiscitis. Study design Prospective cohort study conducted at a single spine center. Patient sample A total of 68 patients with high clinical suspicion of pyogenic spondylodiscitis who underwent C-arm guided percutaneous biopsy between January 2024 and April 2025. Outcome measures Positive rate of bacterial culture (including aerobic and anaerobic) from biopsy specimens; factors associated with positive culture using generalized estimating equations (GEE). Methods All enrolled patients underwent simultaneous percutaneous sample collections of both the vertebral body and the intervertebral disc under C-arm guidance. Specimens were sent for bacterial culture, anaerobic culture, metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS), and histopathological examination. The McNemar test was used to compare paired culture positivity rates between the two sites. Multivariable analysis was performed using GEE to identify factors associated with positive cultures. Results Of 279 screened patients with suspected spinal infections, 68 were included (39 males, 29 females; median age 64.0 years). The intervertebral disc yielded a significantly higher microbial identification rate than the vertebral body (35/68 [51.5%] vs. 22/68 [32.4%]; P=0.002). On multivariable analysis, factors significantly associated with positive cultures included male sex, elevated preoperative dynamic erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR), increased procalcitonin (PCT), elevated interleukin-6 (IL-6), histopathological evidence of acute inflammation, and biopsy site (all P Conclusions In patients with pyogenic spondylodiscitis requiring solid-tissue sampling, percutaneous sampling of the intervertebral disc yields a significantly higher bacterial culture positivity rate than sampling of the vertebral body. Male sex, elevated ESR, PCT, IL-6, and acute inflammation on histopathology are also associated with positive cultures. These findings support prioritizing the intervertebral disc as the preferred percutaneous sampling target-reserving direct aspiration for accessible fluid collections-to optimize microbiological diagnosis in pyogenic spondylodiscitis.

title: Ultrasound-guided biopsy for osteolytic lesions of the appendicular skeleton without extra-osseous component
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Étude comparative rétrospective monocentrique en centre orthopédique tertiaire portant sur **100 patients consécutifs** présentant une **lésion ostéolytique ou mixte du squelette appendiculaire avec amincissement ou rupture corticale mais sans aucune masse extra-osseuse des parties molles** biopsiés entre novembre 2022 et juillet 2026 (**22 sous guidage échographique** vs **78 sous guidage scanner**) (*Skeletal Radiology*, nov. 2026, IF 1,9) : à taille et profondeur lésionnelles comparables, le **rendement diagnostique de la biopsie osseuse échoguidée atteint 90,9 % (20/22, IC 95 % 70,8–98,9 %) contre 75,6 % sous scanner (59/78, IC 95 % 64,4–84,9 %, $p = 0,15$)**, tout en utilisant un **calibre d'aiguille significativement plus fin (majoritairement 14G vs 8G en TDM, $p < 0,001$)**, avec **0 % de complication** et une **suppression totale de l'irradiation** (vs DLP médian de **141 mGy·cm** [IQR 69–292] sous scanner).

[ABSTRACT EN] Objective US-guided biopsy is currently used for soft-tissue tumors or bone tumors with extra-skeletal extension. Percutaneous CT-guided biopsy is the current standard for diagnosing bone lesions, but has significant drawbacks, including radiation exposure, lack of real-time needle evaluation, and limited assessment of intralesional vascularity. We aimed to assess the diagnostic yield and feasibility of ultrasound guidance, with CT-guided biopsies as reference, in osteolytic appendicular bone lesions with cortical thinning or disruption but without an extra-osseous component. Materials and methods Retrospective analysis of 100 consecutive patients with osteolytic or mixed-pattern appendicular lesions with cortical thinning or disruption and no extra-osseous component, biopsied at a tertiary orthopedic center between November 2022 and July 2026: 22 under ultrasound guidance and 78 under CT guidance. Diagnostic yield, needle caliber, complications, and radiation dose were evaluated. Results The cohorts did not differ significantly in demographics or lesion size and depth, whereas anatomical site distribution differed (p = 0.02). The diagnostic yield for ultrasound-guided procedures was 90.9% (n = 20/22; 95% CI: 70.8-98.9%), compared to 75.6% (n = 59/78; 95% CI: 64.4-84.9%) for the CT-guided group (p = 0.15). Needle caliber was significantly smaller in the ultrasound-guided group (predominantly 14 G versus 8 G; p Conclusion Our preliminary experience suggests that ultrasound-guided biopsy may represent a feasible complementary approach to CT guidance in selected osteolytic (or mixed) appendicular bone lesions with cortical involvement even without an extra-osseous extension.

title: French protocol for the diagnosis and management of chronic nonbacterial osteomyelitis
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Synthèse officielle du **Protocole National de Diagnostic et de Soins (PNDS) français** sur l'**ostéomyélite chronique non bactérienne (OCNB / CNO)** et le spectre du **syndrome SAPHO** (Synovite, Acné, Pustulose, Hyperostose, Ostéite) (*La Revue de Médecine Interne*, nov. 2026, IF 1,1) : établit l'**IRM corps entier (Whole-Body MRI)** comme l'examen de référence absolu révélant le caractère **multifocal et symétrique** des lésions inflammatoires métaphysaires des membres inférieurs, de la clavicule, de la mandibule ou du rachis (souvent asymptomatiques), et formalise une règle décisionnelle cruciale pour le radiologue interventionnel — **éviter les biopsies osseuses inutiles dans les formes multifocales typiques**, mais **réaliser impérativement une biopsie osseuse percutanée dans les formes unifocales ou atypiques** pour éliminer une ostéomyélite infectieuse, un sarcome d'Ewing, un ostéosarcome ou un lymphome osseux avant d'instaurer les AINS, les bisphosphonates IV ou les anti-TNF.

[ABSTRACT EN] Chronic Nonbacterial Osteomyelitis (CNO) is a primary, non-infectious inflammatory bone disorder predominantly affecting children (median age 10 years), with a female predominance. It presents as bone pain with an inflammatory pattern, sometimes accompanied by localised swelling, and follows a relapsing-remitting course. Typical lesions involve the metaphysis of the lower limbs, while clavicular, mandibular, and vertebral involvement may also occur, the latter often being asymptomatic. Cutaneous manifestations (such as palmoplantar pustulosis), articular features, or gut inflammation may coexist, placing the disease within the broader spectrum of Synovitis, Acne, Pustulosis, Hyperostosis, and Osteitis (SAPHO) syndrome. Diagnosis is based on imaging, with whole-body MRI being the gold standard in children. It reveals multiple, symmetric inflammatory bone lesions often exceeding the clinically apparent sites. Bone biopsy is reserved for atypical or unifocal presentations or when a diagnostic uncertainty persists. Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) are the first-line treatment. In refractory cases or in patients with vertebral involvement, second-line therapies - including intravenous bisphosphonates or TNF inhibitors - may be considered off-label. Management primarily aims to control pain and preserve quality of life. Overall prognosis is favourable, with spontaneous remission in most patients after a median disease duration of four years. However, up to 50% of patients still experience flares after five years, and orthopaedic sequelae or spinal deformities may persist. General practitioners play a key role in early recognition, appropriate referral to specialist care, avoidance of unnecessary bone biopsies, and initial therapeutic management.

title: Quantitative imaging-pathology correlation in nodular fasciitis and diagnostic discrimination from sarcoma
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Étude rétrospective sur 261 patients (*Insights into Imaging*, nov. 2026 : 128 fasciites nodulaires et 133 sarcomes des tissus mous en IRM 3T) démontrant que l'ADC moyen et le signe de la queue fasciale combinés aux biomarqueurs histopathologiques distinguent fasciite nodulaire et sarcome avec une AUC de 0,96.

[ABSTRACT EN] Objectives To investigate associations between key magnetic resonance imaging features of nodular fasciitis (NF) and quantitative histopathologic biomarkers, and to evaluate whether their integration provides complementary information for differentiating NF from soft tissue sarcoma (STS) in diagnostically equivocal settings. Materials and methods This retrospective study included 128 patients with NF and 133 with STS who underwent preoperative 3-T MRI between May 2023 and June 2025. Two blinded musculoskeletal radiologists independently evaluated predefined imaging features, including fascial tail sign, T2 heterogeneity score, enhancement pattern, perilesional edema, and mean/minimum apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC). Histopathology quantified cellular density, collagen content, and myxoid degeneration. Imaging-pathology correlations were assessed using Spearman analysis and multivariable regression. Diagnostic performance of MRI-only, pathology-only, and combined models was evaluated using logistic regression, receiver operating characteristic (ROC), area under the curve (AUC) analysis, calibration, decision curve analysis, and bootstrap validation. Results T2 heterogeneity correlated positively with myxoid degeneration (ρ = 0.52) and negatively with collagen content (ρ = -0.28) (p Conclusion Imaging features of NF were associated with underlying stromal and cellular substrates. Integrating imaging features with quantitative pathology biomarkers may support radiology-pathology concordance assessment in selected diagnostically equivocal cases. Key points Question How can we improve radiology-pathology concordance and reduce interpretative variability for NF cases presenting with suspicious, diagnostically equivocal magnetic resonance imaging findings? Findings T2 heterogeneity and diffusion measurements are associated with stromal composition and cellularity, while predefined MRI features demonstrated substantial-to-excellent inter-reader agreement. Critical relevance statement Embedding explicit AHA criteria in the prompt let an 8B model approach 671B-model agreement (38.91-81.52%), supporting standardized text-based workflows without fine-tuning.

title: MRI-based virtual radiographs of the pelvis for assessment of acetabular morphology
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Étude de validation sur 103 sujets (50 patients symptomatiques explorés pour conflit fémoro-acétabulaire ou dysplasie de hanche et 53 sujets asymptomatiques, *European Radiology Experimental*, nov. 2026, IF 3,7, Open-Access) évaluant la génération de radiographies virtuelles (VR) de bassin de face à partir d'une séquence IRM 3D T1 VIBE Dixon (via segmentation osseuse 3D nnU-Net, synthèse de pseudo-scanner et projection conique) : biais quasi nul sur l'angle de couverture latérale de Wiberg LCE ($-0,2^\circ \pm 2,5^\circ$, $p = 0,663$), reproductibilité inter-lecteurs élevée ($	ext{ICC}/\kappa = 0,60\text{–}0,94$) et concordance diagnostique substantielle avec la radiographie standard ($\kappa = 0,62$, équivalente à la concordance inter-lecteurs de la radiographie $\kappa = 0,70$).

[ABSTRACT EN] Objectives We generated magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-based virtual radiographs (VRs) from hips with/without intra-articular contrast and compared them with conventional anteroposterior pelvic radiographs (CR) regarding measurement bias, interobserver and intraobserver agreement, and diagnosis of acetabular deformities; we also assessed hip deformity prevalence on VR in asymptomatic participants. Materials and methods Retrospective study of 50 patients (100 hips; mean age 34 years) with femoroacetabular impingement or hip dysplasia undergoing CR and unilateral magnetic resonance arthrography. Additionally, 53 asymptomatic participants underwent noncontrast MRI. Segmentation of the osseous pelvis was performed on T1-weighted volume interpolated breathhold examination (VIBE) Dixon MRI using 3D nnU-Net, pseudo-computed tomography generation, and cone-beam projection to generate VR. Acetabular coverage (lateral center edge angle (LCE), acetabular index (AI), anterior/posterior coverage, extrusion index (EI)), and acetabular version were compared between CR and VR. Interobserver agreement was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC) and κ statistics; bias with Bland-Altman analysis. Results Interobserver agreement for VR ranged from moderate to almost perfect (ICC/κ 0.60-0.94), except for the AI. LCE showed no significant bias with ( - 0.2° ± 2.5, p = 0.663) or without contrast ( - 0.2° ± 2.2, p = 0.530). Systematic differences occurred for AI, EI, anterior/posterior coverage, and ischial spine sign; 57-75% of discrepancies were within CR interobserver variation. Diagnostic classification showed substantial agreement between CR and VR (κ = 0.62), comparable to CR interobserver agreement (κ = 0.70). In asymptomatic participants, 13% had acetabular dysplasia, 68% normal coverage, and 19% overcoverage. Conclusion MRI-based VR provides acetabular morphology assessment comparable to CR and enables radiation-free evaluation in symptomatic patients and asymptomatic populations. Key points Question Can MRI-based virtual radiographs reproduce conventional radiographic measurements of acetabular morphology, enabling radiation-free two-dimensional assessment in symptomatic patients and asymptomatic populations? Findings The lateral center-edge angle showed no significant bias between virtual and conventional radiographs; diagnostic classification of acetabular deformities agreed substantially (κ = 0.62), comparable to conventional radiograph interobserver agreement. Relevance Statement MRI-derived virtual radiographs can provide acetabular measurements comparable to conventional radiographs without ionizing radiation, supporting integration into three-dimensional surgical planning and enabling assessment in young patients and population-based cohorts where repeated radiographs are undesirable.

title: Peripheral and soft-tissue vascular malformations in the 2025 ISSVA classification: a practical MRI approach
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Article didactique de référence (*Insights into Imaging*, nov. 2026, IF 4,1, Open-Access) traduisant la mise à jour **ISSVA 2025** en un **algorithme d'interprétation IRM pratique en 4 étapes** pour les malformations vasculaires périphériques et des parties molles : (1) **hémodynamique** en angio-IRM dynamique (flux lent vs flux rapide / shunt artério-veineux), (2) **composante vasculaire dominante** (veineuse, lymphatique macro/microkystique, capillaire ou combinée), (3) **composition tissulaire non vasculaire** (contingent fibro-adipeux de type FAVA, phlébolithes, thrombi) et (4) **extension anatomique critique** (envahissement musculaire, articulaire, osseux ou périnerveux conditionnant la faisabilité de la sclérothérapie ou de la cryoablation).

[ABSTRACT EN] The 2025 update of the International Society for the Study of Vascular Anomalies (ISSVA) classification introduced several imaging-relevant changes, including the recognition of potentially unique vascular anomalies. Although the main framework for vascular tumors remains unchanged, with continued subdivision into benign, borderline, and malignant tumors, the most radiologically relevant structural changes concern vascular malformations, which were reorganized into fast-flow lesions, slow-flow lesions, and developmental anomalies of named vessels. These updates are important for radiologists because imaging plays a central role in assessing hemodynamic characteristics, defining lesion extent, and identifying findings relevant to procedural planning and multidisciplinary management. This educational review presents an author-derived four-step framework that organizes established MRI observations for peripheral and soft-tissue vascular malformations according to the structure and terminology of the 2025 ISSVA classification, including hemodynamic assessment, vascular components, tissue composition, lesion extent, and treatment-relevant anatomy. KEY POINTS: Question Imaging-relevant organizational and terminology changes in the 2025 ISSVA classification require practical guidance for consistent MRI assessment and reporting of peripheral and soft-tissue vascular malformations. Findings An author-derived four-step, flow-based framework organizes hemodynamics, dominant vascular components, tissue composition, lesion extent, and treatment-relevant anatomy into structured MRI assessment. Critical relevance statement The MRI-focused framework provides a practical way to apply the 2025 ISSVA classification consistently in image interpretation, terminology, and reporting of peripheral and soft-tissue vascular malformations.

title: Diagnostic accuracy of 3D MRI rendering techniques for evaluation of hourglass-like constrictions in Parsonage-Turner syndrome
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Étude rétrospective multi-lecteurs en aveugle sur **30 neurographies IRM 3 Tesla 3D isotropiques (1 mm)** du plexus brachial (20 syndromes de Parsonage-Turner avec atteinte du nerf supra-scapulaire et 10 témoins, *Skeletal Radiology*, nov. 2026, IF 1,9) évaluée par 4 radiologues ostéo-articulaires : les reconstructions **MIP (Maximum Intensity Projection)** et **cMPR (reformatage multiplanaire curviligne)** offrent une **excellente sensibilité (90–100 % en MIP et 85–100 % en cMPR)** et une concordance inter-lecteurs substantielle à quasi parfaite pour détecter la présence et le nombre de **constrictions en sablier (hourglass-like constrictions, HGC) sévères** ($\text{AC1} = 0,67\text{–}0,70$ ; $\text{ICC} = 0,65\text{–}0,79$), le MIP étant **3 fois plus rapide à interpréter (médiane 33 s vs 104 s, $p < 0,001$)**.

[ABSTRACT EN] Objective To evaluate inter-reader agreement and diagnostic accuracy of curved multiplanar reformatting (cMPR) and maximum intensity projection (MIP) techniques for detecting hourglass-like constrictions (HGCs). Materials and methods Thirty brachial plexus 3-Tesla, 3D, 1-mm isotropic MR neurography (MRN) datasets (10 patients without and 20 patients with Parsonage-Turner syndrome (PTS) affecting the suprascapular nerve (SSN)) were retrospectively analyzed by four musculoskeletal radiology fellows for the number and severity of HGCs using both post-processing views in a randomized, blinded fashion. An experienced, attending radiologist served as the reference standard. Inter-reader agreement was assessed using Gwet's AC1 and intraclass correlation (ICC). Image interpretation time was compared using Wilcoxon signed-rank test. Results Inter-reader agreement for HGC presence was substantial to almost perfect among fellows (cMPR AC1 = 0.7, MIP AC1 = 0.67) and when compared to the attending (cMPR AC1 = 0.67-0.83, MIP AC1 = 0.63-0.83). Agreement for severe HGC count was substantial to almost perfect (fellows: cMPR ICC = 0.65, MIP ICC = 0.79; vs. attending: ICC = 0.62-0.83, MIP ICC = 0.69-0.88), but poor to fair for mild HGCs (fellows: cMPR ICC = 0.23, MIP ICC = 0.26; vs. attending: ICC = 0-0.21, MIP ICC = 0-0.09). Sensitivity to HGC presence was excellent (cMPR, 85-100%; MIP, 90-100%), though specificity (cMPR, 50-100%; MIP, 40-90%) and diagnostic accuracy (cMPR, 80-90%; MIP, 76-90%) varied. The MIP method required significantly less interpretation time than cMPR (median: 33 vs. 104 s, p Conclusion High inter-reader agreement and sensitivity but variable specificity for HGC detection suggest both techniques are viable tools for MRN, with cMPR better suited for detailed HGC evaluation and MIP for initial screening.

title: Short-term clinical and imaging outcomes after ultrasound-guided cooled radiofrequency ablation for advanced knee osteoarthritis: a retrospective cohort study
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Étude de cohorte (*Pain Management*, nov. 2026, 31 patients / 35 genoux, 91 % de gonarthrose sévère Kellgren-Lawrence 3–4) démontrant une baisse significative des douleurs (marche, repos, nuit) et une diminution de la synovite en IRM (Hoffa-synovitis / effusion-synovitis) sans aggravation des lésions osseuses sous-chondrales (BML) ni de l'arthrose à 3 mois.

[ABSTRACT EN] OBJECTIVE: To evaluate short-term clinical and imaging outcomes after ultrasound-guided cooled radiofrequency ablation (CRFA) in patients predominantly with advanced knee osteoarthritis (KOA). METHODS: This retrospective cohort analysis included prospectively recorded data from 31 patients (35 knees; age, 73.6 ± 8.8 years; Kellgren-Lawrence [KL] grade 3 or 4 in 91%). Outcomes at baseline and 3 months included visual analog scale (VAS) pain, Knee Injury and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score (KOOS), KL grade, mechanical axis percentage, and MRI Osteoarthritis Knee Score assessments of bone marrow lesions (BMLs), Hoffa-synovitis, and effusion-synovitis. Sensitivity analysis retained the first-treated knee in bilateral cases. RESULTS: VAS changes were -9.3 for rest pain, -24.0 for walking pain, and -15.0 for night pain (all p < 0.05). Walking VAS decreased by at least 30% in 65.7% and by at least 50% in 42.9% of knees. Four KOOS subscales improved, including KOOS Pain by 12.8 points (p < 0.001). No significant group-level changes were observed in KL grade, alignment, or BML scores. Hoffa-synovitis and effusion-synovitis scores decreased. No serious procedure-related adverse events were documented. CONCLUSION: CRFA was associated with improved pain and function at 3 months without group-level worsening in KL grade, alignment, or BML scores. Longer-term controlled studies are required.

title: Evolving role of cryoablation and cryoneurolysis for interventional pain management
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Mise au point de référence publiée dans *European Radiology* (nov. 2026, IF 4,7, équipe de D. Filippiadis) structurant les indications, le mécanisme d'axonotmésis réversible (classification de Sunderland II) et les protocoles de cryoablation tumorale (ostéome ostéoïde, métastases osseuses, tumeurs des parties molles) et de cryoneurolyse périphérique (nerfs intercostaux, clunéaux, géniculés, névrome de Morton).

[ABSTRACT EN] Despite advances in pain management, pain remains a major global health challenge in both oncological and non-oncological patients. Long-term pharmacological treatment is often restricted by insufficient therapeutic benefit and adverse events, highlighting the need for alternative approaches such as image-guided pain therapies. The idea of treating pain with cold has been recognized for centuries, and today cryotherapy has emerged as a valuable minimally invasive option for pain management. Cryoablation refers to the destruction of tissue with extreme cold and has an increasing role, especially in the treatment of benign (e.g., osteoid osteoma), malignant bone (i.e., metastases), and soft tissue tumors, either with a curative or palliative intent. Cryoneurolysis is a related but distinct application, focusing either on peripheral nerve modulation or nerve destruction. Cryoneurolysis may be highly effective for the treatment of acute or chronic pain, including sympathetic neurolysis in cancer and non-cancer-related pain syndromes. The general approach in patients with tumor-related pain depends on whether the lesion itself can be ablated or not. In non-oncologic patients, cryoneurolysis of the responsible nerve is typically performed following a positive response to a diagnostic nerve block. Potential indications for cryotherapy are constantly evolving; however, evidence, especially for cryoneurolysis, is still limited and based mostly on single-center case series and retrospective studies. Standardized ablation protocols are lacking, and for the duration of cycles, most experts rely on imaging visualization and validated protocols. Equally important, successful integration of cryoablation and cryoneurolysis into daily practice requires structured workflows across different patient pathways and interdisciplinary management. KEY POINTS: Question Pain management remains a major global health challenge and an unmet need in oncological and non-oncological patients. Findings Cryotherapy, in terms of cryoablation and cryoneurolysis, is increasingly incorporated in multimodal curative and palliative pain care concepts, for treatment of acute and chronic pain syndromes. Clinical relevance Advancement and validation of standardized treatment protocols are needed to strengthen evidence and further enhance clinical implementation in interventional radiology practice and interdisciplinary patient care.

title: Considerations for cervical medial branch nerve radiofrequency at spinal motion segments adjacent to cervical fusion constructs: a technical note
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Note technique et radio-anatomique de référence (*Pain Medicine*, nov. 2026, IF 2,9, Open-Access) analysant l'impact des montages d'arthrodèse cervicale antérieure (ACDF) et postérieure (vis de masses latérales ou vis pédiculaires) sur l'intégrité des **branches médiales cervicales (MBN)** lors de la prise en charge d'un syndrome facettaire du segment adjacent : alors que l'arthrodèse cervicale antérieure (ACDF) préserve intégralement les branches médiales postérieures, **l'instrumentation cervicale postérieure par vis de masses latérales ou vis pédiculaires interrompt presque systématiquement la branche médiale au niveau des vertèbres instrumentées**, ce qui permet d'adapter le nombre de nerfs à bloquer et à thermocoaguler sur le segment mobile adjacent.

[ABSTRACT EN] Background Cervical fusion alters regional biomechanics and increases load transmission through adjacent facet joints, which may produce facet-mediated pain. Cervical medial branch blocks (MBBs) and radiofrequency ablation (RFA) remain highly useful diagnostic and therapeutic interventions; however, surgical approaches used in cervical fusion frequently disrupt the cervical medial branch nerves (MBNs) at treated levels. Identifying which MBNs remain anatomically intact is essential for accurate diagnostic and therapeutic targeting of relevant nerves (and sensate facet joints) and for avoiding unnecessary procedure levels or procedures altogether. Objective To present an approach to determining which cervical medial branches require management after fusion, drawing upon the surgical approach, anatomic landmarks, implant trajectory, and cross-sectional imaging. Design Technical note. Setting Cervical RFA following spinal fusion surgery. Conclusions A systematic, anatomy-based method improves diagnostic precision, reduces unnecessary procedures, and helps identify patients most likely to benefit from interventions. Posterior cervical fusion using modern screw-and-rod instrumentation will essentially always result in denervation of the MBN at the operated level(s). Anterior surgical approaches reliably preserve the MBNs, making them viable targets for cervical RFA.

title: Denervation Techniques for Chronic Low Back Pain due to Lumbar Facet Joint Arthropathy: A Comparison Between Radiofrequency and Endoscopic Neurotomy
container-title: Pain practice : the official journal of World Institute of Pain
abstract:
