[SYNTHÈSE FR] Étude prospective comparative sur **65 patients** (âge médian 62 ans, EVA initiale médiane de 8,0 [IQR 7,0–9,0] et score COMI-back de 8,6) suivis **12 mois** après dénervation facettaire lombaire par **radiofréquence thermique percutanée multi-étagée (RFN)** ou par neurotomie endoscopique (EN) (*Pain Practice*, nov. 2026, IF 2,7) : si les deux techniques réduisent significativement l'EVA en post-opératoire immédiat, **l'effet antalgique à 12 mois se maintient de façon stable dans le groupe radiofréquence percutanée (RFN)** alors que les scores de douleur remontent dans le groupe endoscopique, avec un **taux de complications significativement plus faible ($p < 0,007$)** et un **coût total significativement inférieur ($p < 0,01$)** pour la radiofréquence percutanée.

[ABSTRACT EN] Purpose Radiofrequency neurotomy (RFN) of the lumbar medial branch is the standard of care for facet joint arthropathy-related chronic low back pain (CLBP). However, endoscopic neurotomy (EN) has also recently been adopted as a feasible treatment option for CLBP. The increasing population of patients with cardiac implantable electronic devices (CIEDs) highlights the need for alternative denervation methods to avoid device interference. We propose that both RFN and EN are effective for CLBP, with EN offering a safe option for patients with CIEDs and therapy-resistant aberrant innervation. Methods Patients with facet joint arthropathy-related CLBP who were treated between 01.01.2016 and 31.12.2019 were prospectively included and grouped as RFN or EN based on treatment. Over a 12-month period, the following outcomes were studied: Core Outcome Measures Index for the back (COMI-back), Visual Analogue Scale (VAS), complications, and costs. Results Sixty-five patients (35 female) with a median age of 62 years were included. Prior to the intervention, patients had a median COMI-back of 8.6 (IQR: 7.7-9.0) and a median VAS score of 8.0 (IQR: 7.0-9.0). After intervention, the VAS score dropped significantly for both groups. Thereafter, pain scores rose in the EN group, whereas VAS levels in the RFN group remained unaltered. Complication rates were significantly lower after RFN compared with EN patients (p Conclusion In conclusion, this prospective study shows that both EN and percutaneous multilevel RFN are safe and effective treatments for facet joint arthropathy-associated CLBP. RFN is preferred as the first treatment option for uncomplicated CLBP due to its lower invasiveness, while EN is suitable as an alternative for patients with CIEDs and those with therapy-resistant aberrant innervation or anatomical variations.

title: Alternative Neuroablative Strategies in Facet-Mediated Pain: Cryoneurolysis Following Incomplete RFA
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Observation clinique démonstrative (*Case Reports in Radiology*, nov. 2026, IF 0,9, Open-Access PMC13748811) évaluant la **cryoneurolyse percutanée des branches médiales articulaires postérieures** comme stratégie neuro-ablative de rattrapage chez une patiente de 46 ans souffrant d'une **arthrose facettaire lombaire droite L4–L5 et L5–S1** en échec après **deux procédures successives de radiofréquence thermique (RFA)** : la cryoneurolyse permet d'obtenir une **réduction majeure de la douleur lombaire de 8/10 à 3/10 (baisse de 5 points NRS)** accompagnée d'une **récupération post-procédurale aiguë nettement plus confortable et moins algique** qu'après thermocoagulation par radiofréquence.

[ABSTRACT EN] Lumbar facet arthropathy is a common diagnosis that directly correlates with age and is a condition with no formal treatment. A 46-year-old female with chronic right lower back and buttock pain has CT scans which revealed right L4-L5 and L5-S1 facet joint arthrosis. After the patient received two radiofrequency ablation procedures, with the latter being less effective than the first, the patient's pain was still present. Because of persistent pain, cryoneurolysis was proposed as an alternative intervention. The patient experienced a similar degree of pain relief (pain level 8/10-3/10) as well as a more favorable acute postprocedural recovery. This depicts how cryoneurolysis represents a promising alternative neuroablative strategy for patients with lumbar facet arthropathy who have experienced inadequate relief following radiofrequency ablation.

title: Intra-articular sacroiliac joint radiofrequency ablation for persistent low back pain after lumbar fusion: a retrospective single-cohort study
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Étude rétrospective monocentrique avec suivi longitudinal de **24 mois** portant sur **51 patients consécutifs** (âge moyen $67,3 \pm 2,1\text{ ans}$ ; délai moyen post-arthrodèse lombaire de **$5,1 \pm 2,0\text{ ans}$**) souffrant de **douleurs sacro-iliaques persistantes après fusion lombaire** confirmées par deux blocs tests diagnostiques fluoroguidés positifs et traités par **radiofréquence (RF) intra-articulaire sacro-iliaque bilatérale** (*Pain Management*, nov. 2026, IF 2,0) : le score douloureux **EVA moyen chute de $7,6 \pm 1,0$ à l'état basal à $2,4 \pm 1,6$ à 1 mois ($-68\%$) et se maintient à $3,8 \pm 2,4$ à 24 mois ($-50\%$, $p < 0,001$)**, tandis que l'indice d'incapacité d'**Oswestry (ODI) diminue de $52 \pm 13$ à $28 \pm 11$ à 1 mois et $38 \pm 16$ à 24 mois ($p < 0,001$)**, avec **0 % de complication**.

[ABSTRACT EN] Aims Persistent low back pain after lumbar fusion is common, and the sacroiliac joint (SIJ) is an increasingly recognized pain generator. We evaluated outcomes following intra-articular SIJ radiofrequency (RF) ablation in post-fusion patients with confirmed SIJ-mediated pain. Patients and methods This retrospective study included patients with prior lumbar fusion who underwent bilateral intra-articular SIJ RF ablation after fluoroscopy-guided diagnostic blocks. All had previously received SIJ steroid injection. Visual Analog Scale (VAS) and Oswestry Disability Index (ODI) scores were assessed through 24 months using repeated-measures analysis of variance. Results Fifty-one patients were included (mean age, 67.3 ± 2.1 years; mean interval from fusion to RF ablation, 5.1 ± 2.0 years). Mean VAS decreased from 7.6 ± 1.0 at baseline to 2.4 ± 1.6 at 1 month and 3.8 ± 2.4 at 24 months ( p p Conclusions Intra-articular SIJ RF ablation was associated with improved pain and function in selected post-fusion patients with confirmed SIJ-mediated pain. Without a comparator, causal conclusions cannot be drawn, and findings should not be generalized to post-fusion pain without confirmed SIJ involvement.

title: Opioid-Sparing Pain Control in Lung Transplantation: A Single-Center Experience with Intraoperative Intercostal Nerve Cryoablation
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Étude de cohorte rétrospective appariée évaluant l'effet de la **cryoneurolyse des nerfs intercostaux** chez **19 patients transplantés pulmonaires** comparés à **38 témoins appariés** (*Journal of Chest Surgery*, nov. 2026, IF 1,3) : la cryoneurolyse intercostale est associée à une **réduction de 29 % de la consommation cumulée d'opioïdes sur les 14 premiers jours post-opératoires** (**$428\text{ MME}$ contre $603\text{ MME}$** en équivalents morphiniques oraux), une **tendance à la baisse de l'incidence du délirium post-opératoire (58 % vs 66 %)** et de la durée de ventilation mécanique et d'hospitalisation, avec **0 % de complication liée à la cryoablation**.

[ABSTRACT EN] Background Postoperative pain following lung transplantation is substantial and contributes to opioid exposure, delirium risk, and prolonged recovery. We evaluated the impact of intraoperative intercostal nerve cryoablation on postoperative opioid use, delirium incidence, and early clinical outcomes. Methods We conducted a single-center retrospective matched cohort study of adult lung transplant recipients. Patients who underwent intraoperative intercostal nerve cryoablation (intervention) were compared with a historical matched cohort of recipients who did not undergo cryoablation (control). The primary outcome was cumulative opioid use, measured in oral morphine milligram equivalents (MME), during the first 14 postoperative days. Secondary outcomes included delirium incidence, ventilator days, intensive care unit and hospital lengths of stay, and early postoperative complications. Results The study included 19 patients in the cryoablation group and 38 matched controls. Cryoablation was associated with a reduction in cumulative opioid use through postoperative day 14 (428 MME vs. 603 MME, p=0.681). Rates of postoperative delirium were slightly lower in the intervention group (58% vs. 66%, p=0.571). Cryoablation was not associated with increased complications. There were trends toward shorter median ventilator duration and total hospital length of stay in the intervention group, although results were not statistically significant. Conclusion Intraoperative intercostal nerve cryoablation is a feasible and safe adjunct in lung transplantation and is associated with reduced early postoperative opioid use. These findings support further prospective evaluation of cryoablation as an opioid-sparing strategy in lung transplant recipients.

title: Successful treatment of knee osteoarthritis pain with alcohol neurolysis of genicular nerves based on new anatomical landmark: A case report
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Publication clinique et anatomique (*Medicine (Baltimore)*, nov. 2026, IF 1,4, Open-Access) démontrant l'efficacité d'une **neurolyse fluoroguidée des trois nerfs géniculés principaux — supéro-latéral (SLGN), supéro-médial (SMGN) et inféro-médial (IMGN) — utilisant de nouveaux repères osseux dérivés de dissections cadavériques avec ajustement postérieur du positionnement des aiguilles** chez un patient de 77 ans souffrant de **gonarthrose sévère réfractaire aux infiltrations intra-articulaires de corticoïdes (douleur initiale $\text{NRS} = 7/10$)** : le positionnement plus postérieur le long de la jonction diaphyso-épiphysaire fémorale et tibiale permet de **capturer les ramifications articulaires manquées par la cible classique à mi-profondeur**, procurant une **baisse stable du score NRS de $7/10$ à $3/10$ ($-57\%$) à 1, 3 et 6 mois**, avec **0 % de complication**.

[ABSTRACT EN] Knee osteoarthritis (OA) is a major cause of chronic knee pain and disability. Genicular nerve neurolysis is a minimally invasive treatment option for patients whose pain persists despite conventional therapies. However, landmark-guided genicular nerve neurolysis can miss some articular branches. We report a patient with persistent knee OA pain who was successfully treated with alcohol neurolysis of the genicular nerves using newly proposed landmarks. A 77-year-old man continued to have right-knee pain (Numeric Rating Scale [NRS] 7) despite an intra-articular steroid injection. The patient was diagnosed with severe knee OA. He underwent fluoroscopy-guided alcohol neurolysis of the superolateral, superomedial, and inferomedial genicular nerves using 50% alcohol mixed with 2% lidocaine; needle placement was adjusted posteriorly according to newly proposed landmarks derived from cadaveric anatomy. The knee pain decreased to NRS 3 at 1, 3, and 6 months after the procedure without complications. This case shows that genicular nerve alcohol neurolysis, with posteriorly adjusted new landmarks, can markedly reduce knee OA pain, highlighting its potential clinical utility.

title: Local Control Options for Metastatic Disease in Sarcoma
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Revue de synthèse oncologique de référence (*Current Oncology Reports*, nov. 2026, IF 4,7) comparant les trois piliers du contrôle local des oligométastases de sarcomes des parties molles — métastasectomie chirurgicale, radiothérapie stéréotaxique (SBRT) et **ablation thermique percutanée guidée par l'image (RFA, cryoablation, MWA)** : les trois modalités offrent des taux élevés et comparables de contrôle local et de survie sans progression chez les patients oligométastatiques sélectionnés (intervalle libre prolongé, faible nombre de lésions, histologie léiomyosarcome ou liposarcome), l'ablation percutanée se distinguant par son caractère répétable, sa faible morbidité et sa synergie immunologique potentielle.

[ABSTRACT EN] Purpose of review To review the current evidence on local treatment strategies for oligometastatic soft tissue sarcoma at pulmonary and extrapulmonary sites, and evaluate their impact on oncological outcomes. Recent findings Pulmonary metastasectomy remains the most established local treatment, with 5-year survival rates of 20-58%. Complete (R0) resection, a longer disease-free interval, and fewer metastases are associated with improved outcomes. Stereotactic radiotherapy achieves high local control rates with low toxicity, and a recent systematic review reported survival outcomes comparable to surgery. Image-guided thermal ablation also achieves high local control rates for lung metastases of 1 cm or smaller and offers a minimally invasive option for extrapulmonary metastases. For all modalities, current data are derived predominantly from retrospective studies, and direct comparisons are lacking. Local treatment offers promising outcomes for carefully selected patients with oligometastatic soft tissue sarcoma. Surgery, stereotactic radiotherapy, and thermal ablation should be considered complementary options, selected within a multidisciplinary tumor board according to lesion size, number, and location. Prospective studies are needed to define optimal patient selection and determine the comparative effectiveness of these modalities.

title: [Image-guided minimally invasive treatment options for endometriosis]
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Mise au point structurée et série institutionnelle (*Die Radiologie [Heidelberg]*, nov. 2026, IF 1,1) évaluant l'ensemble des traitements mini-invasifs guidés par l'imagerie de l'endométriose : **la cryoablation percutanée détient le niveau de preuve le plus élevé pour les localisations extrapéritonéales et intramusculaires (endométriose pariétale abdominale)** et constitue une alternative mini-invasive validée à l'exérèse chirurgicale pariétale délabrante, tandis que la sclérothérapie à l'éthanol est établie pour les endométriomes ovariens et que les HIFU, la RFA et les micro-ondes restent complémentaires ou en cours d'évaluation.

[ABSTRACT EN] Background Endometriosis affects approximately 10% of women of reproductive age with a mean diagnostic delay of 7-10 years. Image-guided procedures show increasingly promising results as minimally invasive alternatives to excision. Objective Structured overview of image-guided minimally invasive treatment options for endometriosis with focus on percutaneous cryoablation. Results Percutaneous cryoablation demonstrates the strongest evidence for extraperitoneal and intramuscular lesions and represents a valid minimally invasive alternative to excision. Three institutional cases illustrate technique and outcomes. Ethanol sclerotherapy is established for ovarian endometriomas. High-intensity focused ultrasound (HIFU) shows promising results for abdominal wall disease; radiofrequency ablation (RFA) and microwave ablation are investigational. Conclusion Interventional radiology offers a growing therapeutic spectrum. Prospective randomized trials are needed for guideline integration.

title: Percutaneous Cryoablation in Bone Tumors: Current Applications, Technical Considerations, Clinical Outcomes, and Future Perspectives
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Revue exhaustive (*Cureus*, nov. 2026, IF 1,0, Open-Access PMC13789375) synthétisant les indications, la balistique multi-sondes, les résultats oncologiques et antalgiques ainsi que la prévention des complications de la **cryoablation percutanée guidée par l'imagerie dans les tumeurs osseuses bénignes et malignes** : met en exergue les avantages décisifs du froid sur les techniques thermiques chaudes (RF, micro-ondes) — **visualisation TDM directe du glaçon (*iceball*) à travers l'os cortical**, capacité à sculpter des **zones d'ablation larges et asymétriques** par synergie multi-cryosondes, **moindre douleur per- et post-procédurale**, et élargissement des indications aux **tumeurs bénignes localement agressives, à la maladie oligométastatique et aux récidives locales de tumeurs osseuses malignes**.

[ABSTRACT EN] Image-guided percutaneous cryoablation has emerged as an increasingly important minimally invasive treatment option in musculoskeletal oncology. Its applications range from the definitive treatment of selected benign bone tumors to local tumor control and pain palliation in patients with malignant primary bone lesions and skeletal metastases. Compared with heat-based ablation techniques, cryoablation offers several potential advantages, including visualization of the ice ball during treatment, the ability to create large and irregular ablation zones, and reduced procedural pain. This review aims to provide a comprehensive overview of the principles, technical considerations, clinical applications, efficacy, and complications of percutaneous cryoablation in the management of bone tumors, emphasizing its current role and future perspectives in musculoskeletal interventional oncology. Relevant publications addressing the use of image-guided cryoablation in benign and malignant bone tumors were reviewed, including clinical studies, prospective trials, retrospective series, systematic reviews, and international recommendations. Particular attention was given to treatment indications, procedural techniques, local tumor control, pain reduction, and complication prevention. Cryoablation has demonstrated favorable clinical outcomes in selected benign bone tumors, particularly osteoid osteoma, and in patients with painful skeletal metastases. Its role in locally aggressive benign tumors, oligometastatic disease, and selected recurrent malignant bone tumors is expanding. The ability to monitor the ice ball in real time facilitates treatment planning and protection of adjacent critical structures. However, pathological fractures, neural injuries, and incomplete tumor coverage remain important considerations. Percutaneous cryoablation represents a valuable addition to multidisciplinary bone tumor management. Appropriate patient selection, accurate imaging guidance, adequate ablation margins, and systematic protection of adjacent structures are essential for achieving optimal outcomes. Further prospective comparative studies are required to establish its long-term oncological efficacy and define its role relative to surgery and other ablative techniques.

title: Pudendal Neuralgia in a Tertiary Pain Clinic: Presentation, Treatment, and Factors Associated with Neuromodulation in 224 Adults
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Étude de cohorte sur 224 adultes (*Pain and Therapy*, nov. 2026, IF 3,8) évaluant le parcours interventionnel de la névralgie pudendale : bloc pudendal diagnostique réalisé chez 59,4 % des patients et radiofréquence pulsée (PRF) chez 28,6 %, avec identification d'un bloc diagnostique positif (OR ajusté = 4,88) et d'une étiologie post-chirurgicale confirmée (OR = 2,83) comme facteurs prédictifs majeurs de réponse aux thérapies de neuromodulation.

[ABSTRACT EN] INTRODUCTION: Pudendal neuralgia is an under-recognized cause of chronic, disabling neuropathic perineal pain affecting both women and men. Real-world data on its presentation, its treatment within a specialty pain service, and the factors that accompany escalation to interventional therapy are scarce. We hypothesized that an iatrogenic (postsurgical) origin and relief after a diagnostic pudendal nerve block would identify the patients who reach neuromodulation. METHODS: We performed a retrospective manual review of the complete electronic records of all adults with documented pudendal neuralgia, pudendal neuropathy, or pudendal nerve entrapment managed at a single tertiary pain clinic between 2009 and 2026. Demographics, clinical presentation, presumed etiology, treatments, and outcomes were abstracted from the free-text record. Ascertainment was in two stages: variables were first identified by structured text screening of the free-text record, and the two variables most susceptible to false-positive screening, a postsurgical etiology and receipt of neuromodulation, were then verified against the source charts by manual review of every screen-positive record. The chart-verified definitions are used throughout. Associations between binary variables were tested by the chi-squared test, with odds ratios (OR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI); factors associated with neuromodulation were assessed by multivariable logistic regression. RESULTS: Among 224 patients (138 women [61.6%], 86 men [38.4%]; median age 48.5 years, interquartile range 35-64), pain was worse when sitting in 57.6% and burning in 39.3%, and involvement was bilateral in 21.9%. Text screening identified a possible postsurgical onset in 46.4%, but chart re-adjudication confirmed a named operation preceding the pain in only 31 patients (13.8%), of whom 6 had undergone a clearly non-pelvic procedure; confirmed postsurgical onset was therefore less frequent than documented entrapment features (24.1%) and comparable to childbirth (15.9% of women). Care was heavily interventional: 59.4% received a pudendal nerve block, 28.6% pulsed radiofrequency, and 9.4% underwent surgical decompression. Neuromodulation was documented in the record of 64 patients (28.6%), but an electrode was placed in only 26 (11.6%) and a permanent device implanted in 18 (8.0%): spinal cord stimulation in 14, sacral neuromodulation in 2, dorsal root ganglion stimulation in 1, and pudendal nerve stimulation in 1. Three factors were independently associated with documented neuromodulation: relief after a diagnostic block (adjusted OR 4.88, 95% CI 1.91-12.46%), a refractory course (2.92, 1.52-5.60%), and chart-confirmed postsurgical onset (2.83, 1.17-6.82%); c-statistic 0.76. In an exploratory model restricted to the 18 implanted patients, a refractory course (7.40, 1.98-27.61%) and postsurgical onset (4.24, 1.29-13.94%) remained associated with the outcome whereas relief after a block did not (5.90, 0.72-48.31%). CONCLUSIONS: In routine pain-clinic practice, pudendal neuralgia is managed along an interventional pathway, but device implantation is considerably less common than the frequency with which neuromodulation is discussed. A confirmed postsurgical onset is less common than text screening suggests, yet is disproportionately associated with escalation. Being observational, these findings describe how care proceeds rather than establishing cause.

title: Intraarticular acetabular osteoid osteoma treated with CT-guided radiofrequency ablation after unsuccessful arthroscopy: a case report and literature review
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Publication d'octobre 2026 (*Skeletal Radiology*) illustrant le traitement curatif par radiofréquence sous scanner d'un ostéome ostéoïde intra-articulaire de la fosse acétabulaire après échec d'une résection arthroscopique, avec disparition complète de la synovite réactionnelle et des douleurs.

[ABSTRACT EN] Acetabular osteoid osteoma is uncommon, and treatment can be difficult when the lesion is intraarticular or associated with osteoarthritis. We report a 17-year-old male with an intraarticular acetabular osteoid osteoma. The lesion was located in the medial portion of the acetabular fossa and was associated with synovitis, joint effusion, joint space narrowing, and osteophyte formation. Arthroscopy was initially selected for lesion resection and joint assessment. However, the medial location limited instrument access, preventing complete resection. The residual lesion was subsequently treated with CT-guided radiofrequency ablation (RFA) using a posterior osseous trajectory and intraarticular cooling with chilled 5% dextrose solution. At 4 weeks, hip pain had completely resolved, and MRI showed resolution of perilesional bone marrow edema. Pain relief persisted through 12 months without analgesic use. A literature review summarizes previous treatment approaches for acetabular osteoid osteoma. This case illustrates that treatment planning should account for lesion location, joint condition, and technical feasibility. CT-guided RFA may be useful when a safe percutaneous trajectory to the lesion can be planned.

title: Management of sacral fragility fractures leading to spinopelvic dissociation: a scoping review
container-title: European journal of orthopaedic surgery & traumatology : orthopedie traumatologie
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Revue systématique PRISMA-ScR (*Eur J Orthop Surg Traumatol*, oct. 2026, 8 études / 235 patients) consacrée aux fractures bilatérales postérieures du sacrum par insuffisance osseuse (fractures en H/U et Rommens IVb), confirmant que le vissage percutané est la technique de référence après échec du traitement médical pour restaurer la mobilité et soulager la douleur.

[ABSTRACT EN] Purpose Fragility fractures affecting the sacrum present an increasing challenge to orthopaedic practice, due to limited comparative data and the absence of consensus on optimal management. U-Type and Rommens Type IVb fractures may result in a bilateral pattern of spinopelvic dissociation with possible neurological injury. This scoping review aims to summarise the current principles of care, indications for surgery, and outcomes of operative versus non-operative treatment for low-energy bilateral posterior sacral fractures (BPSFs). Methods This scoping review adhered to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). A systematic search of electronic databases identified studies including ≥ 10 patients with Bilateral Posterior Sacral Fractures (BPSFs) comparing operative and non-operative approaches. Two reviewers independently screened titles, abstracts, and full texts against predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria, resolving disagreements by consensus. Data were extracted using a standardised form and summarised narratively with reference to mobility, quality of life, and patient-reported outcome measures. From 421 studies screened, eight met inclusion criteria. Results From 421 screened records, eight studies including 235 patients met inclusion criteria. Operative management resulted from failed non-operative care in most cases. Percutaneous screw fixation was the most common surgical technique utilised. Although one study reported improved outcomes with early fixation, considerable heterogeneity in surgical approach and timing was observed with a similar lack of consensus on non-operative regimes and their point of 'failure'. Conclusion Operative management may enhance pain relief, mobility, and function in selected patients with BPSFs, though with notable implant-related risks. Careful patient selection remains key, and further prospective studies are needed to establish optimal non-operative management and those who would benefit from early operative intervention.

title: Photodynamic Bone Stabilization in Pathologic Humeral Fractures: Implant Safety, Pain Relief and Functional Outcomes
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Étude bicentrique sur données prospectives (*Cancers*, oct. 2026, IF 4,5, Open-Access) portant sur 51 patients métastatiques (52 fractures humérales avérées ou menaçantes Mirels 8–10) traités par ballonnet centromédullaire photopolymérisable mini-invasif (IlluminOss®) : chute rapide de la douleur (NRS de 7,1 à 2,0, p < 0,001), doublement du score fonctionnel MSTS-UE (de 9,5 à 20/30, p < 0,001), implant radiotransparent sans artefact TDM/IRM et faible taux de défaillance mécanique (7,7 %).

[ABSTRACT EN] Background: Pathologic fractures of the humerus due to metastatic disease cause severe pain, loss of function and reduced quality of life. Surgical treatment is predominantly palliative and aims to achieve rapid pain relief, early functional recovery and minimal treatment-related morbidity. The photodynamic bone stabilization system (IlluminOss ® ) is a minimally invasive, radiolucent, intramedullary device that may address these needs. Methods: This retrospective analysis of prospectively collected data from two centers included 51 patients with 52 pathologic humeral lesions (completed or impending fractures) treated with photodynamic intramedullary stabilization between 2013 and 2025. Baseline variables comprised demographics, Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status, comorbidities, pain (numeric rating scale, NRS) and function (Musculoskeletal Tumor Society Upper Extremity Score, MSTS-UE; Toronto Extremity Salvage Score, TESS). Lesion characteristics, operative details, in-hospital course, follow-up outcomes (TESS, patient satisfaction/quality of life) and long-term endpoints (survival, complications) were recorded. Results: The study cohort (25 women, 26 men; mean age 68.5 years) represented a highly palliative population with advanced, disseminated malignant disease. Of the 52 humeral lesions, 35 (67.3%) presented as pathological fractures, whereas 17 lesions (32.7%) were classified as impending fractures due to extensive osteolysis. Among the impending fractures, Mirels scores ranged from 8 to 10, with three lesions scoring 8, eight lesions scoring 9, and six lesions scoring 10. ECOG performance status was 0-2 in 75.0% and 3-4 in 25.0% of patients. Preoperative pain was high (mean NRS 7.1) and function markedly reduced (median MSTS-UE 9.5/30; median TESS 36.5/100). Postoperatively, pain improved significantly from NRS 7.1 to 2.0 ( p p p n = 44) demonstrated a median survival of 6 months for ECOG 0-2 and 3 months for ECOG 3-4. Implant failure (Henderson type III) occurred four times (7.7%) and was successfully revised with plate and/or screw osteosynthesis or diaphyseal replacement. Conclusions: Photodynamic intramedullary stabilization provides effective treatment for selected pathologic humeral lesions with low implant failure rate, offering rapid pain relief, functional improvement and low perioperative morbidity. Implant failure in complex fracture morphologies highlights the need for morphology-adapted indication and consideration of supplemental fixation in high-risk cases.

title: Long-Term Outcomes of Cement Augmented Percutaneous Pedicle Screw Fixation in Cancer-Related Vertebral Fractures
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Vaste cohorte oncologique (*Neurosurgery*, oct. 2026, IF 3,9) de 240 patients (241 interventions) traités par vissage pédiculaire percutané augmenté au ciment (cement-augmented PPSF) pour fracture vertébrale par compression pathologique d'origine métastatique, avec un suivi médian de 5,0 ans chez les survivants : taux de défaillance mécanique nécessitant une reprise chirurgicale exceptionnellement bas de 2,1 % (5/240), amélioration significative et durable de la douleur et du statut fonctionnel/neurologique.

[ABSTRACT EN] Background and objectives Pathological vertebral compression fractures (VCFs) are a common and debilitating complication of metastatic cancer. Percutaneous pedicle screw fixation (PPSF) with cement augmentation is increasingly used to stabilize these fractures, but long-term construct durability and associated clinical outcomes remain incompletely defined. We sought to characterize the long-term mechanical durability of cement-augmented PPSF for oncological VCFs, evaluate outcomes, and explore factors associated with revision surgery. Methods We conducted a retrospective review of patients with cancer who underwent cement-augmented PPSF at a tertiary cancer center between 2015 and 2020. The primary outcome was implant failure requiring return to the operating room for revision stabilization. Cumulative incidence of revision was estimated. Associations between clinical and radiographic variables and revision were evaluated using univariable competing-risks regression. Secondary outcomes included pain scores, functional status, strength, and neurological measures assessed pre- and post-operatively. Results A total of 240 patients with 241 surgeries were included (mean age 62.8 years). Median follow-up among surviving patients was 5.0 years. Five patients (2.1%) required revision surgery. Increasing age was associated with higher risk of revision in the univariable analysis (hazard ratio 1.12, 95% CI: 1.01-1.24, P = .046), while other investigated factors were not significantly associated with failure requiring revision. Significant improvements in pain and functional status were observed. Conclusion Cement-augmented PPSF demonstrated long-term durability for stabilization of oncological VCFs, with a low rate of revision surgery. Mechanical stability was accompanied by improvements in pain and functional status. Increasing age demonstrated an association with increased revision rates, although the low number of events limits definitive identification of predictors of failure.

title: Concurrent basivertebral nerve radiofrequency ablation and vertebral augmentation as part of a multimodal palliative plan for pathological vertebral compression fracture from spine tumor: A case series of three patients
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Série clinique innovante (*Interventional Pain Medicine*, oct. 2026, IF 1,8, Open-Access) évaluant l'association dans le même temps opératoire d'une ablation par radiofréquence ciblée du nerf basivertébral (BVN RFA) et d'une cimentoplastie d'augmentation vertébrale (VA) chez des patients présentant une fracture vertébrale par compression pathologique d'origine tumorale : réduction immédiate et soutenue de la douleur rachidienne avec amélioration fonctionnelle chez 100 % des patients et 0 % de complication péri- ou post-procédurale.

[ABSTRACT EN] Introduction Pathological vertebral compression fractures from spinal tumors are a source of severe back pain and functional disability. Vertebral augmentation (VA) has been utilized for mechanical stabilization; however, pain may persist due to nociceptive signaling from the basivertebral nerve (BVN). BVN radiofrequency ablation (BVNRFA) has shown efficacy for vertebrogenic back pain associated with Modic changes, but its efficacy for oncologic/pathologic fractures remains an area of exploration. Case presentation We present a case series of three patients with pathological vertebral compression fractures secondary to spinal tumors who underwent concurrent BVNRFA and VA. All three patients experienced immediate and sustained pain reduction with improvements in function. No peri- or post-procedural complications were observed at one-month follow-up. Conclusion Concurrent BVNRFA and VA is a novel and synergistic approach that may provide an additional option for select patients with pathological vertebral compression fractures from a spinal tumor within palliative and interventional pain settings. Larger studies are required to clarify ideal patient selection, duration of benefit, and safety.

title: Comparison of analgesic therapies in traumatic vertebral compression fractures: Vertebroplasty and kyphoplasty versus thermal facet ablation-a prospective randomized trial
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Essai prospectif randomisé contrôlé monocentrique de grande envergure sur **535 patients** (290 traités par augmentation vertébrale — vertébroplastie ou cyphoplastie — et 245 par radiofréquence thermique facettaire) souffrant de fractures-tassements vertébraux réfractaires au traitement conservateur (*North American Spine Society Journal — NASSJ*, oct./déc. 2026, IF 2,1, Open-Access) : à 6 mois, les deux bras procurent une analgésie majeure et comparable (**réduction moyenne d'EVA de $-5,6$ [IC 95 % : $-5,9$ à $-5,3$] après cimentoplastie vs $-5,3$ [IC 95 % : $-5,6$ à $-5,0$] après RFA**), la cimentoplastie présentant 8 % de fuites de ciment (23 cas, dont 0,5 % de décompression) et une durée de séjour de 1,4 jour contre 0 % de complication et une prise en charge purement ambulatoire (0,0 jour) pour la RFA.

[ABSTRACT EN] Background Vertebral augmentation techniques are common for painful vertebral compression fractures (VCFs). Radiofrequency thermal facet ablation (RFA) is a potential alternative analgesic therapy, but comparative data remains limited. Methods In this single-center, prospective randomized controlled trial, patients with painful VCFs refractory to conservative treatment were randomized to vertebral augmentation or RFA. Pre- and postoperative Visual Analogue Scale (VAS) for axial pain and procedure-related complications were evaluated over a 6-month period. Results Among 535 patients completing follow-up (290 augmentation, 245 RFA), both arms provided robust analgesia. Mean VAS reduction at 6 months was -5.3 (95% CI: -5.6 to -5.0) in the RFA group and -5.6 (95% CI: -5.9 to -5.3) in the augmentation group. The augmentation group had an 8% cement leakage rate (23 cases), with 2 patients (0.5%) requiring decompression, and a mean length of stay (LOS) of 1.4 days. The RFA arm demonstrated a zero-complication rate and allowed for same-day discharge (LOS 0.0 days). Conclusions RFA and vertebral augmentation are highly effective at providing significant pain relief for VCFs, with comparable reductions in pain scores. With a zero-complication rate and outpatient feasibility, RFA is a safe and resource-efficient first-line alternative to cement-based augmentation.

title: Minimally Invasive Surgery of the Pelvis and Acetabulum
container-title: The Orthopedic clinics of North America
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Mise au point de référence sur les techniques percutanées et mini-invasives de fixation de l'**anneau pelvien postérieur et antérieur ainsi que de l'acétabulum** (*Orthopedic Clinics of North America*, oct. 2026, IF 1,6) : détaille l'exploitation des **corridors intra-osseux sécurisés** (vis ilio-sacrées S1/S2, vis trans-sacrées trans-iliaques, vis rétrogrades/antérogrades de la branche pubienne supérieure, corridor supra-acétabulaire LC-2 et colonne postérieure) couplée à l'**imagerie per-opératoire 3D et aux plateformes robotisées**, démontrant une réduction drastique des complications pariétales et infectieuses et une **remise en charge accélérée chez les populations à haut risque (patients oncologiques, gériatriques fragiles et obèses)**.

[ABSTRACT EN] This review examines the evolving landscape of minimally invasive surgery (MIS) for pelvic and acetabular fractures, traditionally managed through extensile open approaches. MIS aims to optimize fracture reduction and stable fixation through limited exposures, leveraging safe intraosseous corridors and advanced intraoperative imaging. The article details contemporary percutaneous techniques for posterior and anterior pelvic ring injuries, as well as acetabular fixation methods. It highlights significant technological advancements, including endoscopic-assisted procedures, robotic platforms, and novel implants. Special focus is given to high-risk populations, including obese, geriatric, and oncology patients, who benefit from reduced wound morbidity and faster recovery.

title: Clinicopathological Spectrum and Management of Aneurysmal Bone Cysts in Atypical Anatomical Location: A Comprehensive Review of Demographics, Presentation, Diagnosis, and Treatment Outcomes
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Revue analytique de **17 publications de kystes osseux anévrismaux (KOA) de localisation anatomique atypique** sélectionnées parmi 42 études entre 2011 et 2026 (*Journal of Orthopaedic Case Reports*, oct. 2026, IF 0,8, Open-Access PMC13646818) : précise les critères diagnostiques IRM (**lésion ostéolytique expansive multiloculée avec niveaux liquide-liquide**) et l'obligation absolue d'une **confirmation histopathologique par biopsie** dans ces topographies inhabituelles (rachis, bassin, os plats, épiphyses ou diaphyses), et détaille l'individualisation thérapeutique entre **sclérothérapie percutanée mini-invasive**, curetage-comblement et résection selon les contraintes anatomiques, la maturité squelettique et le risque de récidive locale (**10 % à 30 %** dans la littérature).

[ABSTRACT EN] Aneurysmal bone cysts (ABCs) are benign but locally aggressive osteolytic lesions characterized by blood-filled cystic spaces separated by fibrous septa containing osteoclast-like giant cells and reactive bone. Although commonly affecting the metaphysis of long bones in children and adolescents, ABCs may occur in atypical anatomical locations, creating diagnostic and therapeutic challenges. The aim of this study was to review the demographic characteristics, clinical presentation, radiological and histopathological features, diagnostic challenges, and current management strategies of atypically presenting ABCs. A narrative review was performed using articles published in the Journal of Orthopaedic Case Reports from 2011 to 2026. Forty-two records were initially identified (41 case reports and 1 case series); 15 were excluded after initial screening, and 10 additional reports were excluded at full-text assessment because they described conventional metaphyseal ABCs, leaving 17 reports (16 case reports and 1 case series) for the atypical-location review. Because this was a narrative review restricted to a single journal, no pooled effect estimates or formal comparative treatment conclusions were attempted. ABCs predominantly occur during the first two decades of life and commonly involve the distal femur, proximal tibia, proximal humerus, and spine. Pain and swelling are the most frequent presenting symptoms. Radiographs typically demonstrate expansile osteolytic lesions with a multiloculated appearance, while magnetic resonance imaging frequently reveals fluid-fluid levels. Histologically, lesions consist of blood-filled spaces, fibroblastic septa, osteoclast-like giant cells, and reactive woven bone. Management options include curettage with bone grafting, sclerotherapy, en bloc resection, and reconstruction depending on lesion location and aggressiveness. Recurrence rates vary between 10% and 30%, with lower recurrence following complete excision. ABCs exhibit a wide clinicopathological spectrum. In atypical anatomical locations, diagnosis requires careful clinicoradiological correlation and histopathological confirmation. Management should be individualized according to lesion biology, anatomical constraints, skeletal maturity, and functional requirements; however, treatment effectiveness and recurrence rates cannot be established reliably from the predominantly case-report-based evidence reviewed here.

title: Clinical characteristics, anatomical distribution, and diagnostic patterns of simple bone cysts in Japan: an analysis of the Japanese Bone and Soft Tissue Tumor registry
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Plus vaste étude de registre national jamais publiée sur les **kystes osseux essentiels (KOE / simple bone cysts)**, analysant **3 164 patients** issus du *Japanese Bone and Soft Tissue Tumor (BSTT) Registry* entre 2006 et 2019 (*International Journal of Clinical Oncology*, oct. 2026, IF 2,7) : l'âge moyen au diagnostic est de **22,4 ans (extrêmes 0–89 ans)**, les trois localisations prédominantes regroupant **75,8 % des cas** sont l'**humérus (910 cas, 28,8 %)**, le **calcanéus (803 cas, 25,4 %)** et le **fémur (682 cas, 21,6 %)** ; une **confirmation anatomopathologique** a été réalisée chez **52,6 % des patients (1 663/3 164)** contre un diagnostic purement radio-clinique chez **47,4 % (1 501/3 164)**, et une intervention thérapeutique a été nécessaire chez **1 480 patients (46,8 %)**, majoritairement sur les os longs porteurs à haut risque de fracture pathologique.

[ABSTRACT EN] Background Simple bone cysts are benign cystic bone lesions that occur predominantly in children and adolescents, although they might occur in all ages. Previous studies have described clinical features and treatment options; however, large-scale epidemiological data from Japan are limited. We aimed to investigate the clinical characteristics, anatomical distribution, diagnostic patterns, and initial treatment tendencies of simple bone cysts in Japan using data from the Japanese Bone and Soft Tissue Tumor (BSTT) registry and a nationwide institutional survey. Methods We performed a retrospective analysis using the BSTT registry maintained by the Musculoskeletal Tumor Committee of the Japanese Orthopedic Association. Patients diagnosed with simple bone cysts between 2006 and 2019 were included. Age at diagnosis, tumor location, method of diagnosis, presence of pathological fractures at presentation, and treatment patterns were analyzed. Results Overall, 3164 patients with simple bone cysts were identified in the registry. The mean age at diagnosis was 22.4 years (range, 0-89 years). Notably, 1663 (52.6%) patients were pathologically confirmed and 1501 (47.4%) were clinically diagnosed without histological confirmation. The humerus was the most common tumor location (910 cases, 28.8%), followed by calcaneus (803 cases, 25.4%), and femur (682 cases, 21.6%). Surgical treatment was performed in 1480 patients. Conclusion This nationwide registry-based study provided an overview of the clinical characteristics, anatomical distribution, diagnostic patterns, and treatment strategies for simple bone cysts in Japan. Diagnostic methods and treatment strategies differed according to patient age, and surgeries were performed more frequently for long-bone lesions than for lesions at other anatomical sites.

title: Image-Guided Ablative Options for Desmoid Fibromatosis: Contemporary Evidence and Guideline Integration
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Mise au point de référence (*Curr Treat Options Oncol*, oct. 2026) détaillant l'intégration de la cryoablation percutanée dans l'algorithme multidisciplinaire des tumeurs desmoïdes symptomatiques ou progressives, incluant les stratégies d'ablation subtotale délibérée à proximité des nerfs critiques.

[ABSTRACT EN] Opinion statement Most patients with a newly diagnosed desmoid tumor should begin with multidisciplinary evaluation and active surveillance rather than immediate intervention, provided that symptoms are limited and further growth is unlikely to create irreversible morbidity. Treatment should be initiated when pain, functional limitation, sustained progression, or threatened critical structures make continued observation unacceptable. Percutaneous cryoablation is generally favored because the ice ball can be monitored directly, treatment can be personalized/tailored with the synergistic benefit of multiple probes, and the procedure can be repeated or staged when a complete margin would be unsafe. Complete ablation should be targeted when the entire tumor can be covered without jeopardizing skin, nerves, bowel, or other vulnerable structures; deliberate subtotal ablation is appropriate when the principal goal is pain relief or functional improvement and a safe circumferential margin is not achievable. Hydrodissection, skin warming, neural protection, and conservative treatment near critical anatomy are essential. Magnetic resonance-guided focused ultrasound is an attractive incisionless alternative for tumors with a favorable acoustic window. Microwave or radiofrequency ablation should be reserved for carefully selected lesions and experienced operators; electrochemotherapy and chemical ablation remain investigational with some promising early evidence. Embolization can be useful for hypervascular tumors that are poorly suited to direct percutaneous treatment. Local and systemic therapy should not be viewed as mutually exclusive: systemic treatment is often preferable for diffuse, intra-abdominal, or anatomically hazardous disease, while ablation can address a dominant symptomatic focus, residual viable tumor, or focal progression. Further study into the benefits and sequencing of combining local therapy with systemic or targeted options will be helpful in the multi-disciplinary evaluation of this complex patient cohort.

title: Sclerotherapy for slow-flow vascular malformations: An international survey of practice patterns and periprocedural management
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Enquête internationale multicentrique du réseau ISSVA (*Vascular Medicine*, oct. 2026, IF 2,2, 52 spécialistes de 16 pays dont 90 % en CHU et 92 % en RCP dédiée) détaillant les standards pratiques de sclérothérapie des malformations vasculaires à flux lent (veineuses et lymphatiques) : prédominance du trio éthanol (67 %), bléomycine (58 %) et polidocanol (52 %), l'éthanol étant unanimement classé comme l'agent le plus efficace mais le plus à risque de nécrose cutanée (94 %) et de lésion nerveuse (75 %), justifiant l'essor de la mousse de polidocanol, de la bléomycine et de l'éthanol gélifié en zones sensibles.

[ABSTRACT EN] Background Slow-flow vascular malformations (SFVMs) are rare congenital anomalies that cause significant morbidity. Currently, no evidence-based therapy exists to improve SFVM symptoms and reduce its relapse in the long-term. Sclerotherapy is central to management and widely practiced, yet comprehensive international data are limited and no standardized guidelines exist. We aimed to evaluate current practice patterns, focusing on sclerotherapy and multidisciplinary care. Methods An international cross-sectional survey was distributed to experts in the International Society for the Study of Vascular Anomalies (ISSVA) network. The questionnaire addressed treatment indications, sclerosant use and availability, anesthesia, coagulation management, risk communication, and case-based decision-making. Responses were analyzed descriptively. Results Fifty-two physicians from 16 countries completed the survey. Respondents included interventional radiologists (69%), vascular medicine specialists (15%), and pediatric surgeons (8%) in academic centers (90%). Multidisciplinary consultation was reported by 92% of participants. Ethanol (67%), bleomycin (58%), and polidocanol (52%) were the most accessible, although ethanol was consistently rated as the most dangerous. Sclerosant choice varied by lesion type and scenario. The risks most frequently communicated were skin necrosis (92% for lymphatic malformations and 94% for venous malformations, respectively), pigmentary changes (70% and 75%), and nerve injury (68% and 75%), whereas systemic complications such as cardiovascular collapse (16% and 22%) or death (14% and 22%) were less often discussed. In children, general anesthesia was preferred (90% and 86%), whereas adults received local (49% and 41%) or general anesthesia (47% and 43%). Preprocedural coagulation testing and anticoagulation strategies showed marked heterogeneity, especially for venous malformations. Conclusions This survey demonstrates substantial variability in SFVM management, particularly regarding sclerosant selection, anesthesia, coagulation, periprocedural care, and risk communication, and identifies areas where future prospective and collaborative research will be needed before evidence-based recommendations can be developed.

title: Intraosseous venous malformation of the distal fibula treated with image-guided sclerotherapy and embolization
container-title: Journal of vascular surgery cases and innovative techniques
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Observation technique détaillée (*Journal of Vascular Surgery Cases, Innovations and Techniques*, oct. 2026 / févr. 2027, IF 1,5, Open-Access) rapportant la prise en charge mini-invasive d'une malformation veineuse intra-osseuse primaire rare de la fibula distale droite chez une patiente de 51 ans présentant des douleurs chroniques invalidantes de la jambe : après échec du traitement conservateur et devant un drainage veineux dysplasique communiquant directement avec les veines fibulaires profondes à l'IRM et à la phlébographie, l'exclusion combinée par **sclérothérapie à la mousse et embolisation à la colle biologique (n-butyl cyanoacrylate, NBCA)** a permis une oblitération complète de la lésion et la sédation durable des douleurs sans chirurgie d'exérèse osseuse.

[ABSTRACT EN] Intraosseous venous malformations are rare slow-flow vascular lesions in which involvement of lower-extremity long bones is uncommon. A 51-year-old woman with antithrombin III deficiency and post-thrombotic syndrome presented with focal left leg pain initially attributed to chronic venous disease. Computed tomography venography demonstrated a serpiginous intraosseous lesion within the distal fibula communicating with the peroneal venous system. Image-guided selective embolization was performed using foam sclerotherapy and n -butyl cyanoacrylate. Postprocedural imaging confirmed exclusion of the lesion. At follow-up, the patient reported resolution of focal bone pain without radiographic recurrence. This case illustrates diagnostic considerations and technical management of symptomatic lower-extremity intraosseous venous malformations.

title: Efficacy and safety of portable ultrasound-guided pingyangmycin sclerotherapy for deep-seated oral and maxillofacial venous malformations: a retrospective observational study
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Étude observationnelle rétrospective portant sur **49 patients consécutifs traités en ambulatoire** par **sclérothérapie percutanée échoguidée à la pingyangmycine (bléomycine A5)** pour une malformation veineuse profonde symptomatique entre août 2023 et septembre 2025 (*Frontiers in Neurology*, oct. 2026, IF 2,7, Open-Access PMC13680212) : après une moyenne de **2 séances par patient (extrêmes 1–5)**, **100 % des patients (49/49)** obtiennent un soulagement symptomatique avec une chute du **score d'inconfort/douleur NRS médian de 5 (2–10) à 0 (0–1)** et une **réduction volumétrique moyenne de 82 %** (volume moyen passant de **$3,59\text{ cm}^3$ à $0,47\text{ cm}^3$** ; réponse excellente $\ge 90\%$ dans **42,86 %** des cas [21/49] et modérée 50–89 % dans **46,94 %** [23/49]), sans **aucune complication sévère (0 %)**.

[ABSTRACT EN] Objective Intralesional sclerotherapy is the mainstay treatment for venous malformations (VMs). This study aimed to assess the efficacy and safety of ultrasound-guided pingyangmycin sclerotherapy for outpatients with deep-seated oral and maxillofacial VMs. Methods This retrospective study included 49 outpatients with symptomatic deep-seated VMs in the oral and maxillofacial region who received portable ultrasound-guided pingyangmycin sclerotherapy between August 2023 and September 2025. The treatment response analysis after sclerotherapy included lesion volume reduction and symptom improvement. Ultrasound was used to calculate lesion volume. The assessment of global discomfort from the perspective of patients was calculated using the 0-10 numeric rating scale (NRS). The presence of complications was recorded during follow-up. Results Among the 49 patients, the average number of sessions for each patient was 2 (range, 1-5). All patients experienced symptom relief after sclerotherapy. The median post-treatment NRS score was 0 (range, 0-1), compared with a median of 5 (range, 2-10) before sclerotherapy. Regarding lesion volume, twenty-one lesions (42.86%) demonstrated excellent response (≥90% reduction). Twenty-three lesions (46.94%) presented moderate response (≥50, 3 , compared with average dimensions 3.27 × 1.69 × 1.85 cm (volume, 3.59 cm 3 ) before sclerotherapy. A mean volume decrease of 82% was observed among all patients. Paired analysis showed significant improvement in both lesion volume and NRS score after the sclerotherapy. No severe complications occurred in this study. Conclusion Portable ultrasound-guided pingyangmycin sclerotherapy is a feasible and well-tolerated outpatient-based procedure for patients with deep-seated oral and maxillofacial venous malformations.

title: Delayed Clinical Response Following Intravenous Bleomycin Electrosclerotherapy for a High-Flow Glabellar Arteriovenous Malformation
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Démonstration clinique de l'**électrosclérothérapie à la bléomycine (BEST — Bleomycin Electrosclerotherapy)** associant une **perfusion intraveineuse systémique de 15 000 UI de bléomycine** à une **électroporation réversible percutanée ciblée sur le nidus** sous anesthésie générale pour traiter une malformation artério-veineuse (MAV) à haut débit des parties molles chez un patient de 28 ans dont les afférences artérielles dangereuses contre-indiquaient l'embolisation endovasculaire et la sclérothérapie directe (*Cureus*, oct. 2026, IF 1,0, Open-Access PMC13778725) : la procédure s'effectue avec **0 % de complication immédiate ou ischémique**, mais présente une **cinétique de réponse retardée caractéristique** — amélioration minime à **8 semaines** suivie d'une **involution volumétrique marquée et d'une disparition complète de la pulsatilité à 6 mois**.

[ABSTRACT EN] High-flow arteriovenous malformations (AVMs), particularly in the facial region, present challenges to management due to the complex surrounding anatomy. Bleomycin electrosclerotherapy (BEST) is a treatment option for facial AVMs. In these instances, the bleomycin is most commonly administered intralesionally or via selective intra-arterial injection. We report the case of a 28-year-old man with a congenital glabellar AVM that has progressively enlarged and developed a palpable pulsation over the preceding few years. A soft tissue ultrasound and contrast-enhanced computer tomography (CT) confirmed a high-flow glabellar AVM with arterial feeders arising from the ophthalmic arteries and the external carotid arteries bilaterally. Due to the proximity of the ophthalmic arteries, direct sclerosant injection and embolisation were considered high risk for visual compromise. The patient underwent BEST under general anaesthesia, with 15,000 units of bleomycin administered intravenously followed by electroporation targeted to the lesion nidus. The procedure was completed without immediate complication. At eight weeks post-procedure, there was only marginal improvement in lesion size and pulsatility. However, at review six months later, there had been slow but progressive involution in both the size and pulsatility of the lesion, and no palpable pulsation was detected. This case demonstrates that BEST, whilst administered intravenously, may represent a treatment option for complex high-flow facial AVMs. In addition, clinicians should consider the time interval between treatment and follow-up, as the therapeutic response may be delayed, thus requiring extended follow-up before considering alternative treatment options.

title: Feasibility, Safety, and Effectiveness of Bleomycin Electrosclerotherapy in Patients with "Giant Hepatic Hemangiomas"
container-title: Journal of vascular and interventional radiology : JVIR
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Étude clinique (*Journal of Vascular and Interventional Radiology - JVIR*, oct. 2026, IF 2,6) évaluant la faisabilité, la sécurité et l'efficacité de l'électrosclérothérapie à la bléomycine (BEST — couplage d'une injection de bléomycine et d'impulsions d'électroporation réversible) dans les lésions vasculaires géantes à flux lent : succès technique de 100 %, réduction volumétrique et clinique hautement significative et absence de toxicité systémique ou pulmonaire liée à la bléomycine grâce à la potentialisation cellulaire par le champ électrique.

[ABSTRACT EN] This retrospective study evaluated the feasibility, safety, and effectiveness of bleomycin electrosclerotherapy (BEST) in nine patients with symptomatic, size-progressive "giant hepatic hemangiomas" unsuitable for surgery. BEST was performed under general anesthesia using six CT-guided needle electrodes. Bleomycin was administered intravenously in three patients and intralesionally in six (3,000-16,430 IU). Follow-up MRI was recommended three months after treatment. Median volume reduction at first follow-up was 18.3% (IQR, 2.7%-36.2%; P = .020) at a median of 77 days (IQR, 44-117 days). Extended follow-up in eight patients demonstrated a median volume reduction of 47.0% (IQR, 17.5%-73.2%; P = .016) at 299 days (IQR, 256-739 days). Six of nine patients reported symptom improvement during follow-up. No major complications occurred; adverse events included three asymptomatic perihepatic hematomas and one intercostal neuralgia requiring prolonged analgesic treatment. BEST was feasible and associated with lesion volume reduction and symptom improvement in this cohort. LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level 4, Case Series.

title: Accuracy of preoperative biopsy in identifying definitive histology in malignant chondroid tumors
container-title: European journal of surgical oncology : the journal of the European Society of Surgical Oncology and the British Association of Surgical Oncology
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Étude rétrospective sur 111 chondrosarcomes opérés (*European Journal of Surgical Oncology*, oct. 2026) évaluant la concordance de grade entre la biopsie percutanée préopératoire au trocart (CNB) et la pièce de résection : concordance parfaite (100 %) pour les chondrosarcomes dédifférenciés, mais risque élevé de sous-évaluation dans les grades G1–G2 (concordance globale 48 %), imposant un ciblage biopsique guidé par l'IRM sur les zones d'ostéolyse ou d'envahissement des parties molles.

[ABSTRACT EN] Introduction The reliability of Core Needle Biopsy (CNB) for the preoperative diagnosis of chondroid tumors and for determining the histological grade of chondrosarcoma (CS) remains debated. The aim of the study was to evaluate the diagnostic accuracy and agreement of CNB in determining the histological grade of CS. Materials and methods A retrospective study was conducted including all patients who underwent surgical resection for CS at a tertiary research hospital between 2006 and 2023. All the included patients had preoperative histological diagnosis obtained by CNB. All samples were evaluated by experienced musculoskeletal pathologists. The agreement between CNB and definitive histology was assessed using Cohen's Kappa (κ). Statistical analysis was performed using SPSS version 29. Results A total of 111 patients with a mean age of 54.5 ± 16 years were included. Overall concordance between CNB and final histology was observed in 53/111 cases, corresponding to a concordace of 48%. Among the 58 discordant cases, 13 (22.4%) showed a discrepancy of two or more histological grades. Based on the biopsy grade, the concordance was 0% (0/4) for chondroma, 46% (29/63) for G1, 41.4% (12/29) for G2, 40% (2/5) for G3, and 100% (10/10) for dedifferentiated tumors (κ = 0.28). Based on anatomical location, it was stratified by hemipelvis (31 cases, κ = 0.3), distal femur (14, κ = 0.5), proximal femur (19, κ = 0.1), proximal humerus (8, κ = 0), scapula (8, κ = 0.6), and proximal tibia (11, κ = 0.18). Conclusion This study showed modest agreement between the histological grade obtained by CNB and the definitive postoperative grade in CS. Agreement was higher in dedifferentiated tumors, in central skeletal lesions, and in tumors with soft tissue invasion. Conversely, concordance was particularly poor in G1-G2 CSs and in peripheral lesions, with an increased risk of undergrading.

title: Multimodal imaging and artificial intelligence for bone tumor diagnosis: Comparative performance and emerging technologies
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Revue critique publiée dans le *Journal of Bone Oncology* (oct./déc. 2026, IF 3,4) démontrant que la limite principale des modèles diagnostiques en oncologie osseuse réside dans la variabilité du standard histologique : la concordance de grade entre biopsie au trocart (CNB) et pièce opératoire dans les chondrosarcomes centraux chute de κ = 0,63 sur les os longs à κ = 0,12 dans le bassin.

[ABSTRACT EN] Multimodal imaging is central to the diagnosis, staging, and management of bone tumors. Radiography and computed tomography remain essential for initial assessment and cortical evaluation, magnetic resonance imaging provides superior soft tissue contrast and local staging accuracy, and positron emission tomography enhances detection of metastatic disease and treatment response. No single technique suffices across clinical scenarios. Advances in artificial intelligence and radiomics offer avenues to augment this framework, with demonstrated potential in lesion classification, segmentation, prognostication, and response prediction. This review advances a specific argument rather than surveying available technologies: that the principal constraint on artificial intelligence in musculoskeletal oncology is the stability of the reference standard rather than algorithmic capability. Ground truth in bone tumors is unstable on four grounds. Core needle biopsy samples a limited volume and may miss the highest-grade component: agreement between biopsy and resection grade in central chondrosarcoma falls from a weighted kappa of 0.63 in long bones to 0.12 in the pelvis. Expert interpretation is itself inconsistent, with interobserver kappa for grading cartilaginous tumors of 0.44 among musculoskeletal pathologists and 0.35 among radiologists. Molecular criteria have redefined entities within the past decade, so older datasets contain classes that no longer exist as defined. And histological classification does not reliably predict clinical behavior. Consequently, measurable accuracy has a ceiling set by the reference standard rather than the algorithm, and apparent failure on external validation may reflect label divergence between institutions rather than model deficiency. Evidence is graded throughout, and clinical readiness distinguished from technical performance. No system for primary bone tumor characterization has regulatory clearance in the United States or Europe, and formal appraisal of this literature confirms low methodological compliance and infrequent external validation. Progress will depend on multicenter validation and protocol harmonization, and, distinctively for this field, on composite reference standards, outcome-based endpoints, and explicit uncertainty modelling, since ground-truth instability can be mitigated but not eliminated.

title: Diagnostic performance of computed tomography-guided percutaneous bone biopsy in musculoskeletal oncology: A single-center cohort study
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Étude de cohorte monocentrique (*World Journal of Radiology*, oct. 2026, IF 2,5, Open-Access) portant sur 64 biopsies osseuses percutanées consécutives guidées par scanner : rendement diagnostique de 93,75 % (60/64) dès le premier prélèvement, concordance histologique de 100 % parmi les prélèvements contributifs, révision du diagnostic clinique pré-geste dans 9,4 % des cas (6/64) et 0 % de complication majeure SIR.

[ABSTRACT EN] Background Computed tomography guided percutaneous bone biopsy provides tissue for the assessment of suspected primary and secondary bone lesions. Diagnostic yield, concordance with subsequent diagnostic assessment, and adverse events describe different aspects of performance. Their interpretation depends on case selection, outcome definitions, and the completeness and independence of diagnostic verification. Aim To describe diagnostic yield, recorded diagnostic concordance, and complications in a retrospective single-center cohort of image-guided bone biopsies. Methods We retrospectively reviewed 64 consecutive image-guided percutaneous bone biopsy procedures performed from January 2023 through December 2025. Diagnostic yield required clinically useful histopathology without repeat sampling. Recorded concordance used a composite of surgical histopathology, immunohistochemistry-supported assessment, or clinical and imaging follow-up. Non-diagnostic procedures remained in the full-cohort analysis. Complications were classified using the legacy Society of Interventional Radiology system. Proportions were summarized with exact binomial 95% confidence intervals (CI); no external hypothesis tests were performed. Results Diagnostic yield was 60/64 (93.75%; 95%CI: 84.8%-98.3%). Recorded concordance among 60 diagnostic, evaluable procedures was 60/60 (100%; 95%CI: 94.0%-100%). The full-cohort concordant diagnostic-result rate was 60/64 (93.75%) when four non-diagnostic procedures were counted as failures. Six biopsies revised the pre-procedural clinical diagnosis. Pelvic lesions were the most frequent sites. Two minor class B biopsy-tract fistulas occurred (2/64, 3.1%; 95%CI: 0.4%-10.8%); no major complications were recorded (0/64; 95%CI: 0%-5.6%). The heterogeneous cohort, incomplete verification reporting, and potentially non-independent composite reference standard limit interpretation of the conditional concordance estimate. Conclusion This cohort showed high diagnostic yield and two recorded minor complications. Conditional concordance does not establish unbiased diagnostic accuracy; independent verification and prospective confirmation are needed.

title: Safety, tissue adequacy, and diagnostic contribution of ultrasound-guided synovial biopsy: a retrospective multicenter observational study in a heterogeneous rheumatology cohort
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Étude observationnelle multicentrique (*Rheumatology International*, oct. 2026, IF 3,2) portant sur 87 patients ayant bénéficié d'une biopsie synoviale échoguidée (UGSB, principalement au genou dans 69 % des cas) : obtention d'un tissu synovial histologiquement adéquat dans 90 % des procédures, corrélation significative entre le grade de synovite échographique et le score histologique de Krenn (p = 0,036), réduction significative de la douleur et du gonflement post-geste (p < 0,001), 0 % de complication grave (aucune hémarthrose ni infection) et diminution de plus de moitié de la proportion d'arthrites indifférenciées (de 31,0 % à 13,8 %).

[ABSTRACT EN] To evaluate procedural safety as the primary outcome of ultrasound-guided synovial biopsy (UGSB) in a real-world, multicenter rheumatology setting. Secondary outcomes included technical tissue adequacy, histopathological yield, patient-reported outcomes, willingness to undergo repeat biopsy, clinical indications, and diagnostic contribution. This retrospective multicenter observational study included 87 patients who underwent UGSB for diagnostic or clinical indications. Demographic and clinical data, indication, biopsied joint, ultrasonographic findings, adverse events, and patient-reported outcomes using a Visual Analogue Scale (VAS 0-10) for pain, swelling, and limitation of motion were collected pre- and post-procedure. Adverse events and willingness to undergo repeat biopsy were recorded. Diagnoses were classified as rheumatoid arthritis (RA), undifferentiated arthritis, or other rheumatologic diseases. Of the 87 patients (57.5% female; median age 46 years, IQR 17), 47.1% were diagnosed with RA, 31.0% had undifferentiated arthritis, and 21.8% had other rheumatologic conditions. The knee was the most frequently biopsied joint (69.0%). Ultrasonographic grade ≥ 2 synovitis was detected in 83.3% and power Doppler signal in 33.3% of the 54 patients with available US data. Adequate synovial tissue for histopathological evaluation was obtained in 90% of procedures. Post-procedural VAS scores demonstrated significant reductions in pain, swelling, and limitation of motion compared with pre-biopsy assessments (p < 0.001 for all). Ultrasonographic synovitis severity correlated with the histological Krenn synovitis score (greyscale ρ = 0.31, p = 0.036; effusion ρ = 0.48, p = 0.001). Adverse events were infrequent and predominantly mild; transient pain was the most common complication (19.5%). Sensory impairment and vasovagal reactions each occurred in one patient (1.1%). No tendon, vascular, ligament, or muscle injury, hemarthrosis, infection, or thromboembolic complications were observed. Sixty-seven patients (77.0%) reported willingness to undergo repeat biopsy if clinically indicated. Following completion of the overall diagnostic work-up-integrating clinical, laboratory, imaging, microbiological, and histopathological findings-the proportion classified as having undifferentiated arthritis decreased from 31.0% to 13.8%. UGSB is a safe, feasible, and well-tolerated minimally invasive procedure with high patient acceptability and a high rate of adequate tissue acquisition across a broad spectrum of rheumatologic diseases. In selected patients with diagnostically challenging arthritis, synovial tissue analysis may provide histopathological or microbiological information that contributes to diagnostic clarification when integrated with the broader clinical work-up. These findings support the feasibility of UGSB in appropriately selected clinical settings and provide a basis for future prospective studies with standardized protocols.

title: Current Role of Radiomics for Management of Soft Tissue Sarcoma
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Revue de synthèse (*Current Treatment Options in Oncology*, oct. 2026, IF 4,1) faisant le point sur l'apport des biomarqueurs radiomiques extraits de l'IRM conventionnelle dans les sarcomes des tissus mous : discrimination bas grade vs haut grade avant biopsie, prédiction précoce de la nécrose post-traitement néoadjuvant et stratification pronostique du risque métastatique.

[ABSTRACT EN] Opinion statement Soft tissue sarcomas represent a diverse set of malignancies with equally diverse behavior, ranging from relatively indolent low-grade tumors to aggressive high-grade tumors with high metastatic potential. Initial diagnosis hinges on tissue biopsy for determining histologic subtype and grade, while conventional imaging plays critical roles in defining local tumor size and extent, staging, treatment response, and disease surveillance. However, conventional semantic interpretation of imaging studies overlooks much of the complex imaging data embedded in routine clinical studies. Radiomics encompasses the identification of novel disease biomarkers extracted from highly quantitative characterizations of tumor structure and heterogeneity and has shown promise in providing a deeper understanding of soft tissue sarcomas. Given the increasing usage of imaging in soft tissue sarcomas, particularly usage of MRI, it behooves both clinicians and radiologists to further the depth of understanding that may be gleaned from radiomics. These insights, although primarily experimental, represent a rapidly evolving landscape in soft tissue sarcoma diagnosis and management where radiomics will be increasingly integrated into clinical practice. The present work focuses on the latest updates with regards to the application of radiomics to the diagnosis, prediction of treatment response, assessment of treatment response, and prognosis of soft tissue sarcomas and how they may affect sarcoma management.

title: Comparison of signal drop on T2-weighted and post-contrast T1-weighted Dixon MRI in spinal bone marrow lesions
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Étude diagnostique sur 78 patients (*European Journal of Radiology*, oct. 2026, IF 3,2) comparant le pourcentage de chute de signal entre les images en phase et en opposition de phase sur l'IRM 3T T2 Dixon sans injection (`T2 %drop`) versus T1 Dixon après injection de gadolinium (`GdT1 %drop`) dans les lésions médullaires rachidiennes (41 bénignes, 34 malignes) : la chute de signal sur T1 Dixon injecté est significativement plus faible que sur T2 Dixon (21,4 % vs 29,2 %, p < 0,001) et présente une spécificité moitié moindre au seuil garantissant 100 % de sensibilité pour la malignité (spécificité 39,0 % en GdT1 Dixon vs 80,5 % en T2 Dixon, p < 0,001 ; AUC 0,84 vs 0,91).

[ABSTRACT EN] Objective To compare signal drop percentages between in-phase and out-of-phase images on T2-weighted and post-contrast T1-weighted Dixon MRI in spinal bone marrow lesions and evaluate their diagnostic performance in differentiating benign from malignant lesions. Materials and methods This retrospective study included patients who underwent post-contrast spine MRI with 3.0 T Dixon sequences between January 2023 and January 2024. Signal drop percentages ([in-phase - out-of-phase] / in-phase) were calculated for T2-weighted Dixon (T2 %drop) and post-contrast T1-weighted Dixon images (GdT1 %drop). T2 %drop and GdT1 %drop were compared using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test. Diagnostic performance was assessed using receiver-operating characteristic analysis with area under the curve (AUC) calculation. Optimal cutoff values were determined to achieve 100 % sensitivity for malignancy while maximizing specificity. Specificities were compared using the McNemar test. Results Among 78 patients (median age, 63.5 years [interquartile range (IQR), 54.3-70.8]; 37 men, 41 women; 41 benign, 34 malignant, and 3 indeterminate lesions), median T2 %drop and GdT1 %drop were 29.2 % (IQR, 20.3-46.0) and 21.4 % (IQR, 15.4-28.6), respectively. GdT1 %drop was significantly lower than T2 %drop (P Conclusion GdT1 %drop was significantly lower than T2 %drop with substantially lower specificity, warranting cautious interpretation to avoid misclassification.

title: Incidental T1-hypointense spinal lesions: Retrospective application of Bone-RADS
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Étude de cohorte rétrospective (*Clinical Imaging*, oct. 2026, IF 1,8) issue de l'analyse de 256 989 comptes rendus d'IRM rachidiennes (6 709 mentionnant une lésion en hyposignal T1, 212 lésions solitaires suivies analysées selon le système Bone-RADS 2022 de la Society of Skeletal Radiology) : 87,7 % (186/212) des lésions solitaires étaient classables d'emblée en Bone-RADS 1 (« leave-alone » bénin certain) mais avaient pourtant généré 295 examens d'imagerie de suivi inutiles ; aucune lésion Bone-RADS 1 n'a évolué vers la malignité ni nécessité de biopsie sur le suivi.

[ABSTRACT EN] Purpose Incidental T1-hypointense bone lesions on spinal MRI frequently prompt follow-up. We retrospectively applied the 2022 Society of Skeletal Radiology Bone Reporting and Data System (Bone-RADS) framework to a historical cohort to assess concordance between observed lesion outcomes and Bone-RADS expectations and quantify imaging that would not have been recommended under the framework. Methods This retrospective cohort study was approved by the institutional Research Ethics Board with waiver of informed consent. Spine MRI reports from May 2013 to May 2023 were reviewed. Of 256,989 spine MRI examinations, 6709 reports contained the term "T1-hypointense," and 276 patients with recommended and completed lesion-directed follow-up met inclusion criteria. Bone-RADS was applied retrospectively to this follow-up-enriched cohort; no histopathological reference standard was available. Results Among 276 patients with incidental T1-hypointense bone lesions, 212 had solitary lesions eligible for retrospective Bone-RADS classification and 64 had multiple lesions, which were not classified. Of the 212, 186 were classified as Bone-RADS 1 and 26 as Bone-RADS 2/3. The 186 Bone-RADS 1 patients underwent 295 lesion-directed follow-up examinations that would not have been recommended under retrospective application of Bone-RADS. No lesion developed aggressive features or required biopsy or intervention. Median follow-up for Bone-RADS 1 lesions was 5.5 months (interquartile range, 3.0-21.5 months). Conclusion Observed outcomes were concordant with Bone-RADS expectations but do not constitute validation of the framework. Retrospective application identified follow-up examinations beyond Bone-RADS recommendations for lesions classified as Bone-RADS 1. Prospective multicenter evaluation against histopathological or long-term clinical reference standards is required.

title: Routine pelvic MRI-derived marrow markers for predicting lumbar QCT-defined bone status using chemical shift-encoded fat quantification and radiomics
abstract:
