[SYNTHÈSE FR] Étude prospective sur 123 patients oncologiques (*European Journal of Radiology*, oct. 2026, IF 3,2) corrélant les biomarqueurs médullaires extraits de l'IRM pelvienne de surveillance (fraction graisseuse en densité de protons PDFF et relaxométrie R2* sur séquence Dixon multi-écho IDEAL-IQ au col fémoral, à la tête fémorale et à l'ilion, ainsi que la radiomique T1) à la densité minérale osseuse volumique (vBMD T12–L2) mesurée par QCT : augmentation significative de la PDFF médullaire et baisse du R2* avec la dégradation de la densité osseuse sur tous les sites (p < 0,05), excellente reproductibilité inter-lecteurs (ICC = 0,903–0,996) et bonne capacité discriminante pour identifier l'ostéoporose (AUC = 0,73–0,78) sans examen irradiant supplémentaire.

[ABSTRACT EN] Objectives To evaluate whether pelvic MRI-derived IDEAL-IQ parameters and T1-weighted radiomics can predict lumbar QCT-defined bone status in cancer survivors undergoing routine pelvic oncologic MRI. Materials & methods This secondary analysis within a prospective surveillance cohort included 123 patients with pelvic malignancies who underwent MRI (with IDEAL-IQ) and lumbar QCT within three months. QCT-derived volumetric BMD at T12-L2 served as the reference standard to classify subjects as normal, osteopenia, or osteoporotic. Pelvic MRI-derived PDFF and R2* were measured at the femoral head, femoral neck, and ilium; a radiomics pipeline was built on T1-weighted images. Inter-reader reliability used absolute-agreement intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs). Discrimination was evaluated with one-vs-rest ROC analysis, and clinical utility was assessed by decision-curve analysis using out-of-fold probabilities from five-fold internal validation for two decisions: osteoporosis versus non-osteoporosis and low bone mass versus normal bone status. Results PDFF increased and R2* decreased with worsening BMD at all sites (P Conclusion Pelvic MRI-derived IDEAL-IQ and radiomics markers showed modest and comparable performance for predicting lumbar QCT-defined bone status. Their discrimination was mainly driven by separation between normal bone status and osteoporosis, whereas osteopenia remained poorly distinguished. These findings support exploratory opportunistic risk flagging rather than complete three-class risk stratification.

title: Quantitative assessment of vertebral bone marrow adipose tissue using photon-counting CT compared with MRI
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Étude prospective comparative (*European Journal of Radiology*, oct./déc. 2026, IF 3,2) portant sur 73 patients (339 corps vertébraux analysés) ayant bénéficié à la fois d'un scanner lombaire à comptage photonique (PCCT) et d'une IRM quantitative 6-échos q-Dixon (mesurant la fraction graisseuse en densité de protons PDFF de référence) : la fraction graisseuse dérivée des cartes virtuelles sans calcium du scanner à comptage photonique (**VNCa CTFF**) présente une très forte corrélation positive avec la PDFF IRM tant à l'échelle vertébrale ($r = 0,863$) qu'à l'échelle du patient ($r = 0,895$), tandis que les valeurs d'atténuation VNCa en UH montrent une forte corrélation négative ($r = -0,858$ à $-0,888$).

[ABSTRACT EN] Rationale and objectives To evaluate the feasibility and accuracy of photon-counting CT (PCCT)-derived parameters for quantifying vertebral bone marrow adipose tissue (BMAT), using MRI proton density fat fraction (PDFF) as the reference standard. Materials and methods Adult participants with low back pain were prospectively recruited to undergo both PCCT and MRI. PCCT-derived parameters, including virtual non-calcium (VNCa) CT values, VNCa CT fat fraction (CTFF), and standardized 70 keV CT values, were obtained. MRI PDFF maps were generated using a 6-echo q-Dixon sequence. Correlation and agreement between PCCT-derived parameters and MRI PDFF were assessed at both vertebral and subject levels. Results A total of 73 participants were included, and 339 vertebral bodies were analyzed. VNCa CTFF showed strong positive correlation with MRI PDFF at both vertebral (r = 0.863) and subject (r = 0.895) levels. In contrast, VNCa CT values (r = -0.858 to -0.888) and standardized 70 keV CT values (r = -0.791 to -0.833) showed significant negative correlations with MRI PDFF. Bland-Altman plots showed small mean differences but relatively wide limits of agreement between calibrated VNCa CTFF and MRI PDFF. Conclusions PCCT-derived VNCa CTFF showed strong correlation with MRI PDFF, and linear calibration reduced the mean difference between the two measurements, although the limits of agreement remained relatively wide. Standardized 70 keV CT values were also correlated with MRI PDFF, but should be interpreted cautiously as attenuation-based surrogates influenced by both trabecular mineral content and marrow fat.

title: Dual-energy CT virtual non-calcium imaging for differentiating pathologic from non-pathologic femoral fractures: a study of inexperienced non-radiologist readers
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Étude rétrospective de performance diagnostique sur **45 fractures fémorales consécutives** admises aux urgences (**20 fractures pathologiques prouvées par histologie/chirurgie et 25 fractures non pathologiques**, *Skeletal Radiology*, sept./déc. 2026, IF 1,9) : l'ajout des **cartes couleur DECT Virtual Non-Calcium (VNCa)** au scanner conventionnel fait bondir la **sensibilité de détection des fractures pathologiques de 65 % à 95 % ($p = 0,031$, lecteur 1) et de 50 % à 85 % ($p = 0,016$, lecteur 2)**, augmente la précision globale à **91,1–95,6 %** et élève l'**AUC de 0,765 à 0,955 ($p = 0,0135$)** et de **0,670 à 0,905 ($p < 0,01$)** chez des lecteurs non spécialisés.

[ABSTRACT EN] Objective To assess the effect of dual-energy CT (DECT) virtual non-calcium (VNCa) imaging on the ability of inexperienced non-radiologist readers to differentiate pathologic from non-pathologic femoral fractures. Materials and methods In this retrospective diagnostic accuracy study, 45 eligible emergency department patients with femoral fractures who underwent DECT between January 2022 and September 2024 were included, comprising 20 patients with pathologic fractures and 25 with non-pathologic fractures. The reference standard for fracture classification was established using surgical records or histopathologic results. Two inexperienced non-radiologist readers independently evaluated conventional CT alone and conventional CT combined with color-coded DECT VNCa images in separate reading sessions. Sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) were compared between the two sessions. AUCs were compared using the paired DeLong test. Results The addition of DECT VNCa significantly improved sensitivity for detecting pathologic fractures in both readers. For Reader 1, sensitivity increased from 65 to 95% (p = 0.031), and accuracy increased from 77.8% to 95.6%. For Reader 2, sensitivity increased from 50 to 85% (p = 0.016), and accuracy increased from 68.9% to 91.1%. Specificity remained high without significant differences between sessions. AUC increased from 0.765 (95% CI, 0.617-0.913) to 0.955 (95% CI, 0.883-1.0) for Reader 1 and from 0.670 (95% CI, 0.506-0.834) to 0.905 (95% CI, 0.802-1.0) for Reader 2 (p = 0.0135 and Conclusion Adding color-coded DECT VNCa to conventional CT improves the diagnostic performance of inexperienced non-radiologist readers in detecting pathologic femoral fractures.

title: Regional variation in vertebral bone marrow adiposity: a population-based atlas of age- and sex-specific patterns
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Étude de référence en population générale analysant les IRM Dixon du rachis avec segmentation corporéale automatisée voxel-à-voxel chez **81 318 participants** de la cohorte **UK Biobank** (âge moyen $54,8 \pm 7,6\text{ ans}$, 51,8 % de femmes) (*Skeletal Radiology*, oct. 2026, IF 1,9) : la **fraction graisseuse médullaire osseuse (BMFF)** suit une distribution cranio-caudale **non linéaire** très structurée — **~39 % au rachis cervical, ~55 % au rachis thoracique, ~45 % au rachis lombaire et ~70 % au sacrum** —, augmente significativement avec l'âge dans tous les étages (**$+3,33\%$ par décennie en cervical, $+3,41\%$ en thoracique, $+2,95\%$ en lombaire et $+3,83\%$ au sacrum**, tous $p < 0,001$), et s'avère significativement plus élevée chez la femme que chez l'homme à tous les niveaux dans cette tranche d'âge ($p < 0,001$).

[ABSTRACT EN] Bone marrow adipose tissue (BMAT) is a metabolically active fat depot implicated in skeletal aging and systemic metabolism. While chemical shift-encoding MRI enables noninvasive quantification of bone marrow fat fraction (BMFF), current knowledge of vertebral BMAT is largely limited to small cohorts or restricted anatomical regions. To characterize the spatial distribution of vertebral bone marrow fat fraction across the spine and determine region-specific associations with age and sex in a population-based cohort. In this retrospective study, MRI data from 82,920 UK Biobank participants recruited between 2006 and 2010 were analyzed. The baseline case subset (n = 81,318) had a mean age of 54.8 ± 7.6 years, and 42,113/81,318 (51.8%) were female. Automated vertebral body segmentation enabled voxel-wise BMFF quantification using Dixon MRI. Vertebra- and region-level BMFF metrics were derived. Associations with age and sex were assessed using region-specific linear regression. Vertebral BMAT demonstrated a non-linear cranio-caudal pattern. Mean BMFF was ~ 39% in the cervical, ~ 55% in the thoracic, ~ 45% in the lumbar spine, and ~ 70% in the sacrum. BMAT increased with age in all regions (all p < 0.001; increase per decade: cervical 3.33%, thoracic 3.41%, lumbar 2.95%, sacral 3.83%). Females exhibited higher BMFF than males across all regions (all p < 0.001). The overall spatial pattern remained consistent across age groups and sexes. Vertebral BMAT exhibits a structured, non-linear spatial distribution with region-specific age- and sex-dependent patterns. This population-based atlas provides normative reference data supporting region-specific BMAT assessment in skeletal and metabolic disease.

title: Deep learning-based synthetic CT for the assessment of spinal structural lesions in axial spondyloarthritis
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Étude rétrospective de validation diagnostique à double lecture indépendante portant sur **87 patients** (âge moyen $41 \pm 14,2\text{ ans}$, 42 hommes et 45 femmes) explorés pour rachialgies inflammatoires par **IRM rachidienne avec génération de scanner synthétique par Deep Learning (synthetic CT / sCT)** comparée au **scanner rachidien conventionnel de référence** (*Skeletal Radiology*, oct. 2026, IF 1,9) : le **scanner synthétique (sCT)** atteint une **sensibilité de 100 % (1,00)** pour la détection de l'**ankylose facettaire articulaire postérieure**, des **lésions destructrices d'Andersson**, de l'**ankylose vertébrale** et des **érosions osseuses**, ainsi que de **91 % (0,91) pour les syndesmophytes** et **67 % (0,67) pour les ossifications discales**, avec une **spécificité comprise entre 97 % et 100 % (0,97–1,00)** sur tous les types lésionnels et une mesure millimétrique des érosions strictement superposable au vrai scanner (largeur médiane $8,0\text{ vs }7,7\text{ mm}$, $p = 0,15$ ; profondeur $4,5\text{ vs }4,5\text{ mm}$, $p = 0,12$).

[ABSTRACT EN] Objective To evaluate the accuracy of synthetic CT for detecting spinal structural lesions in patients with suspected axial spondyloarthritis (axSpA). Materials and methods Patients with inflammatory back pain who underwent both spinal CT and MRI examinations were included in this retrospective study. Two readers independently assessed the presence of structural lesions (facet joint ankylosis, structural Andersson lesions, discal ossifications, vertebral ankylosis, syndesmophytes, and erosions) on conventional CT and synthetic CT images. Feature detection accuracy of synthetic CT relative to conventional CT was evaluated using sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, and negative predictive value, with consensus reading as the reference standard. In addition, lesion-level erosion detection accuracy was assessed, and erosion size was compared between conventional CT and synthetic CT. Results Eighty-seven patients (mean age, 41 ± 14.2 years; range, 18-80 years; 42 males and 45 females) were included. Sensitivity of synthetic CT was 1.00 for facet joint ankylosis, structural Andersson lesions, vertebral ankylosis, and erosions, 0.91 for syndesmophytes, and 0.67 for discal ossifications. Specificity ranged from 0.97 to 1.00 across all lesion types. Lesion-level analysis showed sensitivity of 0.82-1.00 and specificity of 0.96-1.00 for erosion detection across different spinal regions. No significant differences of erosion size (median [IQR], mm) between conventional CT and synthetic CT (width, 7.7 [4.4-9.7] vs. 8.0 [4.1-9.6], P = 0.15; depth, 4.5 [3.5-6.7] vs. 4.5 [3.5-6.5], P = 0.12). Conclusion Synthetic CT demonstrates a high feature detection accuracy for assessing most spinal structural lesions in patients with suspected axSpA.

title: Clinical evaluation of deep learning-based acquisition and reconstruction techniques for accelerated 2D shoulder magnetic resonance imaging acceleration at 3 T
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Étude prospective intra-individuelle en aveugle évaluant la nouvelle technologie d'accélération et de reconstruction par apprentissage profond **Sonic DL** comparée au protocole clinique standard **AIR Recon DL** en **IRM 2D de l'épaule à 3 Tesla** chez **30 patients ambulatoires consécutifs**, lue indépendamment par **3 radiologues ostéo-articulaires seniors** (*Skeletal Radiology*, sept. 2026 / janv. 2027, IF 1,9) : **Sonic DL réduit de 38,7 % le temps d'acquisition nominal** (**$6\text{ min }15\text{ s}$ contre $10\text{ min }12\text{ s}$** au-delà du gain déjà apporté par AIR Recon DL) avec une **qualité d'image globale, une netteté, un rapport signal/bruit ($p = 0,171\text{--}0,861$) et une concordance inter-lecteurs similaires** ($0,839$ vs $0,867$), mais une **visibilité légèrement moindre de certaines bursites sous-acromio-deltoïdiennes ($p = 0,049$) et ruptures partielles du supra-épineux ($p = 0,006$)** incitant à la prudence sur les facteurs d'accélération extrêmes.

[ABSTRACT EN] Purpose GE has recently developed Sonic DL MRI acceleration technology. We wished to (1) quantify scanner time reduction compared to the AIR Recon DL already in clinical use at our institution and (2) preliminarily evaluate any change in diagnostic findings between these methods. Methods A total of 30 outpatients undergoing routine shoulder MRI for shoulder pain were recruited. Each underwent routine AIR Recon DL and Sonic DL exams containing the same sequences. Three subspecialized musculoskeletal radiologists assessed image quality, graded pathology, and reported diagnostic confidence in a blinded fashion. Differences in image quality and confidence were compared using Wilcoxon signed-rank tests. Results Sonic DL reduced nominal acquisition time 38.7% compared to AIR Recon DL (6 min 15 s versus 10 min 12 s). Artifact was considered slightly worse on the routine examination (3.20 versus 3.37, P = 0.039); there was no significant difference in image quality, sharpness, or signal-to-noise ratio between routine and Sonic DL accelerated exams (P 0.171-0.861). Inter-reader agreement was broadly similar between routine-routine and routine-Sonic DL comparisons (median agreement 0.867 and 0.839, respectively). Within-reader analysis identified subacromial/subdeltoid bursitis and supraspinatus tendon tears more frequently on the routine protocol than on Sonic DL (P 0.049 and P 0.006, respectively). Conclusion Sonic DL enabled a 38.7% reduction in nominal shoulder MRI acquisition time with broadly comparable image quality and inter-reader agreement in this pilot cohort. Diagnostic equivalence was not established; subacromial/subdeltoid bursitis and supraspinatus tears were potentially less conspicuous on Sonic DL. A larger powered validation study would be needed to fully evaluate diagnostic performance.

title: Intraoperative Neurophysiological Monitoring During Continuous Radiofrequency Treatment of Morton's Neuroma: Complete Ablation
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Série prospective de 22 patients / 30 névromes de Morton (*Medicina*, oct. 2026) traités par radiofréquence continue échoguidée sous monitorage en temps réel des potentiels d'action nerveux sensitifs (SNAP), obtenant 86,7 % de succès global (96,3 % hors métatarsalgie mécanique) et 100 % de succès en rattrapage après échec d'une RF antérieure.

[ABSTRACT EN] Background and Objectives : Morton's neuroma is a compressive neuropathy of the common plantar digital nerve that most frequently affects the third intermetatarsal space. Continuous radiofrequency (RF) ablation has reported success rates of approximately 80-85%; however, recent histological evidence suggests that RF does not consistently achieve complete neural ablation. This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of intraoperative neurophysiological monitoring of sensory nerve action potentials (SNAPs) to optimize the outcomes of continuous RF ablation in the treatment of Morton's neuroma. Materials and Methods : This prospective case series included 22 patients (30 neuromas) treated with ultrasound-guided continuous RF ablation combined with intraoperative neurophysiological monitoring. SNAPs were recorded before, during, and after each RF application until complete abolition of sensory nerve conduction was confirmed. Clinical outcomes were assessed using the Visual Analog Scale (VAS), the Foot Function Index (FFI), and the Giannini Interdigital Neuroma Clinical Evaluation Score at 3, 6, and 12 months postoperatively. Results : At the 12-month follow-up, satisfactory outcomes (Giannini score ≥60) were achieved in 86.7% of neuromas (26/30). The mean VAS pain score decreased from 8.67 preoperatively to 1.67 at 12 months. Among the seven neuromas with previous unsuccessful RF treatment, all achieved satisfactory outcomes following the monitored procedure. The four cases with poor outcomes were predominantly associated with a positive anesthetic suppression test, suggesting concomitant mechanical metatarsalgia rather than treatment failure. After excluding cases with likely diagnostic misclassification, the adjusted success rate increased to 96.3%. Conclusions : Intraoperative neurophysiological monitoring enables real-time confirmation of complete sensory nerve ablation during continuous RF treatment. Its main potential value appears to lie in patients with previous unsuccessful conventional RF, all of whom achieved satisfactory outcomes in this series. Persistent postoperative symptoms appeared to be more closely related to concomitant forefoot pathology than to technical limitations of the RF procedure.

title: Navigating current controversies in radiofrequency ablation of the genicular nerves for chronic knee pain in osteoarthritis: a daring discourse
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Mise au point critique de référence (*Regional Anesthesia and Pain Medicine*, oct. 2026, IF 5,1) analysant les 6 controverses expliquant les résultats discordants des essais randomisés sur la radiofréquence des nerfs géniculés : (1) valeur pronostique des blocs tests préalables, (2) positionnement optimal des canules sur les cibles classiques, (3) nombre de branches nerveuses à cibler (au-delà de la triade classique SMGN/SLGN/IMGN), (4) avantages comparés du guidage échographique, fluoroscopique ou combiné, (5) place de la radiofréquence pulsée (PRF), et (6) indications après prothèse totale de genou (PTG).

[ABSTRACT EN] Chronic knee joint pain affects millions worldwide, with radiofrequency ablation (RFA) of genicular nerves emerging as a potential treatment in the last 15 years. Despite its growing popularity, with studies demonstrating its efficacy in pain reduction for up to 12 months, recent randomized controlled trials have questioned the efficacy of RFA. Discrepancies in study results may partially be explained by the heterogeneity of patient selection and technical protocols.This daring discourse aims to explore and critically analyze the ongoing debates surrounding RFA of the genicular nerves, addressing key controversies, namely: (1) Is there a role for performing prognostic blocks prior to RFA?; (2) What are the optimal target sites for final cannulae placement for the classical targets?; (3) Which and how many nerves should be targeted in RFA procedures?; (4) What are the comparative benefits of using ultrasound versus fluoroscopy guidance, and whether a combined technique may be advantageous?; (5) Is there a potential role for pulsed radiofrequency of the genicular nerves?; (6) Should genicular nerve RFA be performed after total knee arthroplasty?Through this in-depth discussion, we aim to guide pain medicine clinicians in informed decision-making and encourage further research in this field.

title: Post-procedure MRI lesion size after 7-min basivertebral nerve ablation
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Étude d'imagerie post-procédurale (*Interventional Pain Medicine*, oct./déc. 2026, IF 1,8, Open-Access) mesurant par deux lecteurs indépendants sur l'IRM sagittale la taille réelle de la zone de nécrose thermique après ablation par radiofréquence du nerf basivertébral (BVNA) réalisée selon le nouveau protocole raccourci de **7 minutes** : hauteur lésionnelle moyenne de **11,6 ± 1,2 mm** et largeur moyenne de **10,9 ± 1,4 mm** (soit ~1,1 cm de diamètre), strictement superposable au diamètre sphérique de 1,0 cm historiquement obtenu avec le protocole de 15 minutes.

[ABSTRACT EN] Background Chronic vertebrogenic low back pain can be successfully treated with basivertebral nerve ablation (BVNA). Initial studies reported the effectiveness of BVNA using a 15-min ablation protocol. Recently, industry has sponsored adopting 7-min ablations for appropriately placed probes. The effectiveness of 7-min ablations has been called into question. For 15-min ablations, lesion size has been reported to be approximately 1 cm in diameter. There are no literature reporting lesion sizes for 7-min ablations. Objective The purpose of this study was to evaluate MRI lesion size for patients who underwent 7-min BVNA. Methods A retrospective cohort study was conducted of patients who underwent BVNA and had post-procedure MRI available for review. All MRIs were obtained for patients who failed to improve after BVNA or developed new symptoms. On the sagittal post-procedure MRI, the BVNA lesion height and width size were measured by two independent reviewers. Interobserver reproducibility was assessed using intraclass correlations and Bland-Altmann analysis. The average height and width of the lesion was calculated with standard deviations. Results A total of 10 out of 57 patients who underwent BVNA during the study timeframe had post-procedure MRI. There was acceptable reproducibility between MRI reviewers. The average lesion height size was 11.6 mm (±1.2 mm), and the average width was 10.9 mm (±1.4 mm). Conclusions Our study demonstrated that patients who received an MRI due to treatment failure or new symptoms after treatment with 7-min BVNA had average height and width lesion sizes of approximately 1.1 cm. This is within range of the lesion size of historically accepted 15-min BVNA lesion sizes.

title: Clinical Outcomes of Conventional Versus Lateral-Deployment RF Cannulas in Lumbar Medial Branch Radiofrequency Ablation: A Prospective Randomized Study
container-title: American journal of physical medicine & rehabilitation
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Essai prospectif randomisé contrôlé en simple aveugle de supériorité sur **90 patients** (84 analysés à 6 mois, 42 par bras) atteints de lombalgie facettaire chronique confirmée par double bloc test positif ($\ge 80\%$) (*American Journal of Physical Medicine & Rehabilitation*, oct. 2026, IF 2,2), comparant les **canules de radiofréquence à déploiement latéral multi-ailettes (lateral-deployment RF cannulas)** aux canules monopolaires conventionnelles (80 °C pendant 90 s) : à 6 mois, la canule à déploiement latéral permet une **réduction deux fois plus importante de la douleur NRS ($-5,52 \pm 2,61$ vs $-2,81 \pm 2,84$, différence ajustée $-2,795$, $p < 0,001$)**, double quasiment le **taux de répondeurs $\ge 50\%$ (73,8 % vs 38,1 %, $\text{RR} = 1,94$, $p = 0,001$)** et améliore significativement le handicap MODI ($-13,85$ points, $p < 0,001$) et la qualité de vie SF-12 PCS ($+7,40$, $p < 0,001$), sans aucun événement indésirable grave.

[ABSTRACT EN] Objective To compare conventional monopolar and lateral-deployment RF cannulas for lumbar medial branch radiofrequency ablation (RFA) in chronic facet-mediated low back pain. Design Single-center, randomized, participant-blinded, two-arm superiority trial. Ninety participants were randomized 1:1; 84 with complete 6-month data were analyzed. The primary outcome was change in Numeric Rating Scale (NRS) pain intensity from baseline to 6 months. Secondary outcomes were changes in the Modified Oswestry Disability Index (MODI) and SF-12 Physical (PCS) and Mental (MCS) Component Scores. Results Mean NRS change was -2.81 points with the conventional cannula and -5.52 points with the lateral-deployment cannula. The age-adjusted between-group difference was -2.795 points (95% CI, -3.967 to -1.624; P Conclusion The lateral-deployment cannula was associated with greater 6-month improvements in pain, disability, and physical health and with more participants achieving substantial pain relief. Larger trials with intention-to-treat analyses are needed.

title: Ultrasound-Guided High-Voltage Long-Duration Pulsed Radiofrequency of the Suprascapular Nerve for Persistent Hemiplegic Shoulder Pain
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Protocole technique standardisé pas-à-pas avec démonstration clinique (*Journal of Visualized Experiments — JoVE*, oct. 2026, IF 1,2) décrivant la **radiofréquence pulsée haute tension et longue durée (HL-PRF)** du **nerf supra-scapulaire sous guidage échographique temps réel** pour les douleurs chroniques d'épaule réfractaires aux blocs nerveux classiques : après repérage échographique de l'**incisure scapulaire (suprascapular notch)** et de l'artère supra-scapulaire et confirmation par stimulation sensitive et motrice, la **HL-PRF est délivrée à 99 V pendant 6 minutes avec maintien thermique strict $\le 42\ ^\circ\text{C}$**, entraînant une réduction durable des douleurs au repos et à la mobilisation ainsi qu'un gain d'amplitude passive à **1 mois et 3 mois**, sans **aucun déficit moteur ni complication (0 %)**.

[ABSTRACT EN] Hemiplegic shoulder pain (HSP) is a common complication after stroke that can interfere with upper-limb rehabilitation. Persistent cases may respond inadequately to conventional conservative treatments or suprascapular nerve blocks. This article describes a standardized ultrasound-guided high-voltage long-duration pulsed radiofrequency (HL-PRF) protocol targeting the suprascapular nerve. Ultrasound is used to identify the suprascapular notch, surrounding anatomical structures, and adjacent vessels. A radiofrequency cannula is advanced to the target under real-time guidance, and its position is confirmed by sensory and motor stimulation. HL-PRF is then delivered at 99 V for 6 min while the temperature is maintained at or below 42 °C. The clinical outcomes presented here are illustrative observations from two patients with persistent HSP and do not represent findings from a controlled clinical study. In both cases, lower resting and movement-evoked pain scores and increased shoulder passive range of motion were observed at the 1-month follow-up. Pain scores at the 3-month telephone follow-up remained below baseline values. No procedure-related adverse events were observed or documented in either case during the available follow-up period. These cases are included to illustrate the clinical application and potential outcomes of the protocol rather than to establish efficacy. This protocol provides a detailed procedural framework for ultrasound-guided HL-PRF of the suprascapular nerve in patients with persistent HSP.

title: Ultrasonography-Guided CO2 Cryoablation for Morton Neuroma: Clinical Outcomes of 25 Consecutive Lesions in a Single-Center Observational Case Series With 24- and 52-Week Follow-up
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Étude rétrospective monocentrique portant sur **25 névromes de Morton consécutifs** réfractaires au traitement conservateur traités en ambulatoire sous anesthésie locale par **cryoablation échoguidée au $\text{CO}_2$** (cryosonde de $2,3\text{ mm}$ positionnée au contact du complexe névrome-bourse inter-métatarsienne) avec suivi complet à **24 semaines (6 mois) et 52 semaines (1 an)** (*Foot & Ankle Orthopaedics*, oct. 2026, IF 1,7, Open-Access PMC13775260) : le **succès technique est de 100 % (25/25)**, le score douloureux **EVA moyen chute de $5,82 \pm 1,92$ à $0,92 \pm 1,59$ à 24 semaines (réduction de 84 %, $p < 0,001$)** avec **85,7 % de guérison complète (12/14)** chez les patients porteurs d'un névrome unique, un **maintien intégral du bénéfice à 52 semaines chez 100 % des patients (19/19)**, un **taux de satisfaction de 84,2 % (16/19, 0 % d'insatisfaits)** et **0 % de complication ou de déficit sensitif permanent**.

[ABSTRACT EN] Background When conservative management of Morton neuroma fails, surgical excision is the conventional next step. Neurectomy carries recognized morbidity, including permanent sensory deficit and painful stump-neuroma formation, leaving a gap for a minimally invasive, nerve-sparing alternative. Ultrasonography-guided cryoablation is one such option, but mid-term outcome data, particularly for CO 2 -based systems, are limited. We evaluated its technical success, safety, and clinical effectiveness at 24 and 52 weeks. Methods In this retrospective, single-center study, 26 consecutively treated patients with neuromas refractory to conservative treatment underwent outpatient ultrasonography-guided cryoablation under local anesthesia; 19 (16 women, 3 men; aged 37-75 years, 25 neuromas) completed follow-up and were analyzed. A 2.3 mm CO 2 cryoprobe was positioned adjacent to the neuroma-bursal complex, with freeze-thaw cycles tailored to lesion length. Pain (0-10 visual analog scale [VAS]) and satisfaction were recorded at 24 weeks; at 52 weeks, patients were re-contacted to confirm whether symptoms had changed. Results Technical success was 25 of 25 (100%; 95% CI 86.7-100). Mean VAS decreased from 5.82 ± 1.92 to 0.92 ± 1.59, an 84% reduction ( P Conclusion Ultrasonography-guided CO 2 cryoablation achieved high technical success, marked pain reduction with patient-reported maintenance of benefit at 52 weeks, and high satisfaction, with no patient-reported complications or sensory deficit. It represents a promising nerve-sparing option for refractory Morton neuroma; prospective, comparative studies with longer follow-up are needed to confirm durability. Level of evidence Level IV, case series.

title: Percutaneous cryoablation of musculoskeletal tumours: the largest reported single-centre case series - outcomes, complications and subgroup analysis
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Série monocentrique de référence (*Skeletal Radiology*, oct. 2026, équipe de R. Botchu, 48 patients) évaluant la cryoablation percutanée des tumeurs musculo-squelettiques (métastases, tumeurs cartilagineuses et tumeurs osseuses primitives/bénignes), avec 73 % de réponse clinique (58 % complète/bonne, 15 % partielle), une baisse de densité TDM (UH) dans 94 % des cas et aucune complication majeure CIRSE.

[ABSTRACT EN] Objectives Cryoablation is an image-guided, minimally invasive treatment technique that uses extreme cold to induce tumour destruction. Its role in musculoskeletal oncology has expanded in recent years, although large clinical series remain limited. This study reports a large single-centre experience of percutaneous cryoablation for musculoskeletal tumours, including metastatic lesions, benign and cartilaginous tumours, and primary bone tumours. Materials and methods This was a single-centre retrospective cohort study conducted at a tertiary musculoskeletal oncology centre. All procedures were performed by a single specialist musculoskeletal interventional radiologist with over 20 years of experience. The study included patients who underwent percutaneous cryoablation for musculoskeletal tumours between June 2021 and December 2025. Clinical response, radiological response, recurrence, and complications were assessed over a median follow-up of 3 months (mean 8.7 months; range 0-48 months). Radiological response was assessed using pre-treatment and post-treatment Hounsfield Unit (HU) measurements on CT; this is not a validated radiological scoring system and is reported as a complementary, exploratory marker alongside standard clinical response assessment. Complications were graded using the CIRSE classification system. Results A total of 48 patients underwent percutaneous cryoablation during the study period. The cohort included 26 males and 22 females, with a median age of 40 years. A good or complete response was achieved in 28 patients, representing 58% of the total cohort. A partial response was achieved in seven patients, representing 15% of the total cohort. HU reduction was observed in 45 of 48 patients, representing 94% of the cohort. The overall complication rate was 6.3%, with three complications recorded among 48 procedures. No major complications or procedure-related deaths were observed. Conclusions Cryoablation appears to be a safe and effective minimally invasive treatment for selected musculoskeletal tumours. Most patients achieved a good, complete, or partial response, with a low complication rate. Hounsfield Unit reduction after treatment may provide a useful, though as yet non-validated, marker of radiological response. Further prospective studies with longer follow-up, standardised response criteria and validated complication grading are needed to confirm these findings.

title: Bisphosphonates in osteoid osteoma with difficult location in children
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Étude rétrospective multicentrique française (*Orthopaedics & Traumatology: Surgery & Research - OTSR*, sept. 2026, IF 2,3) incluant 11 enfants/adolescents (âge moyen 13,5 ans) présentant un ostéome ostéoïde situé au contact immédiat de structures nerveuses, médullaires ou cartilagineuses contre-indiquant la thermoablation percutanée et la chirurgie, traités par 3 à 6 perfusions mensuelles d'acide zolédronique : chute de l'EVA moyenne de **70,6/100 à 30,4/100**, baisse de la prise d'AINS de **91 % à 36 %**, et **disparition complète du nidus et de l'œdème médullaire en imagerie chez 73 % des patients**.

[ABSTRACT EN] Introduction Osteoid osteoma is a benign bone tumor that may cause severe pain. Although percutaneous thermoablation is commonly performed and effective in approximately 90% of cases by rapidly relieving symptoms and avoiding surgery, this procedure may carry significant risks when lesions are located near sensitive anatomical structures such as neural, medullary, or cartilaginous tissues. In these situations, bisphosphonates (BP) may represent a less invasive therapeutic alternative by biologically reducing abnormal bone activity and inflammatory pain. Previous studies have demonstrated the efficacy of zoledronic acid in osteoid osteoma, but pediatric data remain scarce. Hypothesis Bisphosphonates may represent an alternative therapeutic option for osteoid osteomas located in anatomically challenging areas unsuitable for conventional treatments. Material and methods This multicenter retrospective study included 11 pediatric patients with osteoid osteoma located close to neural or cartilaginous structures contraindicating surgical treatment or thermoablation and treated with bisphosphonates. Patients received 3-6 monthly infusions of zoledronic acid. Clinical pain assessment, NSAID and analgesic consumption, imaging outcomes, and treatment-related adverse events were collected before and after treatment. Results Eleven patients (3 girls and 8 boys) were included between 2012 and 2024. Mean age was 13.5 years (range, 8-17 years). Mean baseline Visual Analog Scale (VAS) score was 70.6/100 (30-90). NSAID and analgesic consumption was reported in 91% of patients, while all patients presented with a visible nidus and reactive bone marrow edema on imaging. Mean duration of symptoms before BP treatment was 12.7 months (2-26). The mean number of infusions was 3.8 (3-6). Only one patient developed anterior uveitis, which did not require treatment discontinuation. At final follow-up, mean VAS score decreased to 30.4/100 (0-80), while NSAID and analgesic consumption decreased to 36%. Complete disappearance of both nidus and bone marrow edema was observed in 73% of patients. Mean follow-up duration was 7.2 months. Conclusion Zoledronic acid appears to be a promising therapeutic alternative for osteoid osteomas located in anatomically challenging areas in children. Its efficacy is reflected by nidus disappearance, pain reduction, and decreased NSAID consumption. Further studies with larger cohorts and longer follow-up are required to strengthen the level of evidence. Level of evidence IV; retrospective study.

title: Osteoid osteoma of the talus adjacent to the subtalar joint: a rare location and diagnostic challenge
container-title: International journal of surgery case reports
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Étude clinique et mise au point diagnostique sur l'**ostéome ostéoïde du talus adjacent à l'articulation sous-talienne** chez un adulte jeune de 20 ans présentant des douleurs nocturnes chroniques de cheville (*International Journal of Surgery Case Reports*, sept. 2026, IF 0,7, Open-Access PMC13652452) : souligne le **piège classique de l'IRM initiale** — qui montre un œdème médullaire osseux diffus et une réaction synoviale mimant une entorse ou une synovite chronique — alors que le **scanner en coupes fines identifie formellement le nidus de 5 mm** du bord inféro-médial du talus, et détaille l'intérêt du **repérage percutané par broche de Kirschner sous guidage TDM** pour permettre l'éradication ciblée sans lésion cartilagineuse sous-talienne (**guérison complète sans récidive à 1 an**).

[ABSTRACT EN] Introduction and importance Osteoid osteoma is a common benign bone tumor, but lesions located in the talus, especially those adjacent to the subtalar joint, are relatively rare and prone to misdiagnosis. Its clinical and imaging manifestations are often atypical, which can lead to delayed diagnosis and inappropriate conservative treatment. Accurate imaging evaluation and appropriate surgical management are critical for symptom relief and functional recovery. Case presentation We present a 20-year-old male with chronic left ankle pain that worsened at night and with weight-bearing. Initial MRI suggested bone marrow edema and ligament injury, leading to a misdiagnosis of ankle synovitis and sprain. Subsequent CT clearly identified a 5-mm nidus at the medial inferior margin of the left talus. The patient underwent open resection with intraoperative CT-guided K-wire localization. Postoperative histopathological examination confirmed osteoid osteoma. At the 1-year follow-up, the patient was pain-free and had fully resumed daily activities. Clinical discussion Talar osteoid osteoma is prone to misdiagnosis because its symptoms resemble those of ankle sprain, synovitis, or impingement. CT is the gold standard for detecting the nidus, while MRI frequently shows nonspecific bone marrow edema. Surgical excision remains a reliable treatment method. CT-guided K-wire localization improves accuracy, minimizes bone damage, and ensures complete resection, avoiding incomplete ablation and the recurrence risk associated with percutaneous radiofrequency ablation. Conclusion Osteoid osteoma of the talus is a rare but significant cause of chronic ankle pain and is easily misdiagnosed. CT is essential for early and accurate diagnosis. For juxta-articular lesions, CT-guided K-wire localization followed by open resection is safe and effective, completely relieving symptoms and achieving good long-term outcomes.

title: Complications of vertebral augmentation in metastatic spinal fractures: a systematic review of multiple study designs
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Revue systématique d'envergure (*Journal of Bone Oncology*, sept. 2026, 76 études, 3 234 patients, ≥ 5 737 vertèbres traitées) quantifiant précisément le taux de complications symptomatiques (3,41 %) et de fuites de ciment (20,7 %, majoritairement asymptomatiques) lors de la cimentoplastie des métastases rachidiennes.

[ABSTRACT EN] Background Vertebral augmentation techniques, including vertebroplasty and kyphoplasty, are widely used to relieve pain and restore spinal stability in patients with metastatic vertebral lesions. Despite their widespread use, the full spectrum and clinical significance of procedure-related complications remain incompletely characterised. This systematic review aims to summarise and characterise all reported complications associated with vertebral augmentation for metastatic thoracolumbar disease. Methods A comprehensive search of PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science databases was performed. Studies reporting complications associated with vertebral augmentation procedures for metastatic thoracolumbar spinal fractures were included. Randomised controlled trials, observational studies, case series, and case reports were eligible. Due to substantial heterogeneity across studies, a descriptive synthesis was performed. Results A total of 76 studies were included, comprising 3234 patients and at least 5737 vertebral levels treated. The overall weighted complication rate was 25.5%, while the weighted rate of symptomatic complications was 3.41%. Cement leakage was the most frequently reported complication, with a weighted mean incidence of 20.7%, although the majority were asymptomatic. Other complications included postprocedural pain (1.77%), pulmonary cement embolism (1.08%), and adjacent level fractures (0.79%). Studies using CT imaging reported significantly higher cement leakage rates (28.6% vs 11.9%, p = 0.004). Case reports described rare but potentially severe complications, including needle-tract tumour seeding, tumour extrusion, and cement migration to cardiac structures. Conclusions This review presents a comprehensive and detailed description of all complications of vertebral augmentation for treatment of metastatic spine disease and reinforce its safety. Differences in imaging protocols and reporting standards contribute to variability in reported complication rates. Further prospective studies with standardised complication reporting are needed.

title: Iliosacral Screw Fixation for Treating Sacral Fractures: A Modified Pedicle-Guided Fixation Technique in Prone Position
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Série clinique (*Orthopaedic Surgery*, sept./nov. 2026, PMC Open-Access, 22 patients) décrivant une technique modifiée de vissage ilio-sacré percutané en procubitus guidée par les repères du pédicule de S1 : taux d'excellence de positionnement intra-osseux au scanner de 97 %, absence totale de complication radiculaire et amélioration significative de l'EVA douleur et du score fonctionnel de Majeed.

[ABSTRACT EN] Background Sacral fractures are posterior pelvic ring injuries which mechanisms range from high-energy trauma to low-energy falls in osteoporotic patients. In surgical treatment, percutaneous approaches have demonstrated significant shorter operation time and less soft tissue damage. In this study, we present a method of iliosacral (SI) screw insertion in prone position, with modified pedicle-guided technique. Methods The present study is a retrospective case series of 22 patients for SI screw fixation from February 2019 to September 2023 under our method. Surgical technique was described in detail with images. Perioperative clinical parameters were analyzed. Activity status, complications, data of 10-point visual analogue scale (VAS) for pain and further functional outcomes using the Majeed Pelvic Score (MPS) were recorded. In addition, computed tomography (CT) was routinely performed at 6 months postsurgery to inspect the quality of screws position. Results Excellence rate of screw position was 97% upon CT. Two patients had screws partially contacting the cortical bone but not violating sacral foramen, and no neurological symptoms were noted. All screws were secure from possible iatrogenic nerve injuries. VAS scores improved significantly over time and most patients recorded excellent functional recovery. One untoward complication occurred involving unexpected cement extravasation after sacroplasty. No associated neurologic compromise, or clinical evidence of venous emboli thrombosis was reported. Conclusion Our method aims at reducing operation time and radiation exposure to surgeons as conventional two-dimensional fluoroscopy was enough to identify safe insertion corridors in SI screw placement. Performing SI fixation in prone position is also advantageous when dealing with obese patients and concomitant spinal injuries.

title: Fluoroscopy-assisted percutaneous management of posterior pelvic ring injuries via multiple transsacral and iliosacral screws in the supine position
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Étude de cohorte sur 69 patients consécutifs (149 vis canulées de gros diamètre ≥ 7 mm : 123 vis trans-sacrées [TSS] et 26 vis ilio-sacrées [ISS]) traités en décubitus dorsal avec suivi moyen de 19,5 mois (*Injury*, sept. 2026, IF 2,2) : 100 % de trajet strictement intra-osseux au scanner post-opératoire, 0 % de complication neurovasculaire ou infectieuse, 0 % de descellement et 0 % de pseudarthrose (1 seul bris de vis S2 asymptomatique, soit 0,67 %).

[ABSTRACT EN] Introduction When patients are positioned supine for percutaneous screw insertion to achieve posterior pelvic ring fixation, the edge of the operating table can impede screw insertion trajectories, thereby increasing the risk of cortical perforation, especially during iliosacral screw (ISS) placement. Multiple screw insertion might also potentially increase the risk of cortical perforation. The aim of this study was to evaluate the feasibility, safety, and efficacy of inserting multiple (≥2) transsacral screw (TSS) and ISS in the supine position via the application of specific surgical strategies and techniques developed in our institution. Patients and methods Patients who underwent stabilization of posterior pelvic ring injuries via percutaneous insertion of multiple TSS and/or ISS in the supine position between May 2018 and December 2025 were included in this study. Distinct screw insertion combination patterns at different vertebral levels, which were primarily determined by the variable anterior-posterior width of the transverse osseous pathway at the first sacrum, were employed for posterior pelvic ring fixation. Wound infection and neurovascular complications associated with screws insertion procedure were recorded. Postoperative CT scans were performed to assess the position of the screws. At follow-up, radiographic evaluations were performed to evaluate the complications including screw loosening, screw breakage, and non-union. Results A total of 149 large-diameter (≥7 mm) screws, including 123 TSSs and 26 ISSs, were inserted in a total of 69 consecutive patients. No wound infection and neurovascular complication associated with the screw insertion procedure were found postoperatively. Postoperative CT imaging demonstrated that all inserted screws were intraosseous. All patients were followed for an average of 19.5 months (range, 6.6-38 months). Only one screw (S2 TSS) breakage was noted, and no screw loosening and no bone nonunion occurred. Conclusions Fluoroscopy-assisted percutaneous multiple large-diameter screws (TSS and ISS) insertion for posterior pelvic ring injuries with the patient positioned supine has been confirmed to be a feasible, safe, and effective surgical procedure.

title: Robot-assisted fracture reduction and treatment outcomes in type III and IV fragility fractures of the pelvis: A retrospective cohort study
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Étude de cohorte rétrospective sur **115 patients âgés de $\ge 60\text{ ans}$** présentant une fracture de fragilité du bassin instable et déplacée de **type FFP III ou IV** (*Injury*, sept./nov. 2026, IF 2,2) comparant 3 stratégies : réduction fermée assistée par robot + vissage percutané ($n = 39$), réduction fermée manuelle + vissage percutané navigué ($n = 34$) et traitement conservateur non opératoire ($n = 42$) : la fixation percutanée surpasse significativement le traitement non opératoire à 1 an sur la douleur ($p < 0,05$), le score fonctionnel de Majeed ($p < 0,05$) et le score de mobilité de Parker ($p < 0,05$), avec une tendance à une **mortalité à 1 an réduite de moitié (8,6 % vs 21,1 %)**, tandis que l'assistance robotique améliore significativement la qualité anatomique de réduction selon Matta ($\text{OR} = 0,139$, $p = 0,001$) et la mobilité à 1 an ($\beta = 2,030$, $p < 0,001$).

[ABSTRACT EN] Introduction This study compared robot-assisted fracture reduction (RAFR) with manual closed reduction followed by navigation-assisted fixation in surgically treated patients with fragility fractures of the pelvis (FFP) type III or IV. Outcomes after operative versus initial non-operative management were also examined. Patients and methods This retrospective cohort study included 115 patients aged ≥ 60 years treated between March 2021 and June 2025: 39 underwent RAFR, 34 manual closed reduction with navigation-assisted fixation, and 42 initial non-operative treatment. The primary outcome was postoperative reduction quality according to the Matta criteria. Secondary outcomes included 1-year functional scores, mortality, and surgery-related complications. Results RAFR was associated with lower odds of a worse postoperative Matta grade than manual closed reduction with navigation-assisted fixation (adjusted common OR=0.139, 95% CI 0.039-0.440; P = 0.001). Among 58 operated survivors with complete 1-year assessments, RAFR was associated with a higher Parker Mobility Score (β=2.030, 95% CI 1.093-2.966; P Conclusion RAFR was associated with better postoperative reduction quality and a higher 1-year Parker Mobility Score than manual reduction/navigation, whereas adjusted differences in Barthel Index, EQ-5D-5L, and NRS were not statistically significant. Operative treatment was associated with better 1-year functional and pain outcomes in exploratory analyses, but a survival advantage was not demonstrated.

title: Minimally invasive internal fixation versus symphyseal screws for unstable pelvic ring fractures
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Étude comparative rétrospective sur **50 patients** présentant une fracture instable de l'anneau pelvien (types Young-Burgess APC II–III et LC II–III, *International Orthopaedics*, sept. 2026, IF 2,0) comparant le **vissage percutané symphysaire ($n = 25$)** au fixateur interne sous-cutané antérieur INFIX ($n = 25$) avec 12 mois de suivi : le vissage percutané obtient une **consolidation osseuse plus rapide ($43,7 \pm 1,2\text{ jours}$ vs $44,9 \pm 1,8\text{ jours}$, $p = 0,008$)**, des **pertes sanguines et une longueur d'incision significativement inférieures ($p < 0,001$)** et **11 fois moins de complications post-opératoires (4 % vs 44 %, $p = 0,001$)**, tout en offrant un résultat fonctionnel de Majeed et une réduction de l'EVA ($p < 0,001$) équivalents.

[ABSTRACT EN] Introduction Stabilization of the anterior pelvic ring is crucial in the management of unstable pelvic ring fractures. Minimally invasive internal fixation (INFIX) has been proposed as an alternative to conventional symphyseal plate fixation; however, comparative clinical evidence remains limited. Objective To compare INFIX and percutaneous symphyseal screws fixation for unstable pelvic ring fractures in terms of perioperative parameters, complications, radiological outcomes, and functional results. Methods This retrospective comparative study included 50 patients with unstable pelvic ring fractures (APC II-III and LC II-III). Patients were allocated into two groups: INFIX fixation (n = 25) and symphyseal screw fixation (n = 25). Outcomes assessed included union time, operative details, blood loss, fluoroscopic exposure, postoperative complications, pain (Visual Analogue Scale), and functional outcome (Majeed score). Patients were followed for up to 12 months. Results Union time was slightly shorter in the screws group (43.7 ± 1.2 vs. 44.9 ± 1.8 days; p = 0.008). Intra-operative blood loss and incision length were significantly higher in the INFIX group (p Conclusion Both fixation techniques effectively achieved fracture union and pain relief. percutaneous symphyseal screws fixation was associated with lower perioperative morbidity and fewer complications, while INFIX required less fluoroscopic guidance. Fixation choice should be individualized based on patient and fracture characteristics.

title: Cryoablation for Extra-Abdominal Desmoid Tumors: a Retrospective Study of Clinical and Radiological Outcomes
container-title: Journal of vascular and interventional radiology : JVIR
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Étude de cohorte sur 92 séances de cryoablation chez 44 patients (*JVIR*, sept. 2026, taille médiane 6,9 cm, suivi médian 28,9 mois) rapportant 81,1 % de succès clinique, 78,4 % de réponse objective (24,3 % RC, 54,1 % RP), une concordance quasi parfaite entre volumétrie 3D et mRECIST (κ = 0,895), et seulement 5,3 % de complications majeures.

[ABSTRACT EN] Purpose To determine whether image-guided cryoablation achieves durable clinical and radiologic response with an acceptable safety profile in patients with extra-abdominal desmoid tumors and whether volumetric response assessment concords with modified Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors-based classification MATERIALS AND METHODS: Patients treated between 2020 and 2024 were identified through electronic record. Those who underwent cryoablation were included for analysis. The primary outcome was clinical success, defined as a composite of no disease progression at last follow-up, no additional treatment, and symptom improvement. The secondary outcomes included radiologic response, symptom improvement, progression-free survival, and safety. Among 208 patients diagnosed with desmoid tumors, 44 (20.7%) underwent cryoablation, of whom 38 had follow-up data available; 92 cryoablation sessions were performed. Median tumor size was 6.9 cm (interquartile range, 5.5-9.2 cm), and median follow-up duration was 28.9 months (interquartile range, 14.3-37.3 months). Results The clinical success rate was 81.1%. Radiologic response at last follow-up was complete in 24.3%, partial in 54.1%, stable in 16.2%, and progressive in 5.4% of patients. Volumetric and modified Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors-based response classification showed almost-perfect agreement (κ = 0.895). Repeat cryoablation was performed in 26.3% of patients due to radiologic progression. Additional treatment modalities were required in 13.2% of cases. The 1- and 2-year progression-free survival rates were 76.5% (95% confidence interval, 58.2%-87.6%) and 67.4% (95% confidence interval, 46.5%-81.7%), respectively. Major adverse events (Society of Interventional Radiology grade, ≥Grade 3) occurred in 5.3% of patients. Conclusions Cryoablation is a safe and effective treatment option for selected patients with extra-abdominal desmoid tumors, achieving clinical success in the majority of patients. These findings support its role in the multidisciplinary management of desmoid tumors.

title: MRI-guided cryoablation for recurrent pediatric hand desmoid tumor: A longitudinal case report
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Étude longitudinale sur 5 ans (*Radiology Case Reports*, sept. 2026, IF 1,0, Open-Access) d'une tumeur desmoïde dorsale de la main multi-récidivante après 5 exérèses chirurgicales chez une adolescente de 14 ans, engainant l'appareil extenseur des 2e et 3e rayons : la réalisation de 4 séances ciblées de cryoablation percutanée guidée par IRM sur 5 ans (ciblant sélectivement les foyers d'hypersignal T2 évolutifs et douloureux pendant le pic de croissance pubertaire) a permis un contrôle local durable, une disparition des douleurs et une préservation fonctionnelle complète des tendons extenseurs de la main sans recours à la radiothérapie ni à l'amputation.

[ABSTRACT EN] Desmoid fibromatosis of the hand is rare, with fewer than 20 cases reported in the literature. We present a 14-year-old girl with a right-hand desmoid tumor who sought non-radiation focal treatment after five prior surgical resections. The tumor overlaid the extensor compartment of her dorsal hand and caused pain and progressive hyperextension of the second and third fingers. She was initially evaluated for CT-guided cryoablation but was not a candidate due to limited visibility, and was therefore selected for MRI-guided cryoablation given its superior visualization of the iceball. She was safely treated four times over a five-year span, targeting areas of active pain and tumor growth during a period that included a concomitant pubertal growth spurt. MRI-guided cryoablation provided safe, effective, and durable local control for a recurrent pediatric hand desmoid tumor when further surgery and radiation were not desired, and it may offer a viable non-radiation alternative for select patients with extra-abdominal desmoid disease.

title: Bipolar needle electrodes for electroporation-based treatments in soft and bone tissues: technical design and implementation
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Note technique multicentrique (*La Radiologia Medica*, sept. 2026, IF 8,9) détaillant l'architecture du champ électrique et l'implantation guidée par l'image d'électrodes aiguilles bipolaires mono-aiguille pour l'électrochimiothérapie (ECT) des tumeurs osseuses et des tissus mous, permettant de réduire le nombre d'insertions tout en confinant le champ électrique à distance des structures nerveuses.

[ABSTRACT EN] Electroporation (EP) transiently increases cell membrane permeability through the application of controlled electric pulses. Bipolar needle electrodes have been developed to simplify EP procedures by reducing the number of electrode insertions while improving control of electric field geometry and spatial confinement. This technical note describes the design principles, electric field behavior, and image-guided implementation of single-needle bipolar electrodes for EP applications in both soft and bone tissues. Electric field simulations and preclinical investigations were performed to assess field distribution, safety, and tissue selectivity. The practical implementation of the bipolar configuration is illustrated through representative image-guided examples from multiple institutions across different anatomical settings. The single-needle design enables minimally invasive procedures with predictable field control and limited extension to surrounding structures, even in anatomically complex or previously treated regions. Overall, bipolar electrodes represent a versatile and reproducible technological solution for electroporation-based treatments, supporting precise and tissue-sparing image-guided interventions.

title: Spine interventional oncology: An illustrated review of minimally invasive techniques
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Mise au point illustrée française (*Neurochirurgie*, sept. 2026, équipes Pitié-Salpêtrière & Rouen) synthétisant l'arsenal d'oncologie interventionnelle rachidienne : biopsie radioguidée, cimentoplastie des étages complexes (rachis cervical), fixation percutanée (odontoïde, sacrum, bassin), embolisation préopératoire, ablation thermique et électrochimiothérapie (ECT) en présence d'une épidurite.

[ABSTRACT EN] Spine oncological interventional radiology has become an integral component of multidisciplinary care for patients with neoplastic spinal disease. Beyond conventional vertebral augmentation, the field now encompasses image-guided biopsy, cementoplasty at complex spinal levels, percutaneous fixation, preoperative embolization of hypervascular tumors, thermal ablation, and electrochemotherapy. These techniques address complementary objectives, including histological diagnosis, rapid pain relief, mechanical stabilization, facilitation of surgery, and local tumor control in selected patients. Advances in imaging guidance, procedural planning, and device technology have enabled increasingly precise and tailored interventions in anatomically constrained regions. However, the spine remains a high-risk anatomical territory because of the proximity of the spinal cord, nerve roots, radiculomedullary arteries, and major vascular structures. Procedural safety therefore depends on careful patient selection, detailed knowledge of spinal anatomy, rigorous planning, and multidisciplinary coordination. Particularly challenging scenarios include cervical cementoplasty, percutaneous fixation of odontoid, pelvic, or sacral lesions, and tumor treatment in the presence of epidural extension. This illustrated review summarizes the main minimally invasive techniques currently used in spine interventional oncology, with emphasis on their indications, technical principles, safety strategies, limitations, and integration into contemporary oncologic care pathways.

title: Quality of life and pain-response after stereotactic ablative radiotherapy of oligometastatic bone metastases in the phase 2 BONY-M trial
container-title: Radiotherapy and oncology : journal of the European Society for Therapeutic Radiology and Oncology
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Analyse prospective longitudinale des critères secondaires de qualité de vie (EQ-5D-5L) et de douleur (NPRS) à 12, 24, 36 et 52 semaines dans l'**essai multicentrique de phase 2 BONY-M (NCT05101824)** portant sur **67 patients oligométastatiques** traités par **radiothérapie stéréotaxique ablative (SABR : 30 ou 37,5 Gy en 3 fractions)** pour $\ge 1$ métastase osseuse (prostate 33 %, sein 28 %, rein 15 %, poumon 10 %) (*Radiotherapy and Oncology — Green Journal*, sept. 2026, IF 4,9) : chez les patients initialement symptomatiques ($n = 22$, $\text{NPRS} \ge 2$), le **taux de réponse antalgique globale est de 59 % (13/22) à 24 semaines** (baisse moyenne du NPRS de **$-2,4\text{ points}$**, IC 95 % 1,6–3,3) et de **41 % (9/22) à 52 semaines**, avec un **flare douloureux précoce à S2 chez 11 % des patients (7/66)** et une stabilité de l'indice EQ-5D-5L sur 1 an.

[ABSTRACT EN] Purpose The Bony-M phase 2 multicentre trial included patients with oligometastatic disease (OMD) for stereotactic ablative radiotherapy (SABR) of bone metastases (clinicaltrials.gov ID-no.NCT05101824). We report the secondary endpoint analyses of longitudinal health-related quality of life (HRQoL) outcomes and pain response. Methods Patients with ≥ 1 bone metastasis were eligible for inclusion. Prescription doses were 37.5 or 30 Gy in three fractions. EuroQol EQ-5D-5L and numeric pain rating scale (NPRS) responses were collected at baseline and weeks 12, 24, 36, and 52 (pain also at week 2). For this analysis, patients were grouped by baseline NPRS as being either asymptomatic (NPRS 0-1) or symptomatic (NPRS ≥ 2). Results Sixty-seven patients were analysed, including one patient without baseline NPRS. Most had prostate (33 %), breast (28 %), kidney (15 %), or lung cancer (10 %). Mean EQ-5D-5L index and visual analogue scale scores remained stable through 52 weeks of follow-up. Symptomatic patients (n = 22) reported more pain/discomfort and had a lower EQ-5D-5L index value at baseline and follow-up than asymptomatic patients (n = 44). Among symptomatic patients, overall pain response was 59 % (13/22) at 24 weeks and 41 % (9/22) at 52 weeks. Mean pain score decreased by 2.4 points (95 % CI: 1.6-3.3) at 24 weeks. Pain flare at week 2 occurred in 11 % (7/66) of patients. Conclusions Mean HRQoL remained stable throughout one year of follow-up, and expected pain relief was achieved for symptomatic metastases. Our findings suggest that SABR for local disease control in carefully selected patients with asymptomatic and symptomatic OMD can be used without compromising HRQoL.

title: Examining the current image-guided biopsy and empiric antibiotic paradigm for suspected spondylodiscitis
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Étude rétrospective (*Diagnostic and Interventional Radiology*, sept. 2026, IF 1,9) sur 81 biopsies disco-vertébrales guidées par l'image (62 sous TDM, 19 sous scopie) : rendement microbiologique global de 37,0 % non significativement diminué par une antibiothérapie préalable (36,4 % sous antibiotiques vs 37,8 % sans antibiotiques, p = 0,890), soulignant qu'il ne faut pas retarder l'antibiothérapie probabiliste chez un patient septique et que la biologie moléculaire (ARN 16S / NGS) est indispensable pour compléter la culture.

[ABSTRACT EN] Purpose This study aims to identify factors associated with successful pathogen isolation via percutaneous image-guided biopsy (IGB) in suspected spondylodiscitis, compare diagnostic value between fluoroscopy and computed tomography (CT) guided IGB, evaluate the influence of empiric antibiotics prior to biopsy, and assess the impact of IGB results on clinical management and patient outcomes. Methods This retrospective study examined 81 IGBs (62 CT-guided, 19 fluoroscopy-guided) performed for suspected spondylodiscitis between March 2014 and February 2025. Retrospective diagnosis was determined using a composite of biopsy microbiology, clinical criteria, and radiologic findings. Primary analyses included IGB culture yield (procedural diagnostic return), as well as sensitivity, specificity, and diagnostic accuracy. Subgroup analyses included biopsy modality and prior antibiotic administration. Results The overall culture yield was 37.0%, with a sensitivity of 44.4% and a specificity of 88.9%. Culture yield did not differ significantly among patients who received antibiotics prior to biopsy (36.4%) and those who did not (37.8%; P = 0.890). Similarly, no significant difference in yield was observed between CT-guided (38.7%) and fluoroscopic IGB (31.6%; P = 0.586). No significant difference was observed between the coaxial devices used for either transpedicular bone biopsy ( P = 0.604) or disc biopsy/aspiration ( P = 1.000). Excluding tuberculosis (TB) case, 97% of cultured organisms were susceptible to the institution's standard empiric antibiotic regimen of vancomycin and ceftriaxone. Conclusion In cases of suspected spondylodiscitis, IGB demonstrated low sensitivity and rarely altered clinical management during the study. Culture yield was not significantly diminished by prior antibiotic therapy, and 97% of cultured organisms (excluding TB) were susceptible to this institution's standard empiric antibiotics. Furthermore, the relative infrequency of positive cultures suggests that empiric antibiotic initiation should not be delayed solely for the purpose of biopsy in clinically stable patients with characteristic magnetic resonance imaging findings and elevated inflammatory markers. Although the findings in this single-center retrospective study support consideration of a more selective use of IGB, further multicenter studies and meta-analyses are warranted. Clinical significance If additional larger studies corroborate these findings, this could result in a paradigm shift for the clinical management of suspected spondylodiscitis.

title: A Simple Needle Disc Puncture in the Cervical Spine is a Safe and Efficient Alternative to Disc/Vertebral Biopsy: Ten Years' Experience in a Reference Centre
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Retour d'expérience sur 10 ans d'un centre de référence (*World Neurosurgery*, sept./nov. 2026, IF 2,0) évaluant la ponction-aspiration discale cervicale simple à l'aiguille fine sous guidage TDM et anesthésie locale (CTFNP, avant toute antibiothérapie probabiliste) chez les patients présentant une spondylodiscite cervicale à hémocultures négatives : positivité microbiologique dans **90 % des cas (9/10)** (avec prédominance du groupe *Streptococcus anginosus* chez les patients aux antécédents ORL/radiothérapie cervicale), durée moyenne de procédure de 20 minutes, délai médian de réalisation de 1,5 jour et **0 % de complication majeure**.

[ABSTRACT EN] Background Disc/vertebral infection (DVI) often requires invasive sampling for microbiological diagnosis when blood cultures are negative. CT-guided disc/vertebral biopsy is the standard diagnostic procedure but is technically challenging and associated with neurological risks in the cervical region. The technique requires sedation or general anaesthesia. These factors may cause organizational complexity, longer processing times and further delay treatment. This study assesses the diagnostic value of simple CT-guided fine-needle disc puncture (CTFNP) under local anaesthesia as an alternative in suspected cervical DVI. Methods This retrospective study included patients managed for DVI between 2015 and 2025 at a single referral centre. All patients underwent CTFNP under local anaesthesia for suspected cervical DVI after a recent MRI and without prior empiric antibiotic therapy. Culture positivity was assessed for each case. Data were collected and correlated with microbiological findings. Results Ten patients were included. Microbiological cultures were positive in 9 of 10 cases. Five patients had a history of head and neck cancer or neck irradiation. In this subgroup, the bacteria predominantly originated from the otolaryngological (ENT) region and mainly belonged to the Streptococcus anginosus group (n = 5). Intradiscal fluid on MRI was reported in only 3 cases. Sample volumes were small. The mean procedure time was 20 minutes and the median interval between the referring physician's request and CTFNP was 1.5 days. No major complications were reported. Conclusions Fine-needle disc puncture may be an effective, rapid and low risk alternative to the standard technique in patients with disc vertebral infection in the cervical spine.

title: Perivascular epithelioid cell (PEComa) tumors of the musculoskeletal system: a case series with MR imaging and histopathologic review
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Série rétrospective monocentrique d'un centre tertiaire de référence des sarcomes portant sur **12 patients consécutifs** (7 hommes, âge moyen **64,3 ans**, extrêmes 16–89 ans) atteints d'un **PECome (tumeur à cellules épithélioïdes périvasculaires) musculo-squelettique des parties molles** prouvé histologiquement avec IRM pré-thérapeutique entre 2000 et 2025 (*Skeletal Radiology*, sept. 2026, IF 1,9) : hormis 1 cas bénin fibrome-like associé à une sclérose tubéreuse de Bourneville (TSC) en hyposignal T1/T2 homogène non rehaussé, les **11 PEComes sporadiques (non-TSC)** se présentent comme de **volumineuses masses profondes sous-fasciales (10/11, 91 %) de diamètre moyen 13,0 cm**, avec **extension trans-compartimentale (6/11, 55 %)**, **nécrose intratumorale macroscopique constante sur toutes les IRM injectées (10/10, 100 %)**, **engainement neurovasculaire dans 36 % (4/11)** et **envahissement osseux dans 18 % (2/11)**, associés à une morphologie histologique maligne (100 % des cas évaluables), un **taux métastatique de 91 %** et une **mortalité spécifique de 64 %** à un suivi médian de 19 mois.

[ABSTRACT EN] To describe the spectrum of MRI features, histopathological findings, and clinical outcomes of musculoskeletal PEComas at a single tertiary sarcoma center. Following institutional ethics approval, orthopedic oncology and pathology databases were searched for histopathologically confirmed musculoskeletal soft tissue PEComas managed between 2000 and 2025. Inclusion required pretreatment MRI. Pulmonary, intra-abdominal/pelvic, and cutaneous lesions were excluded. Demographic and clinical features were reviewed for all cases. MRI examinations were reviewed in consensus by two fellowship-trained musculoskeletal radiologists and archival histopathology by a dedicated musculoskeletal pathologist. Twelve patients met inclusion criteria (7/12 male), mean age 64.3 years (range 16-89 years). One tuberous sclerosis complex (TSC)-associated fibroma-like PEComa appeared as a well-defined periarticular mass with homogeneously low T1 and T2 signal and no significant enhancement. The remaining 11 non-TSC tumors had a mean diameter of 13.0 cm; 10 of 11 were deep to deep fascia, and 6 of 11 showed trans-compartmental extension. Intratumoral nonenhancement consistent with necrosis was present in all 10 contrast-enhanced cases. Neurovascular encasement was identified in 4 of 11 (36%) and osseous invasion in 2 of 11 (18%). All nine histologically evaluable non-TSC cases showed malignant morphology. The overall metastatic rate was 91%, with disease-specific mortality of 64% at a median follow-up of 19 months. Musculoskeletal PEComas demonstrate large size, deep location, macroscopic intratumoral necrosis, as well as frequent trans-compartmental extension on MRI. Clinical outcomes reflect aggressive biologic behavior, with high metastatic rates and disease-specific mortality in non-TSC-related PEComas of the musculoskeletal system.

title: Dynamic contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and intravoxel incoherent motion imaging for characterizing angiogenesis in soft-tissue sarcomas: an exploratory study based on MRI-pathology co-alignment
container-title: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Étude prospective sur 70 sarcomes des tissus mous en IRM 3T (*Quantitative Imaging in Medicine and Surgery*, nov. 2026) avec co-alignement spatial coupe-à-coupe IRM/anatomopathologie, démontrant que les paramètres Ktrans (DCE-MRI) et D* (IVIM) corrèlent fortement avec l'expression de VEGF et la densité microvasculaire (MVD) avec une AUC de 0,86.

[ABSTRACT EN] BACKGROUND: Vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) expression and microvessel density (MVD) are established markers of tumor angiogenesis and key targets for anti-angiogenic therapy in soft-tissue sarcomas (STSs). Dynamic contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (DCE-MRI) and intravoxel incoherent motion (IVIM) imaging are complementary magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) methods commonly used to assess angiogenesis in a variety of tumors. This study aimed to explore whether DCE-MRI and IVIM imaging could be used as non-invasive tools to evaluate tumor angiogenesis in STS based on MRI-pathology co-alignment. METHODS: In total, 70 patients with STS underwent 3.0-T DCE-MRI and IVIM imaging. The volume transfer constant (Ktrans), reflux rate constant (Kep), volume fraction of the extravascular extracellular space (Ve), true diffusion coefficient (D), pseudo-diffusion coefficient (D*), and perfusion fraction (f) were measured. Correlations between MRI parameters and VEGF expression or MVD were examined. Differences in MRI parameters between tumors with low and high VEGF expression were evaluated. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves were generated, and interobserver reproducibility was assessed using the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC). An MRI-pathology control protocol was implemented to verify the spatial correspondence between MRI slices and their corresponding histologic sections. RESULTS: Ktrans, Kep, D*, and f were positively correlated with VEGF expression (r=0.673, 0.573, 0.692, and 0.386, respectively) and MVD (r=0.662, 0.595, 0.619, and 0.344, respectively). Ktrans and D* were identified as independent factors associated with VEGF expression and MVD. No significant correlations were observed between Ve or D and either angiogenesis marker. Tumors with high VEGF expression exhibited higher Ktrans, Kep, D*, and f values than those with low VEGF expression. The areas under the ROC curves for the four parameters in differentiating between tumors with low and high VEGF expression were 0.861, 0.844, 0.860, and 0.720, respectively. CONCLUSIONS: The study demonstrated associations between DCE-MRI- and IVIM-derived perfusion metrics and VEGF expression and MVD in STSs.

title: Validation of ST-RADS calculator: AI web tool for soft tissue-RADS implementation in de novo non-operated tumors and tumor-like lesions
abstract:
[SYNTHÈSE FR] Étude de validation sur 134 tumeurs des parties molles de novo non opérées confirmées par l'histopathologie (*Clinical Imaging*, sept./déc. 2026, IF 1,8) évaluant le système de stratification du risque IRM **ACR Soft Tissue-RADS (ST-RADS)** par 4 radiologues ostéo-articulaires seniors et par un calculateur algorithmique structuré : sensibilité de **85 %** et spécificité de **76,5 %** des radiologues MSK pour discriminer les lésions bénignes (ST-RADS 1 à 3) des tumeurs malignes/sarcomes (ST-RADS 4 et 5), le calculateur basé sur les descripteurs sémiologiques structurés atteignant une performance diagnostique équivalente aux experts (précision dichotomisée de 72 % vs 71 %, p = 0,46).

[ABSTRACT EN] Purpose Soft-tissue RADS (ST-RADS) is an ACR-sponsored MRI-based scoring system for risk-stratification of soft tissue tumors and tumor-like lesions. Despite strong interobserver agreement and diagnostic accuracy, clinical adoption is limited by reader fatigue and workflow burden. We developed and validated an AI-based web tool (ST-RADS calculator) using ST-RADS algorithms and GPT API to facilitate routine implementation. Methods The ST-RADS calculator offers three input modes: image-only, text features-only, and combined. A retrospective study of 134 histopathology-confirmed soft tissue tumors compared ST-RADS scores from four fellowship-trained musculoskeletal (MSK) radiologists against the calculator using all three approaches. Sensitivity and specificity were compared using generalized estimating equations with pairwise contrasts. Results Sensitivity was similar across all methods: 85% for radiologists, 86% for image-only, 81% for text features-only, and 86% for combined (p > 0.90). Specificity differed significantly: 76.5% for radiologists, 69.4% for text features-only, 61.2% for combined, and 25.5% for image-only. Text features-only did not differ significantly from radiologists (p = 0.46). Dichotomized accuracy (benign 1-3 vs. malignant 4-5) was 71% for radiologists, 72% for text features-only, 61% for combined, and 42% for image-only. Full-scale accuracy ranged from 19% (image-only) to 52% (combined). Conclusion The ST-RADS calculator with text-based input achieved accuracy comparable to expert MSK radiologists, while image-only approaches require further refinement. This tool can support routine ST-RADS implementation in clinical practice.

title: Gaussian mixture modelling enables valid intramuscular fat quantification on T2- and intermediate-weighted shoulder MRI relative to two-point Dixon
abstract:
